- A bare "yes" authorizes authoring only — > "If the user picked `C1-author` and you later want to run the suite, ask again."
- Flag long voice responses and raw digits — > "Flag any response over 3 sentences as a potential voice UX issue."
- A grade of C or below triggers the static safety-review handoff — > "If the grade is C or below, recommend `/agentforce-generate` Section 15 (static safety review) for hardening"
- Requirements are pinned to `sf` CLI 2.131.0+ — > "`sf` CLI **2.131.0+** (plugin-agent 1.32.16+)"
WORKFLOW: Mode A — plan test cases (5 classes) → present for review → start/send/end preview with `--authoring-bundle` → read traces by jq → safety verdict → fix loop (≤3). Mode B — write YAML → `sf agent test create` → `sf agent test run --wait 10` → `sf agent test results --job-id` → parse per-case `topic_assertion`/`action_assertion`/`output_validation` → resolve topic names (run, inspect `generatedData.topic`, redeploy with `--force-overwrite`). Mode C1 — read `.agent`, derive surface, name domain, map surface→cases, write YAML, validate locally with the reference checker, then `--preview` (C1-author) or deploy+run (C1-run). Mode C2 — 1. verify sandbox and resolve bundle via `GenAiPlannerDefinition`; 2. send cases, one fresh session each; 3. judge PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE with confidence and one-line risk; 4. score; 5. report grade line first; 6. map failures to remediation.
TABLES: "When to use which" — `Scenario | Mode`, 7 rows. Fix loop — `Failure Type | Fix Location | Fix Strategy`, 7 rows (TOPIC_NOT_MATCHED, ACTION_NOT_INVOKED, WRONG_ACTION, UNGROUNDED, LOW_SAFETY, DEFAULT_TOPIC, NO_ACTIONS_IN_TOPIC). Ungrounded vs grounded payload comparison — 2 columns × 3 rows. Exit Codes — `Code | Meaning`, 4 rows (0 passed, 1 some failed, 2 critical, 3 execution error). Troubleshooting — `Issue | Solution`, 5 rows. Security scoring scheme — severity weights plus grade bands. Test File Location Convention — 4 file names under `<project-root>/tests/`.
ANTI-PATTERNS: Generic jailbreak payloads → ground each case in the agent's own actions, gates and domain. Claiming an industry on thin evidence → `generic`. Emitting a case for a surface the agent lacks → "A PASS on a capability the agent lacks is not evidence of safety". Reporting "failed LLM06-003" → quote the surface, e.g. "bypassed `available when @variables.customer_verified == True` on `process_return`". Feeding reference replies into a multi-turn chain → send only the user turns. Treating a bare "yes" as authorization to run → that is `C1-author`; "Do not upgrade it." Asking with structured pickers for org/agent → freeform text; mode may use a picker. Passing `--mode quick`/`--mode full` (removed `security_runner.py` syntax) → tell the user the flag is gone and ask which of the three modes.
TOOLING: `sf agent preview start|send|end --json --authoring-bundle <B> --simulate-actions|--use-live-actions -o <org>`; `sf agent test create --json --spec … --api-name … [--preview] [--force-overwrite]`; `sf agent test run --json --api-name … --wait 10 --result-format json`; `sf agent test results --json --job-id …`; `sf org display --json`; `sf data query`; REST `POST $INSTANCE_URL/services/data/v63.0/actions/custom/flow/{flowApiName}` and `/actions/custom/apex/{className}`. Files: `.sfdx/agents/{BundleName}/sessions/{sessionId}/traces/{planId}.json`, `aiAuthoringBundles/<Name>/<Name>.agent`, `tests/<AgentApiName>-{testing-center,regression,smoke,security}.yaml`, `assets/payloads/*.yaml`.
GOTCHAS: CLI output contains control characters — JSON parsing fails unless stripped. `Nonexistent flag: --simulate-actions` means CLI older than 2.131.0. Empty traces → check `transcript.jsonl` or use Mode B. Topic names in Testing Center differ from `.agent` names; topic hash drift after each publish forces re-discovery. `sf agent test create` validates the whole spec, so one malformed case rejects every case "and its error names no case", while `--preview` "catches none of this (no server validation)". `sf agent test run` has no simulated-action mode, so C1-run executes real Apex/Flows/Prompt Templates. Security `topic_assertion` returns an empty-assertion FAILURE that must be ignored. No HTML/PDF report exists. Voice testing has "no audio/TTS/STT validation in the CLI today". Session timeout → split into smaller batches. `connection voice:` is not a valid surface type — flag it.
STRUCTURE: `references/preview-testing.md`, `batch-testing.md`, `security-test-design.md`, `owasp-categories.md`, `security-scoring-methodology.md`, `remediation-guide.md`, `security-troubleshooting.md`, `action-execution.md`, `test-report-format.md`, `troubleshooting.md`; `assets/payloads/*.yaml` (7 files); `../agentforce-generate/references/voice-latency-heuristics.md` (all declared, not bundled).

## S054 · coverage-analysis
SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.09700, https://clang.llvm.org/docs/SourceBasedCodeCoverage.html, https://llvm.org/docs/CommandGuide/llvm-cov.html, https://gcovr.com/, https://clang.llvm.org/docs/SanitizerCoverage.html
PURPOSE: Measure what a fuzzing campaign actually reaches with llvm-cov, gcov/gcovr or the fuzzer's own coverage output, then convert uncovered regions into harness, seed or dictionary work.
CONCEPTS:
- **Coverage instrumentation** — compiler flags record which code paths actually ran, which is the raw material for every later report. > "Compiler flags that track which code paths are executed"
- **Corpus coverage** — coverage measured by running every case in a corpus, which is why the corpus is the unit of measurement. > "Coverage achieved by running all test cases in a fuzzing corpus"
- **Magic value checks** — conditional checks against hardcoded values block progress and show up as unexplored blocks. > "Hard-to-discover conditional checks that block fuzzer progress"
- **Coverage-guided fuzzing** — the fuzzer itself prioritises inputs that reach new paths, so coverage is both the goal and the feedback signal. > "Fuzzing strategy that prioritizes inputs that discover new code paths"
- **Coverage report** — a textual or visual map of executed against unexecuted code. > "Visual or textual representation of executed vs. unexecuted code"
- **Two purposes** — coverage answers whether the harness reaches the application and whether coverage moves when the harness, fuzzer or SUT changes. > "Understand which parts of your application are actually executed by your fuzzing harnesses"
- **Coverage as proxy** — the author is explicit that coverage indicates capability rather than absolute performance. > "Coverage is a proxy for fuzzer capability and performance."
- **Post-campaign corpus measurement** — the key principle: measure the corpus produced after a campaign, not live fuzzer statistics, so results are reproducible and comparable across tools. > "Use the corpus generated *after* each fuzzing campaign to calculate coverage, rather than real-time fuzzer statistics."
- **Ideal workflow decision tree** — the campaign output branches three ways: increased coverage continues with a larger corpus, decreased coverage means fixing the harness or investigating SUT changes, and a plateau calls for new inputs. > "Add dictionary entries or seed inputs"
- **Execution runtime (`execute-rt.cc`)** — a C/C++ main walks the corpus directory and replays it through the same harness entry point. > "Reuse the same harness function (`LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`) with a different main function"
- **LLVM profile pipeline** — instrument, write a `.profraw`, merge to `.profdata`, then report or render HTML. > "`llvm-cov show ./binary -instr-profile=file.profdata -format=html -output-dir html/`"
- **GCC pipeline** — `-ftest-coverage -fprofile-arcs` produces `.gcda` files that gcovr turns into reports. > "-ftest-coverage -fprofile-arcs"
- **Rust pipeline** — cargo-fuzz generates the profile data and a helper script renders HTML through `cargo cov`. > "cargo +nightly fuzz coverage fuzz_target_1"
- **Report filtering** — harness files are excluded so the numbers describe the SUT. > "Use `-ignore-filename-regex` to focus on SUT coverage only"
- **Fork isolation** — a crashing corpus entry otherwise aborts the whole run, so the runtime forks per file. > "Fork before executing to isolate crashes"
- **Incremental coverage** — GCC instrumentation accumulates `.gcda` state across runs, and `gcovr --delete` resets it. > "GCC's gcov instrumentation incrementally updates `.gcda` files across multiple runs."
- **Differential coverage** — two profiles can be passed to one `llvm-cov show` to compare campaigns. > "Compare coverage between two fuzzing campaigns"
- **Large-codebase tactics** — path-prefix restriction, directory grouping and lcov export keep reports usable. > "Organizes large reports by directory structure instead of flat file list"
- **Per-fuzzer integration** — libFuzzer, AFL++, cargo-fuzz and honggfuzz each need their own note because the feedback instrumentation is not the reporting instrumentation. > "libFuzzer uses LLVM's SanitizerCoverage by default for guiding fuzzing, but you need separate instrumentation for generating reports."
- **CMake wiring** — three targets (`fuzz`, `fuzz_exec`, `program`) separate the fuzzing build from the coverage build. > "target_compile_options(fuzz_exec PRIVATE -O2 -fprofile-instr-generate -fcoverage-mapping)"
- **Skip conditions** — measurement is dropped when crashes are still being found, infrastructure is missing, reports are impractical, or the fuzzer's own metrics suffice. > "Fuzzer's internal coverage metrics are sufficient for your needs"
RULES:
- Measure coverage from the post-campaign corpus, not real-time fuzzer statistics — > "rather than real-time fuzzer statistics"
- Never build coverage with `-fsanitize=fuzzer` — > "Don't use `-fsanitize=fuzzer` for coverage builds"
- Do not use AFL++ instrumentation for coverage builds — > "Don't use AFL++'s instrumentation (`afl-clang-fast`) for coverage builds"
- Do not use `hfuzz-clang` for coverage builds — > "Don't use `hfuzz-clang` for coverage builds"
- Use `-O2` or `-O0`, never `-O3` — > "Use `-O2` or `-O0` for coverage builds"
- Keep one toolchain per coverage build — > "Stick to one toolchain for coverage builds"
- Filter harness files out of reports — > "Use `-ignore-filename-regex` or `--exclude` to filter harness files"
- Use LLVM 18+ for directory coverage of large reports — > "Use LLVM 18+ with `-show-directory-coverage`"
- Use gcovr 5.1+ with Clang 14+ — > "Use gcovr 5.1+ for Clang 14+"
- Skip the technique when crashes are still being found or internal metrics suffice — > "Fuzzing campaign is actively finding crashes"
- Store timestamped profiles and track the trend — > "Store coverage data with timestamps and track trends"
- Fix crashes first or fork-isolate them before generating coverage — > "Fix crashes first, or use process forking to isolate them"
WORKFLOW: Step 1 build with instrumentation (`clang++ -fprofile-instr-generate -fcoverage-mapping -O2 -DNO_MAIN main.cc harness.cc execute-rt.cc -o fuzz_exec`; `g++ -ftest-coverage -fprofile-arcs …`; `rustup toolchain install nightly --component llvm-tools-preview` + `cargo +nightly fuzz coverage fuzz_target_1`). Step 2 create `execute-rt.cc` (C/C++ only). Step 3 execute on corpus (`LLVM_PROFILE_FILE=fuzz.profraw ./fuzz_exec corpus/`; `./fuzz_exec_gcov corpus/`). Step 4 process data (`llvm-profdata merge -sparse fuzz.profraw -o fuzz.profdata`; `llvm-cov report …`; `llvm-cov show … -format=html -output-dir fuzz_html/`; `gcovr --html-details -o coverage.html`; Rust `./generate_html fuzz_target_1 src/lib.rs`). Step 5 analyse: uncovered blocks, magic-value checks, dead code, coverage deltas vs baseline.
TABLES: "Key Concepts" — `Concept | Description`, 5 rows. "Quick Reference" — `Task | Command/Pattern`, 7 rows. Ideal-workflow decision diagram — one source, three branches. "Tips and Tricks" — `Tip | Why It Helps`, 6 rows. "Anti-Patterns" — `Anti-Pattern | Problem | Correct Approach`, 6 rows. "Troubleshooting" — `Issue | Cause | Solution`, 8 rows. "Tools That Use This Technique" — `Skill | How It Applies`, 4 rows. "Related Techniques" — `Skill | Relationship`, 4 rows.
ANTI-PATTERNS: Using fuzzer-reported coverage for cross-tool comparisons → dedicated tools. Building coverage with `-O3` → `-O2`/`-O0`. Not filtering harness code → `-ignore-filename-regex`/`--exclude`. Mixing LLVM and GCC instrumentation → one toolchain. Ignoring crashing inputs → fix crashes or fork-isolate. One-time coverage checks → store timestamped `.profdata` and track trends.
TOOLING: `clang++`, `g++`, `llvm-profdata merge -sparse`, `llvm-cov report|show|export`, `gcovr` (`uv tool install gcovr`, `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"`), `cargo +nightly fuzz coverage`, `cargo install cargo-binutils rustfilt`, `cargo +nightly cov -- show`, `-Xdemangler=rustfilt`, `-show-line-counts-or-regions`, `-show-instantiations`, `AFL_USE_ASAN=0`, CMake `target_compile_options(fuzz_exec PRIVATE -O2 -fprofile-instr-generate -fcoverage-mapping)`.
GOTCHAS: `error: no profile data available` (unset `LLVM_PROFILE_FILE`); `Failed to load coverage` (binary/profile mismatch); 0% reports from using the fuzzing binary instead of the instrumented one; `no_working_dir_found` from gcovr → `--gcov-ignore-errors=no_working_dir_found`; crashing corpus entries prevent any coverage output; coverage dropping after a harness change; flat HTML file lists on pre-18 LLVM; `incompatible instrumentation` from mixed toolchains.
STRUCTURE: none bundled.

## S055 · cargo-fuzz
SOURCE: https://rust-fuzz.github.io/book/cargo-fuzz.html, https://docs.rs/arbitrary/latest/arbitrary/, https://github.com/rust-fuzz/cargo-fuzz, https://rustup.rs/
PURPOSE: Set up and run cargo-fuzz on a Cargo Rust crate: init the fuzz target, write a `fuzz_target!` harness, choose sanitizers, generate coverage, and reproduce a saved crash artifact.
CONCEPTS:
- **libFuzzer backend** — cargo-fuzz is a thin Cargo subcommand over libFuzzer that turns the right compilation flags on for you, including sanitizer support. > "It uses libFuzzer as the backend and provides a convenient Cargo subcommand that automatically enables relevant compilation flags for your Rust project"
- **Nightly requirement** — the toolchain floor is nightly because the flags it needs are unstable features. > "cargo-fuzz requires the nightly Rust toolchain because it uses features only available in nightly."
- **Fuzzer selection** — cargo-fuzz is presented as the default for Cargo projects, with AFL++ for multi-core or non-Cargo work and LibAFL for custom fuzzers. > "cargo-fuzz is currently the primary and most mature fuzzing solution for Rust projects using Cargo."
- **Library-crate structure** — the fuzzable code has to be reachable from a library, which is why a binary project is split first. > "cargo-fuzz works best when your code is structured as a library crate."
- **Harness shape** — a `no_main` target that validates input size and calls the target through the `fuzz_target!` macro. > "Validate input size if needed"
- **Structure-aware fuzzing** — deriving `Arbitrary` gives the fuzzer typed values automatically, so the harness works on the type rather than slicing raw bytes. > "structure-aware fuzzing with automatic derivation for Rust types"
- **Sanitizer policy** — ASan is on by default and is what catches memory errors. > "ASan is enabled by default and detects memory errors"
- **Unsafe detection** — `cargo geiger` decides whether the sanitizer can be dropped. > "Check if your project uses unsafe code"
- **Corpus and artifacts** — inputs and crashes land in two fixed directories the runner knows about. > "Corpus location: `fuzz/corpus/fuzz_target_1/`"
- **Replay modes** — a saved artifact can be replayed directly, and the whole corpus can be executed without mutation. > "Run all corpus entries without fuzzing"
- **libFuzzer options** — everything after `--` is passed through to libFuzzer. > "Pass options to libFuzzer after `--`"
- **Output vocabulary** — `NEW`, `pulse`, `INITED` and a crash with a stack trace each mean one specific thing. > "| `NEW` | New coverage-increasing input discovered |"
- **Coverage pipeline** — cargo-fuzz emits profile data and a helper script renders it. > "cargo-fuzz integrates with Rust's coverage tools to analyze fuzzing effectiveness."
- **Multi-core caveat** — the built-in parallel mode is not production-ready. > "The multi-core fuzzing feature is experimental and not recommended."
- **Worked example** — the ogg crate parser is used because parsers consume untrusted input. > "Parsers are excellent fuzzing targets because they handle untrusted data."
RULES:
- Requires nightly and a Cargo project — > "Your project uses Cargo (required)"
- Structure the crate as a library — > "Structure code as library crate"
- Use the `fuzz_target!` macro instead of a custom main — > "Use `fuzz_target!` macro"
- Handle expected errors instead of panicking, and keep the harness deterministic — > "Keep harness deterministic"
- Disable sanitizers only for pure safe Rust, where it buys about 2x — > "ASan adds ~2x overhead"
- Prefer several manual instances over `--jobs` — > "The multi-core fuzzing feature is experimental and not recommended."
- Verify both installs before fuzzing — > "cargo +nightly --version"
- Start from a seed corpus and add a dictionary for parsers — > "Start with a seed corpus"
- Use `-runs=0` to execute the corpus without fuzzing — > "Run all corpus entries without fuzzing"
WORKFLOW: 1. `rustup install nightly`; `cargo install cargo-fuzz`. 2. Split the binary crate into `src/main.rs` + `src/lib.rs`. 3. `cargo fuzz init` (creates `fuzz/Cargo.toml`, `fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_target_1.rs`). 4. Write the harness; optionally derive `Arbitrary`. 5. `cargo +nightly fuzz run fuzz_target_1`. 6. Reproduce a crash: `cargo +nightly fuzz run fuzz_target_1 fuzz/artifacts/fuzz_target_1/crash-<hash>`. 7. Coverage: install `llvm-tools-preview`, `cargo-binutils`, `rustfilt`; `cargo +nightly fuzz coverage fuzz_target_1`; `./generate_html fuzz_target_1 src/lib.rs` → `fuzz_html/`.
TABLES: Fuzzer comparison — `Fuzzer | Best For | Complexity`, 3 rows. "Harness Rules" — `Do | Don't`, 4 rows. "Interpreting Output" — `Output | Meaning`, 4 rows. "Tips and Tricks" — `Tip | Why It Helps`, 5 rows. "Troubleshooting" — `Problem | Cause | Solution`, 6 rows. "Technique Skills" — `Skill | Use Case`, 5 rows. "Related Fuzzers" — `Skill | When to Consider`, 3 rows.
ANTI-PATTERNS: Everything in `main.rs` → move fuzzable code into `lib.rs` ("`cannot find binary`"). Custom `main` function → `fuzz_target!`. Panicking on expected errors → handle `Result::Err` gracefully. RNG in the harness → keep it deterministic. ASan on pure safe Rust → `--sanitizer none` for 2x. No seed corpus → add sample inputs to `fuzz/corpus/fuzz_target_1/`. No dictionary for a parser → create one with magic values.
TOOLING: `cargo fuzz init`, `cargo fuzz build`, `cargo +nightly fuzz run <target> [artifact|corpus] -- <libfuzzer args>`, `--sanitizer none`, `--jobs`, `-dict=`, `-max_len=`, `-timeout=`, `-runs=0`, `-help=1`, `cargo geiger`, `rustup toolchain install nightly --component llvm-tools-preview`, `cargo install cargo-binutils rustfilt`, `cargo +nightly cov -- show -Xdemangler=rustfilt … -show-line-counts-or-regions -show-instantiations -format=html -o fuzz_html/`.
GOTCHAS: "requires nightly" error from using stable → `cargo +nightly fuzz`. Slow fuzzing from ASan on safe Rust. "cannot find binary" means no library crate. Sanitizer compilation issues → try a pinned nightly such as `rustup install nightly-2024-01-01`. Low coverage from a missing seed corpus. Magic value not found → dictionary file. Multi-core support is experimental and may misbehave.
STRUCTURE: none bundled.

## S056 · fuzzing-obstacles
SOURCE: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/afb19f07aecc84998eeea56c4d65f5e0499abb5a/crypto/cmp/cmp_vfy.c#L665-L678, https://github.com/RustAudio/ogg/blob/5ee8316e6e907c24f6d7ec4b3a0ed6a6ce854cc1/src/reading.rs#L298-L300, https://llvm.org/docs/LibFuzzer.html, https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/conditional-compilation.html, https://github.com/openssl/openssl/tree/master/fuzz
PURPOSE: Neutralise anti-fuzzing barriers — checksums, hash verification, magic-value validation, time-based seeds and other non-deterministic global state — behind a fuzzing build flag so the fuzzer reaches deeper code while production behaviour is unchanged.
CONCEPTS:
- **SUT patching** — the System Under Test is modified to be fuzzing-friendly rather than left as written for production. > "Modifying System Under Test to be fuzzing-friendly"
- **Conditional compilation** — the mechanism is a compile-time flag that changes behaviour without a runtime branch in production. > "Code that behaves differently based on compile-time flags"
- **Fuzzing build mode** — a separate build configuration carries all the fuzzing-specific patches. > "Special build configuration that enables fuzzing-specific patches"
- **False positives** — the central risk: crashes found in the patched build that could never occur in production. > "Crashes found during fuzzing that cannot occur in production"
- **Determinism** — the property the patches restore, because global state otherwise makes the same input behave differently per run. > "Same input always produces same behavior (critical for fuzzing)"
- **Obstacle taxonomy** — three families, each with its own reason for blocking: checksums must be guessed exactly, global state breaks reproducibility, and complex validation consumes effort that should go into exploration. > "The fuzzer must guess correct hash values (astronomically unlikely)"
- **Global state failure mode** — same input, different behaviour across runs, which defeats the comparison a fuzzer depends on. > "Same input produces different behavior across runs (breaks determinism)"
- **Validation failure mode** — effort spent on rejections is effort not spent exploring. > "The fuzzer spends effort hitting validation failures instead of exploring deeper code"
- **Macro pair** — C/C++ uses `FUZZING_BUILD_MODE_UNSAFE_FOR_PRODUCTION` and Rust uses the `fuzzing` cfg, in both check and attribute form. > "`#ifdef FUZZING_BUILD_MODE_UNSAFE_FOR_PRODUCTION`"
- **Pattern: checksum bypass** — only the early `return` is guarded so processing continues past the check. > "Only enforced in production"
- **Pattern: deterministic PRNG seeding** — the seed is fixed under the fuzzing macro, keeping every path reachable. > "Fixed seed for fuzzing"
- **Pattern: careful validation skip** — instead of dropping validation, safe defaults substitute for the values it would have guaranteed. > "use safe defaults for failed validation"
- **Pattern: complex format validation bypass** — cheap magic-byte checks stay while structure, checksum and signature validation are gated. > "Keep cheap checks"
- **Effectiveness measurement** — line, block and function coverage plus corpus diversity quantify whether a patch worked. > "Effective patches typically increase coverage by 10-50% or more."
- **Combination techniques** — seeding, dictionaries, structure-aware fuzzing and harness work are alternatives or complements to patching. > "Obstacle patching works well with:"
- **Why patch at all** — the alternative to patching a non-deterministic or checksum-guarded program is not fuzzing it effectively. > "The solution is conditional compilation: modify code behavior during fuzzing builds while keeping production code unchanged."
RULES:
- Apply when the fuzzer stalls at checksum or hash verification — > "The fuzzer gets stuck at checksum or hash verification"
- Apply when coverage shows large unreachable blocks behind validation — > "Coverage reports show large blocks of unreachable code behind validation"
- Skip when a seed corpus or dictionary would do the job — > "The obstacle can be overcome with a good seed corpus or dictionary"
- Keep cheap validation such as magic bytes and size checks — > "Magic bytes and size checks guide fuzzer without much cost"
- Use fixed seeds for PRNGs — > "Makes behavior deterministic while exploring all code paths"
- Patch incrementally, one obstacle at a time, measuring impact — > "Skip one obstacle at a time and measure coverage impact"
- Add defensive defaults when skipping validation — > "When skipping validation, provide safe fallback values"
- Document every patch for future maintainers — > "Future maintainers need to understand fuzzing vs. production differences"
- Confirm coverage actually improved against the unpatched build — > "Compare coverage to the unpatched version"
- Never skip validation wholesale — > "Skip only specific obstacles that block coverage"
- Minimise the difference between fuzzing and production builds — > "Minimize differences between builds"
- Expect roughly 10–50% coverage gain from an effective patch — > "Effective patches typically increase coverage by 10-50% or more."
WORKFLOW: 1. Identify the obstacle (run the fuzzer, analyse coverage, grep for `rand()`/`time()`/`srand()`, find rejecting validation, spot global-state init). 2. Add conditional compilation around the specific check. 3. Verify coverage improvement: rebuild with instrumentation, run briefly, compare to unpatched, confirm new paths. 4. Assess false-positive risk (does downstream code assume validated properties? could crashes be impossible in production? implicit state dependency?) and consider a more targeted patch.
TABLES: "Key Concepts" — `Concept | Description`, 5 rows. "Quick Reference" — `Task | C/C++ | Rust`, 4 rows (build check, skip during fuzzing, common obstacles, supported fuzzers). Four named patterns, each with before/after code and a false-positive risk rating (`LOW`, `LOW`, `MITIGATED`, `MEDIUM`). "Tips and Tricks" — `Tip | Why It Helps`, 5 rows. "Anti-Patterns" — `Anti-Pattern | Problem | Correct Approach`, 5 rows. "Troubleshooting" — `Issue | Cause | Solution`, 5 rows. "Tools That Use This Technique" — `Skill | How It Applies`, 4 rows. "Related Techniques" — `Skill | Relationship`, 4 rows.
ANTI-PATTERNS: Skipping all validation wholesale → "Skip only specific obstacles that block coverage". No risk assessment → analyse downstream assumptions for false positives. Forgetting to document patches → add comments explaining why the patch is safe. Patching without measuring → compare coverage before and after. Over-patching → "Minimize differences between builds" because over-divergence makes production bugs irreproducible.
TOOLING: `clang++ -g -fsanitize=fuzzer,address -DFUZZING_BUILD_MODE_UNSAFE_FOR_PRODUCTION harness.cc target.cc -o fuzzer` (macro normally defined automatically by `-fsanitize=fuzzer`); `afl-clang-fast++ -g -fsanitize=address target.cc harness.cc -o fuzzer` (auto-defines the macro); `afl-clang-lto`; `AFL_LLVM_LAF_ALL`; `hfuzz-clang++ -g -fsanitize=address target.cc harness.cc -o fuzzer`; `cargo fuzz build` / `cargo fuzz run` (sets `fuzzing` cfg); `RUSTFLAGS="--cfg fuzzing"` to enable manually; LibAFL with a manually defined macro.
GOTCHAS: Coverage not improving means the wrong obstacle was identified — profile to find the real bottleneck. Many false-positive crashes mean downstream assumptions — add defensive defaults or partial validation. "Code compiles differently" because the macro isn't defined in all build configs — verify it in all source files and dependencies. Fuzzer finding bugs in patched code means the patch introduced invalid states. Failure to reproduce production bugs means build differences are too large — minimise patches. Dictionaries help with magic bytes "but not checksums or complex validation".
STRUCTURE: none bundled.

## S057 · test-master
SOURCE: https://github.com/Jeffallan (author metadata), company https://synergetic.solutions, docs https://jeffallan.github.io/claude-skills/skills/quality/test-master/, MIT license, version 1.1.1
PURPOSE: Turn an agent into a testing specialist that generates test files, builds mocking strategies, analyses coverage, designs test architectures, and produces test plans and defect reports across functional, performance and security disciplines.
CONCEPTS:
- **scope definition** — The workflow opens by deciding what is in scope and which testing disciplines the target actually needs, so later steps inherit a bounded brief. > "Identify what to test and which testing types apply"
- **testing types matrix** — Functional, performance and security are planned as three parallel perspectives on one strategy rather than as sequential phases. > "Plan the test approach across functional, performance, and security perspectives"
- **assertion specificity** — An assertion must name the expected value, because a truthiness check passes for almost any wrong answer. > "Assert specific outcomes (`expect(result).toBe(90)`), not just truthiness"
- **specification-style naming** — The `it('…')` description is treated as the specification a reader will trust instead of reading the body. > "Use meaningful `it('…')` descriptions that read as plain-English specifications"
- **error-path coverage** — Happy path and failure path are paired obligations; empty input, null and boundary values are the concrete failure cases named. > "Test happy paths AND error/edge cases (e.g., empty input, null, boundary values)"
- **dependency mocking** — Unit tests isolate the unit under test by replacing everything external, so a network or database failure cannot masquerade as a code defect. > "Mock external dependencies — never call real APIs or databases in unit tests"
- **test isolation** — Order-dependence is forbidden because a suite that only passes in one sequence hides the real defect and breaks under sharding. > "Create order-dependent tests — each test must be independently runnable"
- **failure classification** — Step 4 asks what kind of failure occurred before fixing anything, separating a wrong assertion from an environment or flakiness cause. > "classify the failure (assertion error vs. environment/flakiness), fix root cause, re-run"
- **flaky-test handling** — Flakiness is treated as a real defect with causes to isolate, and the remedy escalates from ordering and async checks to retry or stabilization. > "isolate ordering dependencies, check async handling, add retry or stabilization logic"
- **root-cause fixing** — A test that is quarantined must still be repaired; re-running until green is rejected as a way of closing the ticket. > "quarantine and fix them; don't just re-run until green"
- **coverage gating** — Coverage is a closing condition with an explicit obligation to name the gaps, not a number that ends the work when met. > "Verify coverage targets are met before closing; flag gaps explicitly"
- **severity rating scale** — Findings leave the skill graded on a four-level scale so the reader can order remediation. > "Findings with severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low)"
- **behavioural testing** — Internal calls are excluded from assertions because they pin the implementation; only observable behaviour is a valid target. > "Test implementation details (internal method calls) — test observable behaviour"
- **progressive disclosure reference set** — Ten topic reference files are declared behind a Topic / Reference / Load When table, so the agent loads one domain at a time instead of the whole corpus. > "| Testing Anti-Patterns | `references/testing-anti-patterns.md` | Test review, mock issues, test quality problems |"
- **report template** — Output is a five-part artefact: scope and approach, cases with expected outcomes, coverage analysis, graded findings, and fix recommendations. > "Document findings with severity ratings and actionable fix recommendations"
- **fixtures/factories** — Real customer data is replaced by constructed data that the test controls, which also makes the failure reproducible. > "Use production data in tests — use fixtures or factories instead"
- **toolchain coverage** — The trigger surface names concrete performance and security tools rather than generic categories. > "performance testing with k6 or Artillery; security testing with OWASP methods"
- **shift-left / quality gate / continuous testing** — The activation vocabulary comes from QA-process language, so process questions invoke the skill as readily as code-writing ones. > "working on QA, regression, test automation, quality gates, shift-left testing, or test maintenance"
RULES:
- Test the failure branch as deliberately as the success branch, including empty input, null and boundary values — > "Test happy paths AND error/edge cases (e.g., empty input, null, boundary values)"
- Mock every external dependency in unit tests; never reach a real API or database — > "Mock external dependencies — never call real APIs or databases in unit tests"
- Write `it('…')` descriptions that read as specifications and assert specific outcomes such as `expect(result).toBe(90)`, not truthiness — > "Use meaningful `it('…')` descriptions that read as plain-English specifications"
- Run tests in CI/CD, and document and remediate coverage gaps rather than only reporting the percentage — > "Run tests in CI/CD; document and remediate coverage gaps"
- Never test only the success branch of a try/catch — > "Skip error-path testing (e.g., don't test only the success branch of a try/catch)"
- Use fixtures or factories instead of production data in tests — > "Use production data in tests — use fixtures or factories instead"
- Make each test independently runnable; never create order-dependent tests — > "Create order-dependent tests — each test must be independently runnable"
- Never ignore flaky tests: quarantine and fix them instead of re-running until green — > "Ignore flaky tests — quarantine and fix them; don't just re-run until green"
- Never assert on internal method calls; test observable behaviour — > "Test implementation details (internal method calls) — test observable behaviour"
- On failure, classify assertion vs environment/flakiness, fix the root cause, then re-run; on flakiness, isolate ordering deps and check async handling before adding retry — > "If tests fail: classify the failure (assertion error vs. environment/flakiness), fix root cause, re-run"
- The pytest form keeps the same structure with `def test_…` and `assert result == expected` — > "Apply the same structure for pytest (`def test_…`, `assert result == expected`) and other frameworks."
WORKFLOW:
1. Define scope — identify what to test and which testing types apply.
2. Create strategy — plan across functional, performance, security perspectives.
3. Write tests — implement with proper assertions.
4. Execute — run tests and collect results; on failure classify → fix root cause → re-run; on flakiness isolate ordering deps → check async → add retry/stabilization.
5. Report — document findings with severity ratings and actionable fixes; verify coverage targets before closing, flag gaps.
TABLES:
- Reference Guide table: Topic | Reference | Load When (10 rows: Unit Testing, Integration, E2E, Performance, Security, Reports, QA Methodology, Automation, TDD Iron Laws, Testing Anti-Patterns).
- Good/bad inline example commentary in the Jest snippet (annotated "✅ Good" patterns).
ANTI-PATTERNS:
- Testing only the success branch of try/catch → also test the error branch.
- Truthiness assertions → assert the specific expected value.
- Production data in tests → fixtures or factories.
- Order-dependent tests → each test independently runnable.
- Ignoring flaky tests / re-running until green → quarantine and fix root cause.
- Testing internal method calls → test observable behaviour.
- Using real APIs or databases in unit tests → mock external dependencies.
TOOLING:
- `Jest` example: `describe`, `it`, `expect(...).toBe(90)`, `.toThrow('Price must be non-negative')`.
- pytest equivalents `def test_…`, `assert result == expected`.
- k6 / Artillery (performance), OWASP (security), Supertest (API), Vitest.
- Skill metadata keys: `name`, `description`, `license: MIT`, `metadata.author`, `metadata.company`, `metadata.version: "1.1.1"`, `metadata.domain: quality`, `metadata.triggers`, `metadata.role: specialist`, `metadata.scope: testing`, `metadata.output-format: report`, `metadata.related-skills`.
GOTCHAS:
- Tests that pass locally may be flaky in CI; the file warns that ordering dependencies and mishandled async cause intermittent failures.
- Coverage targets can be met superficially; file requires flagging gaps rather than declaring done on the number.
- Failure classified wrongly as code bug when it's environment/flakiness, causing wrong fixes.
STRUCTURE:
- `references/unit-testing.md`, `references/integration-testing.md`, `references/e2e-testing.md`, `references/performance-testing.md`, `references/security-testing.md`, `references/test-reports.md`, `references/qa-methodology.md`, `references/automation-frameworks.md`, `references/tdd-iron-laws.md`, `references/testing-anti-patterns.md` — all declared, not bundled.

## S058 · fuzzing-dictionary
SOURCE: https://github.com/AFLplusplus/AFLplusplus/tree/stable/dictionaries (AFL++ Dictionaries), https://llvm.org/docs/LibFuzzer.html#dictionaries, https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/master/projects
PURPOSE: Build fuzzing dictionary files so a fuzzer can emit the keywords, magic bytes and tokens a parser/protocol/file-format target checks for, then wire that dictionary into libFuzzer, AFL++ or cargo-fuzz.
CONCEPTS:
- **dictionary entry** — A dictionary is a line-oriented text file where each line is one token, either a bare quoted string or a name plus quoted value. > "A quoted string (e.g., `"keyword"`) or key-value pair (e.g., `kw="value"`)"
- **hex escapes** — Binary tokens are written with escape sequences because a text file cannot otherwise carry the non-printable bytes a format expects. > "Byte sequences like `"\xF7\xF8"` for non-printable characters"
- **token injection** — The point of the dictionary is to bias mutation away from random bytes toward tokens that pass early validation and reach deeper code. > "Instead of purely random mutations, the fuzzer incorporates known keywords, magic numbers, protocol commands, and format-specific strings"
- **cross-fuzzer format** — One file format serves every mainstream engine, so a dictionary is not tied to the tool that generated it. > "Dictionary files work with libFuzzer, AFL++, and cargo-fuzz"
- **extraction from headers** — C headers already enumerate the string constants a parser compares against, so a one-line grep harvests them. > "grep -o '".*"' header.h > header.dict"
- **extraction from man pages** — For CLI tools the flags themselves are the vocabulary the argument parser validates, harvested and re-quoted into entries. > "man curl | grep -oP '^\s*(--|-)\K\S+' | sed 's/[,.]$//' | sed 's/^/"&/; s/$/&"/' | sort -u > man.dict"
- **extraction from binary strings** — Built binaries retain their format strings and keywords, so `strings` plus re-quoting produces a dictionary from a shipped artefact. > "strings ./binary | sed 's/^/"&/; s/$/&"/' > strings.dict"
- **LLM-generated dictionary** — The prompt asks the model for the format's magic bytes, chunk types and header values in dictionary syntax, including hex escapes for binary values. > "Each line should be a quoted string or key-value pair like kw="value". Include magic bytes, chunk types, and common header values."
- **AUTODICTIONARY / AFL_LLVM_DICT2FILE** — The compiler wrapper captures the string comparisons it instruments and writes them out as dictionary entries at build time. > "AFL++ automatically extracts dictionary entries from string comparisons in the binary"
- **multi-dictionary composition** — Token sets from different sources are kept separate and passed together instead of being merged into one master file. > "AFL++ supports multiple `-x` flags for multiple dictionaries"
- **coverage-effectiveness comparison** — The dictionary is judged by whether coverage improves against a no-dictionary run, making its value measurable rather than assumed. > "Test dictionary effectiveness | Run with and without dict, compare coverage |"
- **boundary values in dict** — Numeric edge literals are added as tokens because parsers branch on exactly those values. > "Include boundary values | `"0"`, `"-1"`, `"2147483647"` trigger edge cases |"
- **format delimiters** — Structural punctuation is included so mutations can assemble syntactically valid records rather than only valid tokens. > "`:`, `=`, `{`, `}` help fuzzer construct valid structures"
- **go-fuzz workaround** — Engines without dictionary support get tokens through the corpus instead, each token written as a corpus file named by its hash. > "go-fuzz does not have built-in dictionary support, but you can manually seed the corpus with dictionary entries"
- **related techniques** — Corpus supplies structure while the dictionary supplies vocabulary, and coverage data is the arbiter of whether the added tokens helped. > "Dictionaries complement corpus: corpus provides structure, dictionary provides keywords"
RULES:
- One quoted string or `kw="value"` pair per line, with `#` comments and blank lines ignored — > "Create a text file with quoted strings on each line."
- Escape backslash as `\\` and quotes as `\"`; escape arbitrary bytes as `\xAB` — > "Use \xAB for hex values"
- The keyword name before `=` may be omitted, so a bare `"foo\x0Abar"` is a valid entry — > "the name of the keyword followed by '=' may be omitted:"
- Keep dictionaries focused at 50–200 entries rather than thousands — > "Keep dictionaries focused | 50-200 entries perform better than thousands |"
- Do not include prose: split full sentences into individual atomic keywords — > "Including full sentences | Fuzzer needs atomic tokens, not prose | Break into individual keywords"
- Deduplicate entries with `sort -u` before using the file — > "Duplicating entries | Wastes mutation budget | Use `sort -u` to deduplicate"
- Write binary values with `\xXX` escapes rather than literal bytes — > "Missing hex escapes | Non-printable bytes become mangled | Use `\xXX` for binary values"
- Document sections of the file with `#` comments so it stays auditable — > "No comments | Hard to maintain and audit | Document sections with `#` comments"
- Keep entries shorter than `-max_len`, or raise `-max_len`; longer entries are silently ignored — > "Dictionary entries longer than `-max_len` are ignored"
- Apply the technique when coverage stalls at validation or the target compares fixed strings; skip pure algorithms and targets with no keyword parsing — > "Coverage plateaus early without reaching deeper logic"
WORKFLOW:
1. Create Dictionary File — quoted strings per line with `#` comments and escapes.
2. Generate Dictionary Content — choose method: LLM prompt, header files, man pages, or binary strings.
3. Pass Dictionary to Fuzzer — fuzzer-appropriate flag.
4. (Advanced) Auto-generate with `export AFL_LLVM_DICT2FILE=auto.dict` + `afl-clang-lto++ target.cc -o target`, then `afl-fuzz -x auto.dict -i in -o out -- ./target`.
TABLES:
- Key Concepts table: Concept | Description (4 rows: Dictionary Entry, Hex Escapes, Token Injection, Cross-Fuzzer Format).
- Quick Reference table: Task | Command/Pattern (5 rows: libFuzzer, AFL++, cargo-fuzz, extract from header, generate from binary).
- Tips and Tricks table: Tip | Why It Helps (5 rows: combine methods, boundary values, delimiters, 50-200 focus, test effectiveness).
- Anti-Patterns table: Anti-Pattern | Problem | Correct Approach (5 rows).
- Troubleshooting table: Issue | Cause | Solution (5 rows).
- Tools That Use This Technique table: Skill | How It Applies (libfuzzer, aflpp, cargo-fuzz).
- Related Techniques table: Skill | Relationship (fuzzing-corpus, coverage-analysis, harness-writing).
ANTI-PATTERNS:
- Including full sentences → break into individual atomic keywords.
- Duplicating entries → `sort -u` to deduplicate.
- Over-sized dictionaries → keep 50-200 most relevant entries.
- Missing hex escapes → non-printable bytes become mangled; use `\xXX`.
- No comments → document sections with `#` for maintainability and audit.
TOOLING:
- libFuzzer: `./fuzz -dict=./dictionary.dict corpus/`; combine with `-max_len`; `-print_final_stats=1` shows dictionary effectiveness.
- AFL++: `afl-fuzz -x ./dictionary.dict -i input/ -o output/ -- ./target @@`.
- cargo-fuzz: `cargo fuzz run fuzz_target -- -dict=./dictionary.dict`; place dict in `fuzz/` and reference `-dict=../dictionary.dict`.
- AFL++ auto: `export AFL_LLVM_DICT2FILE=auto.dict`, `afl-clang-lto++`.
- go-fuzz: `grep -o '".*"' dict.txt | while read line; do echo -n "$line" | base64 > corpus/$(echo "$line" | md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1); done`.
GOTCHAS:
- Dictionary silently unused if path wrong or format invalid — check fuzzer output for dict parsing errors.
- Unescaped quotes or invalid escapes produce syntax errors; validate with a test run.
- No coverage improvement often means tokens are irrelevant to actual comparisons, not that dictionaries fail.
- Oversized dictionary "Slows fuzzer, dilutes useful tokens".
- go-fuzz has no built-in dictionary support at all.
- Auto-dictionary only exists with the `afl-clang-lto` compiler path.
STRUCTURE:
- none (single-file technique skill; external resource links only).

## S059 · playwright-expert
SOURCE: https://github.com/Jeffallan (author), https://synergetic.solutions, docs https://jeffallan.github.io/claude-skills/skills/quality/playwright-expert/, MIT, version 1.1.0
PURPOSE: Make an agent write and maintain Playwright E2E browser tests — page objects, fixtures, reporters, API mocking, visual regression and CI integration — and debug flaky browser tests.
CONCEPTS:
- **Page Object Model** — A page class owns its locators and exposes intent-level methods, so the test file reads as a user journey and selector changes stay in one file. > "await loginPage.login('user@example.com', '<test-password>');"
- **role-based locators** — Selectors keyed on accessible role and name survive styling refactors that break class-based chains. > "// ✅ Role-based selector — resilient to styling changes"
- **auto-waiting** — Waiting is delegated to the locator actions instead of being written as fixed sleeps in the test body. > "Leverage auto-waiting (don't add arbitrary timeouts)"
- **test independence** — Fresh state per test, built in `beforeEach`, is what makes parallel execution safe. > "Keep tests independent (no shared state)"
- **trace/screenshot capture** — The config records artefacts only when they are needed, keeping routine runs cheap and failures diagnosable. > "// 1. Run failing test with trace enabled"
- **trace viewer workflow** — The capture is only useful once opened as a timeline; the viewer command is part of the debugging loop. > "// 3. Open trace viewer to inspect timeline"
- **state-based wait** — Replacing a sleep with an explicit element-state wait removes the race instead of widening it. > "await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' }).waitFor({ state: 'visible' });"
- **stability verification** — A fix is only claimed after the test is run ten times, because one green run proves nothing about a flake. > "Verify fix — run test 10x to confirm stability"
- **retry capture** — Retries exist to produce a trace for an intermittent failure, and the switch is `--retries=2`. > "// 2. Re-run with retries to capture trace"
- **assertion vocabulary** — Assertions are written against URL, visibility and text so the failure message states what the user should have seen. > "await expect(page).toHaveURL('/dashboard');"
- **accessibility-adjacent selectors** — Error regions are located by alert role, mirroring how assistive technology finds them. > "this.errorMessage = page.getByRole('alert');"
- **parallel execution / CI/CD integration** — Parallel running and pipeline placement are named as required operating modes rather than options. > "Run tests in parallel"
- **API mocking / route interception** — Network-level isolation is a declared reference topic so tests can control backend responses. > "| API Mocking | `references/api-mocking.md` | Route interception, mocking |"
- **visual comparisons** — Visual regression is listed as a knowledge area the skill is expected to perform. > "implement API mocking, or perform visual regression testing"
- **fixtures** — Setup objects are part of the page-object infrastructure and are emitted alongside it. > "Fixture setup if needed"
- **output template** — Deliverables are an ordered set: page classes, test files, fixtures, then configuration advice. > "Test files with proper assertions"
RULES:
- Prefer role-based selectors whenever a role and accessible name exist — > "Use role-based selectors when possible"
- Rely on auto-waiting instead of adding arbitrary timeouts — > "Leverage auto-waiting (don't add arbitrary timeouts)"
- Give each test its own state; never share state between tests — > "Keep tests independent (no shared state)"
- Route test interaction through page objects for maintainability — > "Use Page Object Model for maintainability"
- Enable traces and screenshots so failures can be debugged after the fact — > "Enable traces/screenshots for debugging"
- Run the suite in parallel — > "Run tests in parallel"
- Never call `waitForTimeout()`; wait on element state instead — > "Use `waitForTimeout()` (use proper waits)"
- Never anchor tests on CSS class selectors — > "Rely on CSS class selectors (brittle)"
- Never ignore flaky tests; capture a trace with retries and fix the wait — > "Ignore flaky tests"
- Avoid `first()` and `nth()` index picking unless there is a stated reason — > "Use `first()`, `nth()` without good reason"
WORKFLOW:
1. Analyze requirements — identify user flows to test.
2. Setup — configure Playwright with proper settings.
3. Write tests — use POM pattern, proper selectors, auto-waiting.
4. Debug — run test → check trace → identify issue → fix → verify fix (trace enabled, `--retries=2`, `show-trace`, then `--repeat-each=10`).
5. Integrate — add to CI/CD pipeline.
TABLES:
- Reference Guide table: Topic | Reference | Load When (5 rows: Selectors, Page Objects, API Mocking, Configuration, Debugging).
- Implicit correct/wrong comparison pairs in code comments (role vs CSS, arbitrary timeout vs `waitFor`).
ANTI-PATTERNS:
- `waitForTimeout(2000)` → wait on element state (`waitFor({ state: 'visible' })`).
- `.btn-primary.submit-btn` CSS chains → `getByRole` with accessible name.
- Shared state between tests → fresh `beforeEach` setup.
- Ignoring flaky tests → capture trace with retries and fix the wait.
- `first()`/`nth()` index picking → role/label-based targeting unless justified.
TOOLING:
- `@playwright/test` imports `test`, `expect`, `type Page`, `type Locator`.
- Config keys: `use: { trace: 'on-first-retry', screenshot: 'only-on-failure' }`.
- Commands: `npx playwright test --retries=2`, `npx playwright show-trace test-results/.../trace.zip`, `npx playwright test --repeat-each=10`.
- `playwright.config.ts` named as the configuration artefact.
GOTCHAS:
- Arbitrary timeouts create flakiness that survives retries; the fix is state-based waiting.
- CSS class selectors "breaks on refactor" — silent test drift after styling changes.
- Trace files are only written when `trace` is enabled and (with `on-first-retry`) only after a retry occurs.
- A single passing re-run does not prove a flake is fixed; requires `--repeat-each=10`.
STRUCTURE:
- `references/selectors-locators.md`, `references/page-object-model.md`, `references/api-mocking.md`, `references/configuration.md`, `references/debugging-flaky.md` — all declared, not bundled.

## S060 · libfuzzer
SOURCE: https://llvm.org/docs/LibFuzzer.html, https://github.com/google/fuzzing/blob/master/tutorial/libFuzzerTutorial.md, https://clang.llvm.org/docs/SanitizerCoverage.html, structure-aware doc https://github.com/google/fuzzing/blob/master/docs/structure-aware-fuzzing.md
PURPOSE: Set up, compile, run and triage coverage-guided libFuzzer campaigns on C/C++ code with Clang — harness structure, sanitizer builds, corpus/dictionary management, coverage analysis and crash triage.
CONCEPTS:
- **LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput** — The harness is a plain function the runtime calls in-process with each input, which is why per-call cost dominates campaign throughput. > "libFuzzer calls the `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` function repeatedly with different inputs."
- **-fsanitize=fuzzer** — One flag supplies the runtime entry point and the coverage instrumentation the campaign steers by. > "Enables SanitizerCoverage instrumentation for coverage tracking"
- **-fsanitize=fuzzer-no-link** — Library builds get instrumentation without the runtime, so the harness link step decides where `main` comes from. > "Instrument without linking fuzzer (for libraries)"
- **FuzzedDataProvider** — Structured parameters are extracted from the raw byte stream by a helper that consumes typed values in a fixed order. > "For complex inputs (strings, multiple parameters), use the `FuzzedDataProvider` helper"
- **interleaved fuzzing** — Related functions that take the same argument shape share one harness, with the first byte selecting the branch. > "Use a single harness to test multiple related functions"
- **harness determinism** — Reproducibility is a harness property: identical bytes must produce identical behaviour, so global state is reset and no RNG is used. > "Crashes must be reproducible after fuzzing completes"
- **corpus** — The corpus is the accumulated set of inputs that each reach distinct code paths, and its filenames are content hashes. > "Input files that trigger unique code paths"
- **corpus minimization** — Merging into a fresh directory keeps only the entries that still contribute coverage. > "This creates a deduplicated, minimized corpus in `minimized_corpus/`."
- **-fork / -ignore_crashes** — Campaign continuation after a crash is opt-in, because the default is to stop at the first finding. > "allow fuzzing to continue after finding crashes"
- **-jobs / -workers** — Multi-core is expressed as N campaigns served by N processes with one shared test-case directory. > "Test cases are shared between jobs"
- **-max_len** — Input size is bounded deliberately rather than left at the default, with a size heuristic tied to realistic inputs. > "Rule of thumb: 2x the size of minimal realistic input."
- **-close_fd_mask=3** — Silencing the target's own output is a throughput measure, not a debugging measure. > "| `-close_fd_mask=3` | Closes stdout/stderr, speeds up fuzzing |"
- **-rss_limit_mb=0** — ASan's enormous virtual reservation collides with the RSS limit, so the limit is disabled for sanitizer runs. > "Requires ~20TB virtual memory (disable memory limits: `-rss_limit_mb=0`)"
- **-seed=<value>** — Campaign replay is available but only in single-core mode, which limits how far it reproduces a parallel run. > "Use `-seed=<value>` to reproduce a fuzzing campaign (single-core only)."
- **coverage statistics vocabulary** — The console line is read as a tuple of coverage, corpus size, executions per second and memory. > "#2      INITED cov: 3 ft: 4 corp: 1/1b exec/s: 0 rss: 26Mb"
- **crash artefacts** — Each finding is written next to the binary under a hash name, with the input emitted in three encodings for triage. > "The crash is saved to `./crash-<hash>` with the input shown in hex, UTF-8, and Base64."
- **source-based coverage** — Detailed coverage requires a second instrumented build, a profile file per process, a merge, and then a report render. > "llvm-cov show ./fuzz -instr-profile=coverage.profdata -format=html > coverage.html"
- **sanitizer tiers** — Each sanitizer targets a distinct bug class and some, like MSan, impose build-wide requirements on dependencies. > "MSan detects uninitialized memory reads."
- **ASAN_OPTIONS tuning** — Runtime behaviour is adjusted with environment variables, including turning errors into aborts so the fuzzer notices them. > "`abort_on_error=1`: Call `abort()` instead of `_exit()` on errors"
- **custom mutator/crossover** — When byte mutation cannot produce valid structure, the mutation strategy itself is replaced through the two exported hooks. > "libFuzzer allows custom mutators for specialized fuzzing"
- **structure-aware fuzzing** — For highly structured formats the input is a typed message that mutation preserves, then converted back to bytes by the harness. > "libFuzzer mutates protobuf messages (structure-preserving mutations)"
- **fuzzer selection matrix** — The choice between libFuzzer, AFL++, LibAFL and Honggfuzz is framed by setup cost and by whether a later migration is acceptable. > "Transitioning to AFL++ later is an option (harnesses are compatible)"
RULES:
- The harness must return 0, since non-zero is reserved — > "Always return 0 (non-zero reserved for future use)"
- Handle empty, huge and malformed inputs; join threads before returning; keep the harness fast, deterministic and narrowly targeted — > "Handle all input types (empty, huge, malformed)"
- Never call `exit()`, never leave threads running, never use RNG or `/dev/random`, never rely on state from a previous execution — > "Call `exit()` - stops fuzzing process"
- Target hundreds to thousands of executions per second per core — > "Aim for 100s-1000s executions per second per core"
- Build with `-fsanitize=fuzzer,address -g -O2 -U_FORTIFY_SOURCE` and prefer `-O2` over `-O0` — > "clang++ -fsanitize=fuzzer,address -g -O2 -U_FORTIFY_SOURCE harness.cc target.cc -o fuzz"
- Campaigns are expected to run for days or weeks rather than minutes — > "| Run for days/weeks, not minutes | Coverage plateaus take time to break |"
- Run `./fuzz -fork=1 -ignore_crashes=1 corpus/` so fuzzing continues past the first crash — > "./fuzz -fork=1 -ignore_crashes=1 corpus/"
- Choose libFuzzer for quick single-core setup on a Clang project, accepting a later move to AFL++ — > "You need a simple, quick setup for C/C++ code"
WORKFLOW:
1. Write harness with `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` (size validation, optional structured decode, target call, `return 0`).
2. Compile: `clang++ -fsanitize=fuzzer,address -g -O2 -U_FORTIFY_SOURCE harness.cc target.cc -o fuzz`.
3. Create corpus (`mkdir corpus/`) and seed with valid examples.
4. Run: `./fuzz corpus/`; recommended `./fuzz -fork=1 -ignore_crashes=1 corpus/`.
5. Tune: `-max_len=4000`, `-timeout=2`, `-dict=./format.dict`, `-close_fd_mask=3`; scale with `-jobs=4 -workers=4`.
6. Reproduce/minimize: `./fuzz ./crash-<hash>`, `./fuzz -runs=0 corpus/`, `-merge=1`.
7. Coverage: recompile with profiling → run with `LLVM_PROFILE_FILE` → `llvm-profdata merge` → `llvm-cov show`.
TABLES:
- Fuzzer comparison table: Fuzzer | Best For | Complexity (libFuzzer/AFL++/LibAFL/Honggfuzz).
- Harness Rules table: Do | Don't (6 rows).
- Build Flags table: Flag | Purpose (7 rows).
- Fuzzer output table: Output | Meaning (INITED, NEW, REDUCE, cov, corp, exec/s, rss).
- Common Sanitizer Issues table: Issue | Solution (5 rows).
- Tips and Tricks table: Tip | Why It Helps (6 rows).
- Performance Tuning table: Setting | Impact (6 rows).
- Troubleshooting table: Problem | Cause | Solution (9 rows).
- Related Skills tables: Technique Skills | Use Case; Related Fuzzers | When to Consider.
ANTI-PATTERNS:
- Adding `exit()` in harness → let libFuzzer keep the process alive; return 0.
- Leaving threads running or relying on cross-run state → join threads and reset global state.
- Mixing unrelated formats in one harness → narrow, focused targets.
- Running default behavior after first crash → add `-fork=1 -ignore_crashes=1`.
- Huge `-max_len` / excessive logging → set reasonable `-max_len` and `-close_fd_mask=3`.
- Fuzzing without ASan and then wondering why memory bugs are missed → recompile with `-fsanitize=address`.
- Using GCC-specific code with Clang → switch to AFL++ with `gcc_plugin`.
TOOLING:
- `clang++ -fsanitize=fuzzer -g -O2 harness.cc target.cc -o fuzz`; `-DNO_MAIN` when target has `main`.
- Static lib: `export CC=clang CFLAGS="-fsanitize=fuzzer-no-link -fsanitize=address"`, `./configure --enable-shared=no`, `make`, then link `libmylib.a`.
- CMake: `target_compile_options(fuzz PRIVATE -g -O2 -fsanitize=fuzzer -fsanitize=address)`, `cmake -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++ .`.
- Instances: `./fuzz -help=1`, `-print_final_stats=1`, `-runs=0`, `-merge=1`.
- Coverage: `clang++ -fprofile-instr-generate -fcoverage-mapping`, `LLVM_PROFILE_FILE="coverage-%p.profraw"`, `llvm-profdata merge -sparse coverage-*.profraw -o coverage.profdata`, `llvm-cov show ./fuzz -instr-profile=coverage.profdata [-format=html]`.
- libpng example: `curl -L -O .../libpng-1.6.37.tar.xz`, `apt install zlib1g-dev`, fetch `libpng_read_fuzzer.cc`, `png.dict`.
GOTCHAS:
- libFuzzer is in "maintenance-only mode since late 2022" but remains recommended for ease.
- ASan costs "2-4x slowdown" and needs ~20TB virtual memory; memory limits must be disabled (`-rss_limit_mb=0`).
- `_FORTIFY_SOURCE` causes false positives with ASan — use `-U_FORTIFY_SOURCE`.
- MSan requires rebuilding all dependencies with `-fsanitize=memory`.
- Dictionary entries longer than `-max_len` are ignored; `-seed` reproducibility is single-core only.
- Non-determinism (RNG, global state) makes crashes irreproducible.
- If crashes appear but ASan does not trigger, memory error detection was not compiled in.
- Slow executions/sec (<100) traced to complex targets or excessive logging.
STRUCTURE:
- none bundled; cross-references technique skills `fuzz-harness-writing`, `address-sanitizer`, `undefined-behavior-sanitizer`, `coverage-analysis`, `fuzzing-corpus`, `fuzzing-dictionaries`, `aflpp`, `honggfuzz`, `libafl` (declared, not bundled).

## S061 · ossfuzz
SOURCE: https://google.github.io/oss-fuzz/, https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz, bug tracker https://issues.oss-fuzz.com, https://github.com/ossf/fuzz-introspector/blob/main/doc/CaseStudies.md, https://github.com/ossf/criticality_score
PURPOSE: Enrol an open-source project in OSS-Fuzz (project.yaml + Dockerfile + build.sh), run its harnesses locally through `infra/helper.py`, and reproduce OSS-Fuzz crash reports.
CONCEPTS:
- **helper.py** — The local workflow is one script, so building and running a harness never requires hosting the platform. > "CLI script for building images, building fuzzers, and running harnesses locally"
- **base image hierarchy** — Build images stack in a fixed order, and each project image inherits from the builder tier rather than starting from Ubuntu. > "Images build on each other in this sequence:"
- **runner images** — Execution happens in a separate image family from building, which is why a working build and a working run are distinct results. > "Executes harnesses; based on `base_clang`"
- **project.yaml** — Enrolment metadata is declarative and is read by the service to pick engines and sanitizers. > "Configuration file defining project metadata for OSS-Fuzz enrollment"
- **Dockerfile** — Dependencies belong in the image definition, and approval for enrolment can depend on them being declared there. > "Add `apt-get install` or equivalent in Dockerfile"
- **build.sh** — Harness compilation is a script with a fixed contract: build the project, then link each harness into `$OUT`. > "Script that builds fuzzing harnesses for your project"
- **criticality score** — Acceptance is a scored decision, not a first-come queue, and a low score does not mean the work is impossible. > "Metric used by OSS-Fuzz team to evaluate project acceptance"
- **bug tracker** — Reports are cross-project searchable, so a new finding can be compared against every other enrolled project. > "Search for similar bugs across **all projects** to understand issues"
- **build status system** — The dashboard exists because a silently broken build stops fuzzing without stopping the badge. > "Date of last successful build"
- **Fuzz Introspector** — Coverage, hit frequency and blockers are presented per project to explain why a target is not being reached. > "Hit frequency for covered code"
- **sanitizer matrix** — Sanitizer choice is a build flag, with ASan paired with LeakSanitizer and language support varying. > "`--sanitizer=address` for [AddressSanitizer](https://appsec.guide/docs/fuzzing/techniques/asan/) with [LeakSanitizer](https://github.com/google/sanitizers/wiki/AddressSanitizerLeakSanitizer)"
- **coverage mode** — Coverage is a different build than fuzzing, and the corpus source can be restricted to local data. > "Use `--no-corpus-download` to use only local corpus."
- **fuzzing engines** — Engine choice is per-project configuration, with C/C++ defaulting to libFuzzer and other languages mapped to their own harness tooling. > "OSS-Fuzz primarily uses libFuzzer as the fuzzing engine for C/C++ projects."
- **Python C-extension fuzzing** — Atheris instruments the extension under test and the build script compiles each discovered fuzzer entry point. > "Use `compile_python_fuzzer` helper provided by OSS-Fuzz"
- **$LIB_FUZZING_ENGINE** — Link flags and sanitizer choice come from the environment, so the project build script does not hardcode them. > "Use `$LIB_FUZZING_ENGINE` variable provided by OSS-Fuzz"
- **seed corpus/dictionary output convention** — Supporting inputs are not passed by path but published into `$OUT` under harness-derived names. > "cp $SRC/yourproject/fuzz/corpus.zip $OUT/harness_seed_corpus.zip"
- **self-hosting** — The same infrastructure can be run privately, which removes the criticality threshold as a hard blocker. > "the project's core is open-source, allowing anyone to host their own instance for private projects."
RULES:
- Enrolment artefacts are exactly three files under `projects/<your-project>/`: `project.yaml`, `Dockerfile`, `build.sh` — > "Create three files in `projects/<your-project>/`"
- Never pull source in `build.sh`; let the Dockerfile clone it — > "Manually pulling source in build.sh | Doesn't use latest version | Let Dockerfile handle git clone"
- Keep harnesses in a separate repository from the main project — > "Keep harnesses in separate repo"
- Pin to the provided base images and compilers rather than choosing your own versions — > "Ignoring base image versions | Build inconsistencies | Use provided base images and compilers"
- Declare build dependencies in the Dockerfile, never by hand in the build script — > "**Install dependencies in Dockerfile** | May require approval for OSS-Fuzz enrollment"
- Test the build locally through helper.py before opening an enrolment PR — > "Skipping local testing | Wastes CI resources | Use helper.py locally before PR"
- Monitor the build status page, because a failing build stops fuzzing silently — > "Not checking build status | Unnoticed build failures | Monitor build status page regularly"
- Never copy project code into the OSS-Fuzz repository — > "Copying code to OSS-Fuzz repo | Hard to maintain, violates separation | Reference external harness repo"
- Rust projects list only `address` under sanitizers — > "Only AddressSanitizer supported for Rust"
- An Atheris build.sh installs the package, then compiles every fuzzer found under `$SRC` — > "for fuzzer in $(find $SRC -name 'fuzz_*.py'); do"
WORKFLOW:
1. `git clone https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz`; `cd oss-fuzz`; `uv run --no-project python infra/helper.py --help`.
2. `uv run --no-project python infra/helper.py build_image --pull <project-name>`.
3. `uv run --no-project python infra/helper.py build_fuzzers --sanitizer=address <project-name>` (output in `/build/out/<project-name>/`).
4. `uv run --no-project python infra/helper.py run_fuzzer <project-name> <harness-name> [<fuzzer-args>]`.
5. Optional coverage: install gsutil, `build_fuzzers --sanitizer=coverage`, `coverage <project-name>`; add `--no-corpus-download` for local corpus only.
6. Enrolment: add `project.yaml`, `Dockerfile`, `build.sh` under `projects/<your-project>/`, test locally before PR.
TABLES:
- Key Concepts table: Concept | Description (6 rows: helper.py, Base Images, project.yaml, Dockerfile, build.sh, Criticality Score).
- Quick Reference table: Task | Command (6 rows).
- Anti-Patterns table: Anti-Pattern | Problem | Correct Approach (5 rows).
- Troubleshooting table: Issue | Cause | Solution (6 rows).
- Tools That Use This Technique table: Skill | How It Applies (libfuzzer, aflpp, atheris, cargo-fuzz).
- Related Techniques table: Skill | Relationship (coverage-analysis, address-sanitizer, fuzz-harness-writing, corpus-management).
- Image hierarchy as a numbered dependency list, with runner images as a separate list.
ANTI-PATTERNS:
- Manually pulling source in build.sh → let the Dockerfile handle `git clone`.
- Copying source into the OSS-Fuzz repo → reference an external harness repo.
- Ignoring base image versions → pin to provided base images/compilers.
- Skipping local testing → run helper.py locally before opening a PR.
- Not checking build status → monitor the build status page.
TOOLING:
- `uv run --no-project python infra/helper.py build_image|build_fuzzers|run_fuzzer|coverage`.
- Docker invocation seen in output: `docker run --rm --privileged --shm-size=2g --platform linux/amd64 -e FUZZING_ENGINE=libfuzzer -e SANITIZER=address -e RUN_FUZZER_MODE=interactive -e HELPER=True -v .../build/out/irssi:/out -t gcr.io/oss-fuzz-base/base-runner run_fuzzer irssi-fuzz`.
- Runtime flags surfaced: `-rss_limit_mb=2560 -timeout=25 -max_len=2048`.
- `FROM gcr.io/oss-fuzz-base/base-builder`; env vars `$SRC`, `$OUT`, `$CXX`, `$CXXFLAGS`, `$LIB_FUZZING_ENGINE`.
- build.sh header `#!/bin/bash -eu`; Rust `cargo fuzz build -O --debug-assertions` + copy from `fuzz/target/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/release/`.
- project.yaml keys: `homepage`, `language`, `primary_contact`, `main_repo`, `fuzzing_engines`, `sanitizers`.
GOTCHAS:
- Enrolment is gated: "only select projects are accepted"; criticality score threshold applies.
- Skipped helper steps are auto-run by the script, which can mask a broken step sequence.
- Coverage of 0% usually means the harness never calls the target, not a reporting bug.
- Build timeouts from complex build processes; missing WORKDIR causes "Cannot find source code".
- Incompatible sanitizer flags cause build errors — use OSS-Fuzz environment variables.
- Rust sanitizer support limited to AddressSanitizer.
- Harnesses crashing immediately usually lack input size validation.
- `allow-legacy-python` note: build.sh runs inside the container "where the shims are absent".
STRUCTURE:
- `projects/<your-project>/project.yaml`, `Dockerfile`, `build.sh` referenced as required enrolment artefacts (external to this skill); no local `references/` declared.

## S062 · dx-devops-test-suite-assignments-configure
SOURCE: none (Salesforce DevOps Center Connect API `testSuiteStages`, API v67.0; no URLs)
PURPOSE: Recommend which existing test suites cover a commit diff and manage suite-to-stage assignments (assign one, bulk-map many, add/remove test classes) through the org-resident `testSuiteStages` Connect API with mandatory confirmation gates.
CONCEPTS:
- **Mode A — Recommend suites** — Diff analysis is a read-only reasoning mode, so it can run before any stage or write decision exists. > "Mode A is pure reasoning (no writes)."
- **Mode B — Assign a single suite** — The narrowest mutation covers the case where one suite is simply not linked to a stage. > "Assign **one** suite to a stage as a one-off"
- **Mode C — Map multiple suites** — Bulk mapping is treated as a testing strategy decision, which is why it earns a preview table before confirmation. > "a **mandatory impact-preview table** (Suite / Stage / Event / Action) before the confirmation gate"
- **Mode D — Add/remove classes** — Class-level editing inside an assignment carries the tightest governance because it changes what a stage will execute. > "**Add/remove** individual test classes within a suite assignment"
- **diff classification** — Changed files are categorised before any suite can be matched to them, so the recommendation has stated grounds. > "Mode A analyzes a commit diff against assigned suite metadata to recommend relevant existing suites and flag coverage gaps (pure reasoning)"
- **provider matching** — A diff artefact is matched against the provider that tests it, which is also the step that fails when the provider is not registered. > "if the suite you want to assign doesn't appear yet, configure or re-sync the provider"
- **ranking** — Candidate suites are ordered rather than listed, so the user gets a priority order instead of a set. > "diff classification, provider matching, ranking, gap flagging, output format"
- **gap flagging** — A relevant-but-unassigned suite is the bridge between recommendation and assignment; the gap is the handoff input. > "that gap is the input to Mode B/C"
- **prerequisite gate set** — Four fixed checks plus one mode-dependent check run before any call, and failure ends the flow rather than degrading it. > "Run the prerequisite checks in `references/prerequisite-checks.md` before any query or system call."
- **pipeline-level Review trigger** — Recommendation reads a trigger at the pipeline level, which is why no stage is required for Mode A. > "No stage required — recommendation reads the pipeline-level Review trigger."
- **governance confirmation** — Every mutating mode stops for explicit affirmative approval; there is no default-yes path. > "Modes B–D **must** confirm before any write"
- **impact-preview table** — The preview names the four things the change touches so the approver sees the diff before it exists. > "Suite / Stage / Event / Action"
- **payload exclusion** — Tests the user rejected are removed from the request body, not merely annotated. > "**Rejected tests must be EXCLUDED from the payload.**"
- **org-not-repo data locality** — Suite configuration is org state, so filesystem searching is a category error rather than a slow path. > "All DevOps Center data lives in the Salesforce org — NOT the local repo."
- **error translation** — API failures are converted through status-code tables so the user never sees transport-level output. > "Never expose raw API errors, stack traces, or JSON to the user."
- **v1 constraint** — An uncovered method ends the automated flow and returns authorship to the developer, which deliberately stops short of generation. > "direct the developer to author tests manually (v1 constraint — never suggest generating tests here)"
- **handoff skills** — Recommendation hands to running rather than duplicating execution. > "execute a recommended/assigned suite on a stage"
RULES:
- Every system call targets Salesforce API v67.0 or newer — > "All DevOps testing system calls target Salesforce API **v67.0** (minimum required)."
- Never look for suite configuration on disk; it only exists in the org — > "All DevOps Center data lives in the Salesforce org — NOT the local repo. Never search the filesystem for suite configuration."
- Query the org with `sf data query` or `sf api request rest` — > "Always query the org with `sf data query` or `sf api request rest`."
- Run prerequisites before any query and stop on the first failure — > "On any failure, surface the plain-language message and stop."
- Modes B–D additionally require the stage prerequisite and the three identifiers `doce-org-alias`, `pipelineId`, `stageId` — > "You need `doce-org-alias`, `pipelineId`, and `stageId`."
- No mutating call happens without explicit approval — > "Do not call the API until the user gives an affirmative response."
- Mode C shows the mandatory impact-preview table before its confirmation gate — > "Mode C — a **mandatory impact-preview table** (Suite / Stage / Event / Action) before the confirmation gate"
- Mode D excludes rejected tests and re-presents the final list if tests changed during review — > "Never call without explicit approval."
- A declined confirmation ends the flow with nothing written — > "If the user declines, stop without writing."
- Mode A requires no confirmation gate because it writes nothing — > "Mode A (recommendation) makes no writes and needs no confirmation gate."
- Surface translated messages only, never raw API errors, stack traces or JSON — > "Never expose raw API errors, stack traces, or JSON to the user."
- Declare `minApiVersion: "67.0"` and require `sf` CLI `>=2.67.0` — > "minApiVersion: "67.0""
WORKFLOW:
1. Run prerequisites from `references/prerequisite-checks.md` (1–4, plus 5 for B–D); stop on failure with the plain-language message.
2. Select the mode via the routing table (A recommend / B assign single / C map multiple / D add-remove classes).
3. Governance & confirmation (B–D only): Mode B single prompt naming suite/stage/event; Mode C impact-preview table then gate; Mode D re-present final test list.
4. Execute and report per reference: `recommendation-logic.md` (A), `suite-assignment-modes.md` (B–D), `api-endpoint.md` (payload schema), `error-handling.md` (status codes).
TABLES:
- Mode selection table: "If the user wants to… | Mode | Follow" (4 rows: A recommend, B assign one, C bulk-map, D add/remove classes).
- Impact-preview table (Mode C): columns Suite / Stage / Event / Action.
- Status-code → plain-language tables in `references/error-handling.md` (declared).
ANTI-PATTERNS:
- Searching the local filesystem for suite configuration → query the org (`sf data query`, `sf api request rest`).
- Calling the mutating API before confirmation → gate first; stop silently on decline.
- Including rejected tests in a Mode D payload → exclude them.
- Exposing raw API errors/stack traces/JSON → translate via error-handling tables.
- Suggesting test generation for uncovered methods → v1 forbids it; direct the developer to author tests.
- Skipping the impact preview in Mode C → mandatory before confirmation.
TOOLING:
- `sf data query`, `sf api request rest` (org access).
- Connect API `testSuiteStages` endpoint via `references/api-endpoint.md` POST payload schema (Modes B–D).
- Frontmatter keys: `name`, `description`, `metadata.version: "1.0"`, `metadata.domains: ["Developer Experience"]`, `metadata.minApiVersion: "67.0"`, `metadata.relatedSkills`, `metadata.cliTools` (`tool: ["sf"]`, `semver: ">=2.67.0"`).
- Required identifiers: `doce-org-alias`, `pipelineId`, `stageId`.
GOTCHAS:
- Recommendation without a stage only works because it reads the pipeline-level Review trigger; B–D silently need stage context.
- A gap flagged in Mode A must route either to assignment (B/C) or manual authoring — never auto-generation.
- Declining mid-flow must not leave partial writes; stop without writing.
- Frontmatter description is long enough to be truncated by some readers; part after "add/remove/sy…" carries the DO NOT TRIGGER routing.
STRUCTURE:
- `references/prerequisite-checks.md`, `references/recommendation-logic.md`, `references/suite-assignment-modes.md`, `references/api-endpoint.md`, `references/error-handling.md` — all declared, not bundled.

## S063 · dx-devops-test-suite-run
SOURCE: none (Salesforce DevOps Center Connect API execute endpoint, API v67.0; no URLs)
PURPOSE: Trigger a DevOps Center test-suite execution on a pipeline stage after a confirmation gate, poll the `runId` to completion, surface results, and retrigger a quality gate only when coverage meets threshold.
CONCEPTS:
- **execution trigger endpoint** — Execution is one REST POST addressed by pipeline and stage, with the suite list in the body. > "/services/data/v67.0/connect/devopstesting/pipeline/<pipelineId>/stage/execute"
- **event model** — The stage hook being exercised is a closed set of three events, confirmed with the user before the call. > "`event` | string | `Pre-Promote`, `Post-Promote`, or `Review`"
- **runId** — The identifier returned belongs to the suite-execution object, and picking the wrong object breaks polling entirely. > "the `runId` is a `DevopsTestSuiteExecution` Id — poll that object, not `DevopsTestExecution`"
