## S114 · libafl
SOURCE: AFLplusplus/LibAFL (github), LibAFL Book `aflplus.plus/libafl-book/`, docs.rs `libafl`, Trail of Bits testing-handbook materials.
PURPOSE: Tells an agent how to use LibAFL either as a libFuzzer drop-in or as a Rust library to assemble a bespoke fuzzer from observers, feedback, objectives, state, mutators, schedulers and executors.
CONCEPTS:
- **Two usage modes** — LibAFL serves either as a drop-in libFuzzer replacement for existing harnesses or as a library for building a fuzzer from scratch. > "It can be used as a drop-in replacement for libFuzzer or as a library to build custom fuzzers from scratch."
- **`libafl_libfuzzer_runtime` + `build.sh` → `libFuzzer.a`** — a script in the runtime directory builds the compatibility layer the drop-in mode links against. > "Build LibAFL's libFuzzer compatibility layer:"
- **Seven fuzzer components** — a custom fuzzer is assembled from observers, feedback, objective, state, mutators, scheduler and executor. > "A LibAFL fuzzer consists of modular components:"
- **`HitcountsMapObserver` / `std_edges_map_observer`** — edge coverage is collected by an observer built from the target's shared edges map. > "**Observers** - Collect execution feedback (coverage, timing)"
- **`TimeObserver` + `TimeFeedback`** — a second observer records execution time, and its feedback makes timing part of interestingness. > "let time_observer = TimeObserver::new("time");"
- **`feedback_or!` / `feedback_or_fast!` / `feedback_and!`** — macros compose several feedbacks into one interestingness decision and several objectives into one crash criterion. > "// 3. Define objective"
- **`StdState` with `StdRand`, `InMemoryCorpus`, `OnDiskCorpus`** — state is created or restored with a random source and both in-memory and on-disk corpus backends. > "// 4. Create or restore state"
- **`StdScheduledMutator` + `havoc_mutations()` + `StdMutationalStage`** — the mutation stage wraps a scheduled havoc mutator. > "let mutator = StdScheduledMutator::new(havoc_mutations());"
- **`IndexesLenTimeMinimizerScheduler` over `QueueScheduler`** — the scheduler is a minimizer that ranks queue entries by index, length and time. > "// 6. Setup scheduler"
- **`InProcessExecutor::with_timeout` + `RestartingMgr`** — the in-process executor runs the harness under a timeout with a restarting manager. > "let mut executor = InProcessExecutor::with_timeout("
- **`Launcher` with `cores()`** — the launcher spawns one client per core; `--cores 0,8-15` produces 9 clients. > "This runs 9 clients: one on core 0, and 8 on cores 8-15."
- **libafl_cc compiler wrapper** — `ClangWrapper` is extended to add the coverage map and AddressSanitizer flags, so instrumentation is not spelled out by hand. > "Create a LibAFL compiler wrapper to handle instrumentation automatically."
- **Backtrace-based crash deduplication** — a `BacktraceObserver` feeds `NewHashFeedback`, so only crashes with unique backtraces are stored. > "This ensures only crashes with unique backtraces are saved."
- **Dictionary fuzzing** — tokens are loaded with `Tokens::add_from_file` and merged into the mutator as `tokens_mutations()`. > "Use dictionaries to guide fuzzing toward specific tokens:"
- **Auto tokens** — the `LLVMPasses::AutoTokens` compiler pass extracts magic values and checksums, and `libafl_targets::autotokens()` loads them. > "Automatically extract magic values and checksums from the program:"
- **Verbose manual instrumentation** — the alternative to the wrapper specifies `-fsanitize-coverage=trace-pc-guard` and whole-archive linking by hand. > "Manually specify all instrumentation flags:"
- **Debug mode** — calling `run_client` directly skips the launcher so the fuzzer runs single-process and GDB can attach. > "Run fuzzer in single-process mode for easier debugging:"
- **Worked examples** — the skill ships a libpng end-to-end walkthrough and a CMake integration. > "Fuzzing libpng using LibAFL:"
RULES:
- Install Clang/LLVM 15-18 plus Rust via rustup first — > "LibAFL requires LLVM 15-18"
- Pin the dependencies at 0.13 with the libfuzzer and sancov_pcguard_hitcounts features — > "cargo add libafl@0.13 libafl_targets@0.13 libafl_bolts@0.13 libafl_cc@0.13 \"
- The custom-fuzzer crate is a staticlib — > "crate-type = ["staticlib"]"
- For libFuzzer compatibility mode, install nightly Rust with the `llvm-tools` component — > "For libFuzzer compatibility mode, install nightly Rust:"
- The harness keeps the `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` signature and returns 0 — > "extern "C" int LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput(const uint8_t *data, size_t size) {"
- For long campaigns run with `-fork=1 -ignore_crashes=1` — > "| Use `-fork=1 -ignore_crashes=1` | Continue fuzzing after first crash |"
- Compose the objective with `feedback_and!` over crash/timeout and `NewHashFeedback` for dedup — > "let mut objective = feedback_and!("
- Unset `CC`, `CXX` and `RUSTFLAGS` after building the LibAFL project — > "| Environment variable interference | `CC`, `CXX`, `RUSTFLAGS` set | Unset after building LibAFL project |"
WORKFLOW:
1. Install clang (15-18), set `RUSTFLAGS="-C linker=/usr/bin/clang-15"`, `CC=clang-15`, `CXX=clang++-15`; `apt install libssl-dev pkg-config`.
2. Verify: `cd LibAFL/libafl_libfuzzer_runtime && ./build.sh` → `libFuzzer.a`.
3. Drop-in: `clang++ -DNO_MAIN -g -O2 -fsanitize=fuzzer-no-link libFuzzer.a harness.cc main.cc -o fuzz`; run `./fuzz corpus/`.
4. Custom: `cargo init --lib my_fuzzer`, `cargo add …`, edit `Cargo.toml`.
5. Write `libafl_main` with observers → feedback → objective → state → mutator/stages → scheduler → `StdFuzzer` → harness → executor → `load_initial_inputs` → `fuzz_loop`, wrapped in `Launcher::builder().run_client(&mut run_client).cores(&cores).build().launch()`.
6. Optionally build the `libafl_cc`/`libafl_cxx` wrapper and use it as `CC`/`CXX`.
7. Run `./fuzz --cores 0,8-15 --input corpus/ --output crashes/ --timeout 1000`, optional `-tui=1`.
TABLES: "When to Use" (libFuzzer/AFL++/LibAFL × Best For/Complexity); Interpreting Output (6 × Output/Meaning); Tips and Tricks (5 × Tip/Why); Performance Tuning (5 × Setting/Impact); Troubleshooting (8 × Problem/Cause/Solution); Related Skills / Related Fuzzers.
ANTI-PATTERNS: instrumenting without the compiler wrapper → check for `-fsanitize-coverage` when "No coverage increases"; empty corpus → seed inputs that trigger code paths; duplicate crashes from one bug → add `BacktraceObserver` + `NewHashFeedback`; debugging a multi-process campaign → switch to single-process mode.
TOOLING: `./build.sh`, `libFuzzer.a`, `cargo add libafl@0.13 …`, `-fsanitize=fuzzer-no-link`, `-fsanitize-coverage=trace-pc-guard`, `-Wl,--whole-archive ... -Wl,--no-whole-archive` or `-u libafl_main`, `--cores 0-7`, `--input`, `--output`, `--timeout 1000`, `-tui=1`, `-x png.dict`, `gdb --args ./fuzz`.
GOTCHAS: LLVM version mismatch breaks the build; missing `libafl_main` link is fixed by whole-archive/`-u`; sanitizers cost "2-5x slowdown"; environment variable interference after building; auto-token section can be verified with `echo "p (uint8_t *)__token_start" | gdb fuzz`.
STRUCTURE: none (sibling technique skills declared, not bundled).

## S116 · ruzzy
SOURCE: github.com/trailofbits/ruzzy, Trail of Bits blog "Introducing Ruzzy" (2024-03-29), llvm.org libFuzzer docs.
PURPOSE: Tells an agent how to install, harness and run Ruzzy — Trail of Bits' coverage-guided Ruby fuzzer — for pure Ruby code and for gem C extensions, with ASan/UBSan.
CONCEPTS:
- **Coverage-guided Ruby fuzzing built on libFuzzer** — Ruzzy supplies coverage guidance for Ruby by wrapping libFuzzer, and the author asserts it is the only production-ready option for the language. > "Ruzzy is currently the only production-ready coverage-guided fuzzer for Ruby."
- **Platform scope** — fuzzing runs natively on Linux x86-64 and AArch64/ARM64; macOS and Windows go through a Dockerfile or development environment. > "Ruzzy supports Linux x86-64 and AArch64/ARM64."
- **Compiler pinning via gem env** — `MAKE`, `CC`, `CXX`, `LDSHARED` and `LDSHAREDXX` are overridden at install time so the gem and its extensions build with the intended clang. > "Ensure proper clang binaries are used for latest features"
- **Tracer pattern** — pure Ruby needs two files: a tracer that calls `Ruzzy.trace('test_harness.rb')` and the harness it traces. > "Pure Ruby fuzzing requires two scripts due to Ruby interpreter implementation details."
- **Single-file harness for C extensions** — an extension harness needs no tracer, only the `Ruzzy.fuzz(test_one_input)` loop. > "C extensions can be fuzzed with a single harness file, no tracer needed."
- **`test_one_input` lambda** — the lambda wraps the target call and returns 0 to libFuzzer. > "Return 0 from test_one_input lambda"
- **Exception swallowing** — the extension harness rescues `Exception`, so Ruby-level errors do not abort the campaign while memory corruption still crashes it. > "We're looking for memory corruption, not Ruby exceptions"
- **Sanitizer injection via `LD_PRELOAD`** — `Ruzzy::ASAN_PATH` is expanded inline into the ruby command to preload the sanitizer. > "`LD_PRELOAD` is required for sanitizer injection."
- **`Ruzzy::UBSAN_PATH`** — the same preload mechanism loads a bundled UBSan build for undefined behaviour. > "LD_PRELOAD=$(ruby -e 'require "ruzzy"; print Ruzzy::UBSAN_PATH') \"
- **ASAN_OPTIONS triplet** — three options are exported before any campaign: `allocator_may_return_null=1`, `detect_leaks=0`, `use_sigaltstack=0`. > "Before running any fuzzing campaign, set ASAN_OPTIONS:"
- **Sanitizer-flagged gem builds** — gems with C extensions are installed with `CFLAGS`/`CXXFLAGS` containing `-fsanitize=address,fuzzer-no-link`. > "When installing Ruby gems with C extensions for fuzzing, compile with sanitizer flags:"
- **libFuzzer option pass-through** — arguments after the corpus path go straight to libFuzzer, e.g. `-max_len=1024 -timeout=10`. > "All libFuzzer options can be passed as arguments:"
- **Crash reproduction by filename** — passing the `crash-…` file path to the harness replays the input; output also prints a `Base64:` line for transport. > "Re-run a crash case by passing the crash file:"
- **`Ruzzy.dummy` toy example** — the bundled dummy target doubles as an installation self-test. > "This should quickly find a crash demonstrating that Ruzzy is working correctly."
- **Output interpretation table** — the campaign output is read through the entropic power schedule line, ASan error lines, the SUMMARY line and the artifact prefix. > "| `INFO: Running with entropic power schedule` | Fuzzing campaign started |"
RULES:
- Export `ASAN_OPTIONS="allocator_may_return_null=1:detect_leaks=0:use_sigaltstack=0"` before a campaign — > "Before running any fuzzing campaign, set ASAN_OPTIONS:"
- Do not export `LD_PRELOAD`; set it inline on the ruby command — > "Unlike `ASAN_OPTIONS`, do not export it as it may interfere with other programs."
- Clang is tested back to 14.0.0, with the latest release recommended — > "tested back to 14.0.0, latest release recommended"
- Pure Ruby needs the tracer script; the harness returns 0 and stays deterministic — > "| Use tracer script for pure Ruby | Skip tracer for pure Ruby code |"
- Install with `MAKE="make --environment-overrides V=1"` so the other overrides apply — > "Overrides make to respect subsequent environment variables"
- Debug a failing install with `RUZZY_DEBUG=1 gem install --verbose` — > "If installation fails, enable debug output:"
WORKFLOW:
1. Set `ASAN_OPTIONS`.
2. Verify with `LD_PRELOAD=… ruby -e 'require "ruzzy"; Ruzzy.dummy'` — should "quickly find a crash".
3. Install: `gem install ruzzy` with the five env overrides.
4. Write harness (`Ruzzy.fuzz(test_one_input)`); add `Ruzzy.trace(...)` tracer for pure Ruby.
5. Run `LD_PRELOAD=$(…) ruby test_tracer.rb` (or `fuzz_msgpack.rb`), optionally passing a corpus dir and libFuzzer flags.
6. Reproduce crashes by passing the crash file path.
TABLES: Harness Rules (Do/Don't, 4 rows); Build Flags (5 × Flag/Purpose); Interpreting Output (5 × Output/Meaning); Common Sanitizer Issues (4 × Issue/Solution); Troubleshooting (6 × Problem/Cause/Solution); Related Skills / Related Fuzzers.
ANTI-PATTERNS: exporting `LD_PRELOAD` → set inline; letting Ruby exceptions abort the fuzzer when fuzzing C extensions → rescue them; skipping the tracer for pure Ruby → "No coverage progress"; fuzzing on macOS/Windows natively → use the Dockerfile or dev environment.
TOOLING: `gem install ruzzy`, `Ruzzy.trace`, `Ruzzy.fuzz`, `Ruzzy.dummy`, `Ruzzy::ASAN_PATH`, `Ruzzy::UBSAN_PATH`, `-fsanitize=address,fuzzer-no-link -fno-omit-frame-pointer -fno-common -fPIC -g`, `-max_len=1024 -timeout=10`, `RUZZY_DEBUG=1`.
GOTCHAS: "cannot open shared object file" means `LD_PRELOAD` was not set; "Fuzzer immediately exits" means missing corpus directory; Ruby interpreter leaks produce leak-detection spam; sigaltstack conflicts need `use_sigaltstack=0`; allocation-failure spam needs `allocator_may_return_null=1`.
STRUCTURE: none (sibling technique skills declared, not bundled).

## S118 · bats-testing-patterns
SOURCE: none.
PURPOSE: Tells an agent how to write and run Bats unit tests for shell scripts — error paths, dependency skips, dialect compatibility, parallelism, helpers and CI wiring.
CONCEPTS:
- **Bats test file structure** — tests are Bats files starting with `#!/usr/bin/env bats` and declaring cases as `@test` blocks, named by behaviour. > "Comprehensive guidance for writing comprehensive unit tests for shell scripts using Bats"
- **`run` helper** — every case wraps the call in `run` and asserts on the captured `$status` and `$output`. > "[[ "$output" == *"not found"* ]]"
- **Error-path testing** — cases cover a missing file, invalid input, permission denied and a helpful usage message. > "@test "Function fails with missing file" {"
- **Ad-hoc skip pattern** — a dependency is probed with `command -v` and the case calls `skip` when it is absent. > "if ! command -v jq &>/dev/null; then"
- **`BATS_TEST_DIRNAME`** — the script under test is located relative to the test file, so tests run from any working directory. > "export SCRIPT="${BATS_TEST_DIRNAME}/../bin/script.sh""
- **Dialect matrix** — the same case is run under bash, `sh` (POSIX) and `dash`, skipping the dialect when it is not installed. > "@test "Script works in dash" {"
- **Parallel execution patterns** — independent operations are backgrounded with `&` and collected with `wait`, then asserted on their effects. > "@test "Concurrent file operations" {"
- **`test_helper.sh`** — a sourced helper supplies assertion functions and temp-directory setup/cleanup. > "Common test utilities"
- **`mktemp -d` temp directory lifecycle** — `setup_test_dir` creates `TEST_DIR` with `mktemp -d` and `cleanup_test_dir` removes it. > "export TEST_DIR=$(mktemp -d)"
- **CI integration** — a GitHub Actions job checks out, installs Bats via npm, then runs the suite. > "npm install --global bats"
- **TAP output** — the suite can emit TAP through `--tap`, teed to `test_output.tap`. > "bats tests/*.bats --tap | tee test_output.tap"
- **Makefile targets** — `test`, `test-verbose`, `test-tap`, `test-parallel` and `coverage` wrap the invocations. > "bats tests/*.bats --parallel 4"
- **Progressive disclosure** — full pattern documentation is deferred to a reference file. > "Detailed pattern documentation lives in `references/details.md`."
RULES:
- Test one thing per test — > "**Test one thing per test** - Single responsibility principle"
- Use descriptive test names — > "**Use descriptive test names** - Clearly states what is being tested"
- Clean up after tests, including temporary files — > "**Clean up after tests** - Always remove temporary files in teardown"
- Test both success and failure paths — > "**Test both success and failure paths** - Don't just test happy path"
- Mock external dependencies — > "**Mock external dependencies** - Isolate unit under test"
- Use fixtures for complex data — > "**Use fixtures for complex data** - Makes tests more readable"
- Keep tests fast, running them in parallel when possible — > "**Keep tests fast** - Run in parallel when possible"
- Restore permissions after a `chmod 000` case (`chmod 644 "$TMPDIR/readonly.txt"`) — > "chmod 644 "$TMPDIR/readonly.txt"  # Cleanup"
- Assert zero status on success (`[ "$status" -eq 0 ]`) and non-zero on failure (`[ "$status" -ne 0 ]`) — > "[ "$status" -ne 0 ]"
WORKFLOW:
1. Read `references/details.md` when the navigation tier is insufficient.
2. Create `tests/*.bats` with `@test` blocks using `run`.
3. Add `setup()` to check tools and export `SCRIPT` from `BATS_TEST_DIRNAME`.
4. Add `test_helper.sh` sourced for assertions and temp dirs.
5. Run locally: `bats tests/*.bats`, `--verbose`, `--tap`, `--parallel 4`.
6. Wire CI: checkout → `npm install --global bats` → `bats tests/*.bats` → TAP variant.
TABLES: none (Best Practices is a numbered list of 10 items, not a table).
ANTI-PATTERNS: only testing the happy path → add failure/error-path tests; leaving `chmod 000` files behind → restore permissions; hard-failing when a dependency is absent → `skip` instead; sequential slow suites → `--parallel 4` or background jobs.
TOOLING: `bats tests/*.bats --tap`, `--verbose`, `--parallel 4`, `.github/workflows` job using `actions/checkout@v3` and `npm install --global bats`, Makefile targets, `BATS_TEST_DIRNAME`, `mktemp -d`.
GOTCHAS: `dash` may be absent and needs a guard; `$output`/`$status` only exist after `run`; `skip` vs the non-standard `skip_if` helper (the example uses `skip_if` without defining it); permission tests need explicit restore; temp dirs leak without `teardown`.
STRUCTURE: `references/details.md` — "Detailed pattern documentation lives in `references/details.md`" (declared, not bundled).

## S119 · screen-reader-testing
SOURCE: none
PURPOSE: Tells an agent how to validate a web app with real screen readers (VoiceOver, NVDA, JAWS, TalkBack, Narrator), including setup reading, ARIA patterns to test, and debugging what assistive technology actually perceives.
CONCEPTS:
- **Major Screen Readers** — The file ranks five readers by platform, browser, and rough share, which is what justifies the coverage tiers below; the shares run VoiceOver ~15%, NVDA ~31%, JAWS ~40%, TalkBack ~10%, Narrator ~4%. > "Test web applications with screen readers including VoiceOver, NVDA, and JAWS."
- **Testing priority** — Coverage is split into a "Minimum Coverage" block of three reader/browser pairs and a "Comprehensive Coverage" block that adds three more, so a reviewer knows the floor and the ceiling. > "2. VoiceOver + Safari (macOS)"
- **Screen reader modes** — Browse/virtual mode reads content, focus/forms mode interacts with controls, application mode handles custom widgets, and testing must cross the modes because each gives a different experience. > "**Test in browse and focus modes** - Different experiences"
- **Modal dialog pattern** — The accessible modal carries `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby`, with comments marking the structure as accessible so the pattern is copied whole rather than partially. > "<!-- Accessible modal structure -->"
- **Focus trap** — Tab and Shift+Tab wrap by querying the focusable set and comparing `document.activeElement` against the first and last members, with `tabindex="-1"` excluded from the query. > "'button, [href], input, select, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])',"
- **Escape to close** — Dismissal is handled in the same keydown handler as the trap, so the mechanism that keeps focus in also lets the reader leave. > "if (e.key === "Escape") {"
- **Live regions** — Status uses `role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"` and `aria-atomic="true"` so updates wait for current speech; alerts use `role="alert"` with `aria-live="assertive"` so they interrupt. > "<div role="status" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true">"
- **Progress announcement** — A progress update is exposed as `role="progressbar"` carrying `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and a label. > "<!-- Progress updates -->"
- **Log region** — `role="log"` is paired with `aria-relevant="additions"` so new messages are announced while removals stay silent. > "<div role="log" aria-live="polite" aria-relevant="additions">"
- **Tab interface** — The tablist/tab/tabpanel trio uses `aria-selected`, `aria-controls`, `aria-labelledby`, and roving `tabindex="-1"` on the inactive tab. > "<div role="tablist" aria-label="Product information">"
- **Arrow/Home/End keyboard model** — Left and right move modularly over the tab array, Home jumps to index 0, End to the last index, and each move re-activates the tab. > "newIndex = (index + 1) % tabs.length;"
- **Accessible name computation** — A debug helper logs the name as `aria-label` falling back to `aria-labelledby` then `textContent`, so the agent sees the name the reader would compute rather than the DOM attribute it assumed. > "// Log what screen reader sees"
- **State inspection** — The same helper logs `aria-expanded`/`aria-selected`/`aria-checked`/`disabled` and derives visibility from computed `display` and `visibility`. > "visible: computed.display !== "none" && computed.visibility !== "hidden","
- **Progressive disclosure into references/** — Four reader-specific setup and command docs are declared and meant to be read before testing on that platform. > "Before testing with NVDA, read [NVDA setup, modes, commands, and test scripts](references/nvda.md)."
- **Semantic HTML first** — ARIA is framed as a supplement to native semantics, not a replacement for them. > "**Use semantic HTML first** - ARIA is supplemental"
- **Keyboard-only testing** — Keyboard-only navigation is the first step, described as the foundation the screen-reader pass is built on. > "**Test keyboard only first** - Foundation for SR testing"
- **Dynamic content testing** — Dynamic content is treated as a mandatory scenario class because it is where most issues appear. > "**Don't skip dynamic content** - Most common issues"
RULES:
- Minimum coverage is the three pairs NVDA + Firefox (Windows), VoiceOver + Safari (macOS), VoiceOver + Safari (iOS) — > "Minimum Coverage:"
- Comprehensive coverage adds JAWS + Chrome (Windows), TalkBack + Chrome (Android), Narrator + Edge (Windows) — > "+ Narrator + Edge (Windows)"
- Test with actual screen readers, not simulators — > "**Test with actual screen readers** - Not just simulators"
- Use semantic HTML first; ARIA is supplemental — > "**Use semantic HTML first** - ARIA is supplemental"
- Test in browse and focus modes — > "**Test in browse and focus modes** - Different experiences"
- Verify focus management, especially for SPAs — > "**Verify focus management** - Especially for SPAs"
- Test keyboard only first — > "**Test keyboard only first** - Foundation for SR testing"
- Don't assume one screen reader is enough; test multiple — > "**Don't assume one SR is enough** - Test multiple"
- Don't ignore mobile — > "**Don't ignore mobile** - Growing user base"
- Don't test only the happy path; cover error states — > "**Don't test only happy path** - Test error states"
- Don't skip dynamic content — > "**Don't skip dynamic content** - Most common issues"
- Don't rely on visual testing — > "**Don't rely on visual testing** - Different experience"
WORKFLOW: (1) Determine coverage tier from the priority block. (2) Read the matching reference doc before testing: `references/voiceover.md`, `references/voiceover-ios.md`, `references/nvda.md`, `references/jaws-talkback.md`. (3) Test keyboard-only first. (4) Reproduce each scenario (modal, live region, tab interface) in browse and focus modes. (5) Verify focus move/restore and trap boundaries. (6) Use the debugging helper to compare computed role/name/state against expectation.
TABLES: `Major Screen Readers` — rows = 5 readers; columns = Platform, Browser, Usage. `Testing Priority` — two blocks (Minimum Coverage 3 items, Comprehensive Coverage +3). `Screen Reader Modes` — rows = Browse/Virtual, Focus/Forms, Application; columns = Purpose, When Used.
ANTI-PATTERNS: "Don't assume one SR is enough" → test multiple. "Don't ignore mobile" → include iOS/Android. "Don't test only happy path" → test error states. "Don't skip dynamic content" → most common issues. "Don't rely on visual testing" → different experience. "Don't assume one SR is enough - Test multiple". Simulator-only testing → use actual screen readers.
TOOLING: HTML attributes: `role`, `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-live`, `aria-atomic`, `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-relevant`, `aria-selected`, `aria-controls`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-checked`, `tabindex="-1"`. JS: `document.activeElement`, `window.getComputedStyle`, `querySelectorAll('button, [href], input, select, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])')`. Reader pairs: NVDA+Firefox, VoiceOver+Safari, JAWS+Chrome, TalkBack+Chrome, Narrator+Edge.
GOTCHAS: Focusable query must exclude `tabindex="-1"` or the trap wraps to removed elements. Shift+Tab from first element and Tab from last must both `preventDefault()` or focus escapes to browser chrome. Hidden panels need `hidden` or they remain reachable. Log region removals are silent unless `aria-relevant` is set. Debug helper's `visible` check is derived from `display`/`visibility` only.
STRUCTURE: `references/voiceover.md` (declared, not bundled), `references/voiceover-ios.md` (declared, not bundled), `references/nvda.md` (declared, not bundled), `references/jaws-talkback.md` (declared, not bundled).

## S120 · swift-protocol-di-testing
SOURCE: none (`metadata: origin: ECC`)
PURPOSE: Instils a protocol-per-concern dependency injection pattern so Swift code touching file system, network, or iCloud boundaries can be tested deterministically with mocks instead of I/O.
CONCEPTS:
- **Focused protocol** — One protocol per external concern, so a test can substitute the single capability it needs: `FileSystemProviding`, `FileAccessorProviding`, `BookmarkStorageProviding` are each narrow. > "Each protocol handles exactly one external concern."
- **Sendable protocol requirement** — Every boundary protocol conforms to `Sendable`, because the injected value may cross an actor boundary. > "Sendable conformance**: Required when protocols are used across actor boundaries"
- **Default production implementation** — Small structs (`DefaultFileSystemProvider`, `DefaultFileAccessor`) wrap the real APIs — `FileManager`, `Data(contentsOf:)` — so production wiring stays a one-liner. > "public struct DefaultFileSystemProvider: FileSystemProviding {"
- **Mock implementation** — The mock is a `final class` backed by a `[URL: Data]` dictionary plus settable `readError`/`writeError`, so a fake file tree is just dictionary assignment. > "public final class MockFileAccessor: FileAccessorProviding, @unchecked Sendable {"
- **@unchecked Sendable on the mock** — The mock opts out of the compiler's Sendable check because its mutable storage is not statically safe; the file supplies no synchronization to make it true. > "public var files: [URL: Data] = [:]"
- **Configurable error simulation** — Mocks expose error properties specifically so failure paths that are hard to trigger against real I/O become one-line arrangements. > "Error simulation**: Design mocks with configurable error properties for testing failure paths"
- **Default-parameter injection** — The subject's initializer defaults to real providers, so production call sites pass nothing and tests override only the dependency under test. > "Default parameters**: Let production code use real implementations by default; only tests need to specify mocks"
- **Actor-based subject under test** — `SyncManager` is a `public actor` with an async `sync()`, which is why the boundary protocols need `Sendable`. > "public actor SyncManager {"
- **Swift Testing suite** — Tests are named `@Test("…")` cases using `#expect` and `#expect(throws:)` rather than XCTest. > "@Test("Sync manager handles missing container")"
- **Error-type expectation** — A specific error case is asserted with `#expect(throws: SyncError.containerNotAvailable)`, while a broader one uses `throws: SyncError.self`. > "await #expect(throws: SyncError.containerNotAvailable) {"
- **Container absence path** — The optional `containerURL` returning nil is the branch that throws `SyncError.containerNotAvailable`, and it is the only route to that error. > "guard let containerURL = fileSystem.containerURL(for: .sync) else {"
- **Atomic write** — The production writer passes `.atomic` so a failed write cannot leave a partial file. > "try data.write(to: url, options: .atomic)"
- **Environment portability** — The point of the abstraction is one module working in app, test, and SwiftUI preview contexts. > "Building modules that need to work in app, test, and SwiftUI preview contexts"
- **Boundary-only mocking** — Only genuinely external dependencies get mocked; internal types stay concrete. > "Only mock boundaries**: Mock external dependencies (file system, network, APIs), not internal types"
RULES:
- Each protocol handles exactly one concern; no god protocols — > "Single Responsibility**: Each protocol should handle one concern — don't create "god protocols" with many methods"
- Sendable conformance is required when protocols cross actor boundaries — > "Sendable conformance**: Required when protocols are used across actor boundaries"
- Production code uses real implementations by default; only tests specify mocks — > "Default parameters**: Let production code use real implementations by default; only tests need to specify mocks"
- Design mocks with configurable error properties — > "Error simulation**: Design mocks with configurable error properties for testing failure paths"
- Only mock boundaries, not internal types — > "Only mock boundaries**: Mock external dependencies (file system, network, APIs), not internal types"
- A type with no external dependencies gets no protocol — > "Over-engineering: if a type has no external dependencies, it doesn't need a protocol"
- Don't create a single large protocol covering all external access — > "Creating a single large protocol that covers all external access"
- Don't mock internal types that have no external dependencies — > "Mocking internal types that have no external dependencies"
- Use proper injection instead of `#if DEBUG` conditionals — > "Using `#if DEBUG` conditionals instead of proper dependency injection"
- Don't forget `Sendable` conformance when used with actors — > "Forgetting `Sendable` conformance when used with actors"
WORKFLOW: (1) Define a small `Sendable` protocol for each external concern. (2) Implement a default production struct for each. (3) Implement a mock class with storage plus `readError`/`writeError`. (4) Inject via init default parameters in the subject type. (5) Write `@Test` cases covering missing-container, read path, and read-error path with `#expect`/`#expect(throws:)`.
TABLES: none
ANTI-PATTERNS: "god protocols" → split into one protocol per concern. Mocking internal types → mock only boundaries. `#if DEBUG` conditionals → proper injection. Missing `Sendable` → add conformance. Protocol on a type with no external dependency → drop the protocol ("Over-engineering").
TOOLING: Swift `protocol …: Sendable`; `FileManager.default.url(forUbiquityContainerIdentifier:)`; `Data(contentsOf:)`; `data.write(to:options:.atomic)`; `CocoaError(.fileReadNoSuchFile)`, `CocoaError(.fileReadCorruptFile)`; `import Testing`; `@Test("…")`, `#expect`, `#expect(throws:)`; `public final class MockFileAccessor: FileAccessorProviding, @unchecked Sendable`; `public actor SyncManager`.
GOTCHAS: A mock with a mutable dictionary is not genuinely `Sendable`, hence `@unchecked` — the file supplies no synchronization. Missing-key reads must throw `CocoaError(.fileReadNoSuchFile)` or tests pass vacuously. `containerURL` nil path is the only way to reach `SyncError.containerNotAvailable`. Default parameters on an actor init still evaluate the real providers at construction.
STRUCTURE: none

## S121 · browser-qa
SOURCE: none (`metadata: origin: ECC`)
PURPOSE: Runs a four-phase automated post-deploy UI verification (smoke, interaction, visual regression, accessibility) with a browser automation MCP and ends in an explicit ship verdict.
CONCEPTS:
- **Blast radius** — The safety frame comes first: browser QA drives real auth and real journeys, so the default is read-only and mutating journeys need opt-in plus a staging/preview URL. > "Browser QA drives real auth and real user journeys, so treat the blast radius explicitly."
- **Credential hygiene** — Only seeded test credentials are used, and secrets are stripped before any screenshot is saved. > "Use seeded **test credentials**, never real production logins, and **redact**"
- **Phase 1 smoke test** — The smoke phase captures console errors with noise filtered, scans for 4xx/5xx, screenshots above the fold on desktop and mobile, and reads Core Web Vitals. > "Check for console errors (filter noise: analytics, third-party)"
- **Core Web Vitals gate** — The gate is numeric: LCP under 2.5s, CLS under 0.1, INP under 200ms, with INP noted as having replaced FID in March 2024. > "Check Core Web Vitals: LCP < 2.5s, CLS < 0.1, INP < 200ms"
- **Phase 2 interaction test** — Every nav link is clicked for dead links, forms are submitted valid and invalid, and the auth flow runs login → protected page → logout with test credentials only. > "Test auth flow: login → protected page → logout (test creds only, never prod)"
- **Phase 3 visual regression** — Key pages are captured at three breakpoints and diffed against committed baselines. > "Screenshot key pages at 3 breakpoints (375px, 768px, 1440px)"
- **INCONCLUSIVE state** — A missing baseline produces INCONCLUSIVE rather than a silent pass, so an absent check cannot be mistaken for a clean one. > "no baseline ⇒ report INCONCLUSIVE, never a silent PASS"
- **Layout-shift threshold** — Shifts beyond 5px, missing elements and overflow are flagged, and dark mode is checked when applicable. > "Flag layout shifts > 5px, missing elements, overflow"
- **Phase 4 accessibility** — axe-core runs per page, WCAG 2.2 AA violations are flagged, keyboard navigation is verified end to end, and landmarks are checked. > "Flag WCAG 2.2 AA violations (contrast, labels, focus order)"
- **Automation coverage ceiling** — axe-core covers roughly 30–40% of WCAG, so a clean automated run is necessary but not sufficient and the manual pass still applies. > "axe-core automatically covers roughly 30–40% of WCAG."
- **Verdict taxonomy** — The report ends in one of SHIP, SHIP WITH FIXES, or DO NOT SHIP, with INCONCLUSIVE reserved for the no-baseline case. > "verdict ∈ SHIP / SHIP WITH FIXES / DO NOT SHIP; use INCONCLUSIVE if no visual baseline"
- **Structured QA report** — The output is a fixed markdown skeleton with one section per phase, checkbox marks per finding, and a counted verdict line. > "## QA Report — [URL] — [timestamp]"
- **MCP abstraction** — The same procedure runs over the claude-in-chrome tools, Playwright through Browserbase, or raw Puppeteer scripts. > "Works with any browser MCP:"
RULES:
- Default to read-only; never run a mutating journey (checkout, payment, delete, mass-update) against a production URL — require explicit opt-in and a staging/preview URL — > "never run a **mutating** journey (checkout, payment, delete,"
- Use seeded test credentials, never real production logins — > "Use seeded **test credentials**, never real production logins, and **redact**"
- Redact credentials, tokens and PII before saving any screenshot — > "credentials/tokens/PII before saving any screenshot."
- Filter console noise from analytics and third parties — > "Check for console errors (filter noise: analytics, third-party)"
- Core Web Vitals must clear LCP < 2.5s, CLS < 0.1, INP < 200ms — > "Check Core Web Vitals: LCP < 2.5s, CLS < 0.1, INP < 200ms"
- Screenshot exactly three breakpoints: 375px, 768px, 1440px — > "Screenshot key pages at 3 breakpoints (375px, 768px, 1440px)"
- Flag layout shifts over 5px — > "Flag layout shifts > 5px, missing elements, overflow"
- No baseline means INCONCLUSIVE, never a silent PASS — > "no baseline ⇒ report INCONCLUSIVE, never a silent PASS"
- Flag WCAG 2.2 AA violations — > "Flag WCAG 2.2 AA violations (contrast, labels, focus order)"
- The verdict is one of SHIP / SHIP WITH FIXES / DO NOT SHIP, or INCONCLUSIVE with no visual baseline — > "verdict ∈ SHIP / SHIP WITH FIXES / DO NOT SHIP; use INCONCLUSIVE if no visual baseline"
- Don't report "accessible" from an automated pass alone — > "Don't report "accessible" from an automated pass alone."
WORKFLOW: (1) Confirm target is staging/preview and journey is non-mutating. (2) Smoke: navigate, check console errors, verify no 4xx/5xx, screenshot desktop + mobile above the fold, check CWV thresholds. (3) Interactions: click every nav link, submit valid and invalid forms, run auth flow with test creds, exercise critical journeys. (4) Visual: screenshot key pages at 375/768/1440, diff against baselines, flag >5px shifts/overflow, check dark mode. (5) Accessibility: axe-core per page, flag AA violations, keyboard nav, landmarks. (6) Emit the QA report and one verdict.
TABLES: None formatted as a table; the verdict scheme `SHIP / SHIP WITH FIXES / DO NOT SHIP / INCONCLUSIVE` functions as the scoring scale. The QA report template is a fixed four-section layout (Smoke Test, Interactions, Visual, Accessibility) plus a verdict line.
ANTI-PATTERNS: Running mutating journeys against production → require opt-in and staging URL. Real production logins → seeded test credentials. Unredacted screenshots → redact credentials/tokens/PII. Treating a clean axe run as "accessible" → manual keyboard/focus/screen-reader pass. Counting analytics noise as console errors → filter third-party noise. Missing visual baseline reported as PASS → INCONCLUSIVE.
TOOLING: MCP tool prefixes `mChild__claude-in-chrome__*` (preferred), `mcp__browserbase__*` (Playwright), direct Puppeteer scripts. `axe-core`. Companion `/canary-watch` for post-deploy monitoring. Report header `## QA Report — [URL] — [timestamp]`.
GOTCHAS: INP replaced FID in March 2024, so stale FID-based checks are wrong. axe-core catches only ~30–40% of WCAG. No baseline = no visual verdict. Console noise from analytics/third-party must be filtered or the smoke phase is unusable. Dark mode is conditional ("if applicable").
STRUCTURE: none

## S122 · csharp-testing
SOURCE: none (`metadata: origin: ECC`)
PURPOSE: Prescribes a .NET test stack and the house patterns for unit, integration, and data-driven tests so an agent writes xUnit/FluentAssertions tests with mocked or containerised infrastructure instead of ad-hoc ones.
CONCEPTS:
- **Framework stack** — Six tools are fixed: xUnit for the framework, FluentAssertions for syntax, NSubstitute or Moq for mocks, Testcontainers for real infrastructure, WebApplicationFactory for ASP.NET Core, and Bogus for data. > "| **xUnit** | Test framework (preferred for .NET) |"
- **Arrange-Act-Assert** — Test classes are `sealed`, hold an `_sut` field plus substitute fields built in the constructor, and mark the three sections with comments. > "public sealed class OrderServiceTests"
- **Per-test construction** — xUnit constructs the test class per test, which is the mechanism the file relies on for fresh state; static fields would defeat it. > "Fresh instance per test (xUnit does this via constructors)"
- **Result-object assertions** — Success is asserted through `IsSuccess`, `Value` and `Error` rather than by catching thrown exceptions. > "result.IsSuccess.Should().BeFalse();"
- **Theory/InlineData** — Table-driven validators put each input/expectation pair in an `[InlineData(...)]` row on a `[Theory]`. > "[InlineData("user+tag@example.co.uk", true)]"
- **MemberData** — Larger invalid-input sets come from a `static TheoryData<CreateOrderRequest, string>` source property. > "public static TheoryData<CreateOrderRequest, string> InvalidOrderCases => new()"
- **NSubstitute arrangement** — Stubbing returns uses `.Returns((Order?)null)` and matches any token with `Arg.Any<CancellationToken>()`. > ".Returns((Order?)null);"
- **Interaction assertion** — Persistence is verified through `.Received(1)` with an `Arg.Is<Order>` predicate rather than by re-reading the store. > "await _repository.Received(1).AddAsync("
- **WebApplicationFactory integration test** — The API test class implements `IClassFixture<WebApplicationFactory<Program>>` and rebuilds the host with `WithWebHostBuilder` plus `ConfigureServices`. > "public sealed class OrderApiTests : IClassFixture<WebApplicationFactory<Program>>"
- **Service replacement** — The real DbContext registration is removed with `RemoveAll<DbContextOptions<AppDbContext>>()` before the in-memory one is added. > "services.RemoveAll<DbContextOptions<AppDbContext>>();"
- **Testcontainers** — Repository tests build a `PostgreSqlContainer` pinned to `postgres:16-alpine` and manage it through `IAsyncLifetime`. > ".WithImage("postgres:16-alpine")"
- **Migration on startup** — The container schema is created by running `MigrateAsync()` before any assertion, so constraints match reality. > "await _db.Database.MigrateAsync();"
- **Test project layout** — Three projects split by boundary, with a separate helpers project for builders and fixtures. > "dotnet test tests/MyApp.UnitTests/"
- **Test data builder** — A fluent `OrderBuilder` with `WithCustomer`/`WithItem`/`Build` seeds sensible defaults so each test states only what it cares about. > "public OrderBuilder WithCustomer(string customerId)"
- **Coverage collection** — Coverage is collected through the built-in collector flag on `dotnet test`. > "dotnet test --collect:"XPlat Code Coverage""
RULES:
- Test names follow `Method_ExpectedResult_WhenCondition` and describe behaviour, not implementation — > "Name by behavior: `Method_ExpectedResult_WhenCondition`"
- One logical assertion per test — > "One logical assertion per test"
- Always pass and verify cancellation — > "Always pass and verify cancellation"
- Fresh instance per test; xUnit does this via constructors — > "Fresh instance per test (xUnit does this via constructors)"
- Never `Thread.Sleep` in async tests; use `Task.Delay` with timeout or polling helpers — > "Use `Task.Delay` with timeout, or polling helpers"
- Test behaviour and outcomes, not implementation details — > "Test behavior and outcomes"
- Assert on typed properties, not on `ToString()` output — > "Assert on typed properties"
- Integration fixtures replace the real DB with `UseInMemoryDatabase("TestDb")` — > "options.UseInMemoryDatabase("TestDb"));"
- Repository tests run against a real `postgres:16-alpine` container — > "public sealed class PostgresOrderRepositoryTests : IAsyncLifetime"
WORKFLOW: (1) Pick the project (unit vs integration) by test boundary. (2) Build a `Substitute.For<>` field per dependency in the class constructor. (3) Write Arrange-Act-Assert with FluentAssertions. (4) Move repeated invalid inputs into `[Theory]`/`[MemberData]`. (5) For HTTP endpoints, subclass the factory and swap services via `ConfigureServices`. (6) For repositories, start a Testcontainers Postgres, migrate, assert persistence. (7) Run `dotnet test`, optionally with coverage, filter, or `dotnet watch test`.
TABLES: `Test Framework Stack` — rows = 6 tools; columns = Tool, Purpose. `Common Anti-Patterns` — rows = 7; columns = Anti-Pattern, Fix.
ANTI-PATTERNS: Testing implementation details → test behavior. Shared mutable test state → fresh instance per test. `Thread.Sleep` in async tests → `Task.Delay` with timeout or polling. Asserting on `ToString()` → typed properties. One giant assertion per test → "One logical assertion per test". Implementation-named tests → `Method_ExpectedResult_WhenCondition`. Ignoring `CancellationToken` → always pass and verify.
TOOLING: `dotnet test`; `dotnet test --collect:"XPlat Code Coverage"`; `dotnet test tests/MyApp.UnitTests/`; `dotnet test --filter "FullyQualifiedName~OrderService"`; `dotnet watch test --project tests/MyApp.UnitTests/`. APIs: `[Fact]`, `[Theory]`, `[InlineData]`, `[MemberData]`, `TheoryData<,>`, `Substitute.For`, `.Returns`, `.Received(1)`, `Arg.Any`, `Arg.Is`, `IClassFixture`, `WithWebHostBuilder`, `RemoveAll`, `PostgreSqlContainer`, `PostgreSqlBuilder`, `IAsyncLifetime`, `PostAsJsonAsync`.
GOTCHAS: xUnit's per-test class construction is the mechanism behind "no shared mutable state" — static fields break it. `RemoveAll<DbContextOptions<AppDbContext>>()` is required before re-registering, otherwise both providers resolve. In-memory database diverges from real Postgres constraints and SQL, so repository tests use a container. Container tests must `MigrateAsync()` before asserting. `CancellationToken.None` in tests never verifies cancellation.
STRUCTURE: none

## S123 · playwright
SOURCE: none (self-hosted path `$CODEX_HOME/skills/playwright/scripts/playwright_cli.sh`; upstream CLI `@playwright/cli@latest`)
PURPOSE: Drives a real browser from the terminal with `playwright-cli` via a bundled wrapper, using snapshot-derived element refs for navigation, forms, screenshots, and traces rather than authoring Playwright test specs.
CONCEPTS:
- **CLI-first stance** — The default mode is terminal automation; authoring `@playwright/test` files is only on explicit request. > "Treat this skill as CLI-first automation. Do not pivot to `@playwright/test` unless the user explicitly asks for test files."
- **Prerequisite gate** — The wrapper depends on `npx`, so availability is checked before any command is proposed. > "Before proposing commands, check whether `npx` is available (the wrapper depends on it):"
- **Wrapper script** — The wrapper runs the CLI through `npx --package`, which is why no global install is required. > "The wrapper script uses `npx --package @playwright/cli playwright-cli` so the CLI can run without a global install:"
- **Skill path pinning** — `CODEX_HOME` defaults to `~/.codex` and `PWCLI` is exported once, because user-scoped skills install under the codex home. > "User-scoped skills install under `$CODEX_HOME/skills` (default: `~/.codex/skills`)."
- **Snapshot** — A snapshot returns stable element refs such as `e15`, `e3`, `e12` that later commands address by name. > "Snapshot to get stable element refs."
- **Ref freshness / staleness** — Refs go stale silently, and a command failing on a missing ref is the signal to snapshot again. > "Refs can go stale. When a command fails due to a missing ref, snapshot again."
- **Core interaction loop** — The loop is open, snapshot, click, snapshot — always interacting from the latest snapshot's refs. > "Interact using refs from the latest snapshot."
- **Placeholder refs** — With no fresh snapshot the agent uses an `eX` placeholder and states the reason, rather than escaping the ref model with `run-code`. > "use placeholder refs like `eX` and say why; do not bypass refs with `run-code`."
- **Headed mode** — `--headed` is used when a visual check helps and when debugging a flow. > "Use `--headed` when a visual check will help."
- **Tracing** — `tracing-start` and `tracing-stop` bracket a UI-flow reproduction so the failure can be inspected afterwards. > "Debug a UI flow with traces"
- **Multi-tab management** — Extra tabs are created, listed and selected explicitly rather than assumed. > ""$PWCLI" tab-new https://example.com"
- **Artifact convention** — Captures land in `output/playwright/` and no new top-level artifact folder is introduced. > "use `output/playwright/` and avoid introducing new top-level artifact folders."
- **Progressive disclosure** — The two reference files are opened only as needed rather than loaded up front. > "Open only what you need:"
RULES:
- Check `npx` before proposing commands; if absent, pause and ask the user to install Node.js/npm — > "If it is not available, pause and ask the user to install Node.js/npm (which provides `npx`)."
- Always snapshot before referencing element ids like `e12` — > "Always snapshot before referencing element ids like `e12`."
- Re-snapshot when refs seem stale — > "Re-snapshot when refs seem stale."
- Prefer explicit commands over `eval` and `run-code` unless needed — > "Prefer explicit commands over `eval` and `run-code` unless needed."
- Without a fresh snapshot, use `eX` placeholders and say why; never bypass refs with `run-code` — > "When you do not have a fresh snapshot, use placeholder refs like `eX` and say why; do not bypass refs with `run-code`."
- Use `--headed` when a visual check will help — > "Use `--headed` when a visual check will help."
- Capture artifacts under `output/playwright/`; avoid new top-level artifact folders — > "When capturing artifacts in this repo, use `output/playwright/` and avoid introducing new top-level artifact folders."
- Default to CLI commands and workflows, not Playwright test specs — > "Default to CLI commands and workflows, not Playwright test specs."
- A global `playwright-cli` install is optional — > "A global install of `playwright-cli` is optional."
WORKFLOW: (1) `command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1`; if missing, give the Node/npm install steps verbatim and stop. (2) `export CODEX_HOME="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}"` and `export PWCLI="$CODEX_HOME/skills/playwright/scripts/playwright_cli.sh"`. (3) Open the page. (4) `snapshot` to get refs. (5) Interact using refs from the latest snapshot. (6) Re-snapshot after navigation or significant DOM change. (7) Capture artifacts (screenshot, pdf, traces) when useful.
TABLES: none
ANTI-PATTERNS: Pivoting to `@playwright/test` test files → stay CLI-first unless explicitly asked. Referencing refs without a snapshot → snapshot first. Reusing refs after navigation → re-snapshot. Bypassing refs with `run-code`/`eval` → use `eX` placeholders and explain. Creating new top-level artifact folders → use `output/playwright/`. Hard-depending on a global install → use the wrapper.
TOOLING: `command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1`; `node --version`; `npm --version`; `npm install -g @playwright/cli@latest`; `playwright-cli --help`; `"$PWCLI" open <url> [--headed]`; `"$PWCLI" snapshot`; `"$PWCLI" click e15`; `"$PWCLI" type "Playwright"`; `"$PWCLI" press Enter`; `"$PWCLI" fill e1 "user@example.com"`; `"$PWCLI" screenshot`; `"$PWCLI" tracing-start` / `tracing-stop`; `"$PWCLI" tab-new <url>`; `"$PWCLI" tab-list`; `"$PWCLI" tab-select 0`; wrapper internals `npx --package @playwright/cli playwright-cli`.
GOTCHAS: Refs go stale silently between snapshots — "When a command fails due to a missing ref, snapshot again". Without `npx` the wrapper cannot run at all. User-scoped skills resolve to `~/.codex/skills` unless `CODEX_HOME` is overridden. Wrapper path assumes the skill is installed at `$CODEX_HOME/skills/playwright/`.
STRUCTURE: `scripts/playwright_cli.sh` (declared, not bundled), `references/cli.md` (declared, not bundled), `references/workflows.md` (declared, not bundled).

## S124 · csharp-mstest
SOURCE: none (links `https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/testing/unit-testing-mstest-writing-tests-testcontext`)
PURPOSE: Instructs an agent to write MSTest 3.x/4.x unit tests using current assertion APIs, constructor lifecycle, data-driven sources, and attributes, replacing obsolete MSTest idioms.
CONCEPTS:
- **Test project convention** — A separate project named `[ProjectName].Tests` references MSTest 3.x+ NuGet packages, which include the analyzers, with `MSTest.Sdk` as an optional simplification. > "Use a separate test project with naming convention `[ProjectName].Tests`"
- **Sealed test classes** — Classes are sealed by default for performance and design clarity, not left open for inheritance. > "**Seal test classes by default** for performance and design clarity"
- **[TestMethod] over [DataTestMethod]** — `[DataTestMethod]` is superseded; data rows hang off `[TestMethod]` directly. > "Use `[TestMethod]` for test methods (prefer over `[DataTestMethod]`)"
- **Naming pattern** — Test names follow `MethodName_Scenario_ExpectedBehavior`, and bodies follow Arrange-Act-Assert. > "Name tests using pattern `MethodName_Scenario_ExpectedBehavior`"
- **Constructor-over-[TestInitialize]** — The constructor is preferred because it enables `readonly` fields; `[TestInitialize]` remains only for async setup. > "**Prefer constructors over `[TestInitialize]`** - enables `readonly` fields and follows standard C# patterns"
- **Execution order model** — A seven-stage sequence runs assembly init, class init, per-test init (constructor, TestContext, `[TestInitialize]`), execution, per-test cleanup, class cleanup, assembly cleanup. > "**Assembly Initialization** - `[AssemblyInitialize]` (once per test assembly)"
- **Assert widening** — `Assert.Throws` matches the type or derived types, while `Assert.ThrowsExactly` matches the exact type, with async variants of both. > "// Assert.Throws - matches TException or derived types"
- **Collection assertions** — The `Assert` class covers containment, single-element, count, empty and non-empty checks. > "Assert.ContainsSingle(collection);  // exactly one element"
- **String assertions** — Prefix, suffix, their negations, and regex matching all live on `Assert`. > "Assert.StartsWith("prefix", actualString);"
- **Comparison assertions** — Greater/less with equality variants, range checks, and sign checks. > "Assert.IsInRange(actual, low, high);"
- **Type assertions** — MSTest 3.x uses an out parameter, while 4.x returns the typed result directly. > "// MSTest 4.x - returns typed result directly"
- **Assert.That (4.0+)** — A single boolean form that auto-captures the expression into the failure message. > "Assert.That(result.Count > 0);  // Auto-captures expression in failure message"
- **Legacy assertion classes** — `StringAssert` and `CollectionAssert` still exist but `Assert` equivalents are preferred when available. > "Prefer `Assert` class equivalents when available (e.g., `Assert.Contains`)."
- **CollectionAssert semantics** — `AreEqual` is order-sensitive while `AreEquivalent` accepts any order, with subset checks and `AllItemsAre*` validators alongside. > "// Equality (same elements, same order)"
- **DataRow metadata** — A `[DataRow]` can carry `DisplayName` and, from 3.8+, `IgnoreMessage`. > "`IEnumerable<TestDataRow>` - provides type safety plus control over test metadata (display name, categories)"
- **DynamicData source ranking** — ValueTuple is preferred (3.7+), then `TestDataRow` for metadata, with `object[]` the least preferred because it has no compile-time checking. > "`IEnumerable<(T1, T2, ...)>` (ValueTuple) - **preferred**, provides type safety (MSTest 3.7+)"
- **TestContext access** — It arrives as a property, a constructor parameter (3.6+, preferred for immutability), a static method parameter, or a cleanup parameter. > "// Constructor injection (MSTest 3.6+) - preferred for immutability"
- **Cancellation** — Cooperative cancellation pairs `TestContext.CancellationToken` with `[Timeout]`. > "Always use `TestContext.CancellationToken` for cooperative cancellation with `[Timeout]`:"
- **Retry (3.9+)** — `[Retry(n)]` wraps flaky tests rather than loosening their assertions. > "### Retry for Flaky Tests (MSTest 3.9+)"
- **Conditional execution (3.10+)** — `[OSCondition]` and `[CICondition]` skip or run tests by platform and CI, with `ConditionMode.Include/Exclude`. > "Skip or run tests based on OS or CI environment:"
- **Parallelization** — Assembly-level `Parallelize` sets workers and scope, while `[DoNotParallelize]` opts a class out. > "[assembly: Parallelize(Workers = 4, Scope = ExecutionScope.MethodLevel)]"
- **Traceability** — `[WorkItem]` and `[GitHubWorkItem]` link tests to issues so reports can trace coverage back to requirements. > "Link tests to work items for traceability in test reports:"
- **Categorisation** — `[TestCategory]`, `[TestProperty]` and `[Priority]` provide filtering and custom metadata. > "Use `[TestCategory("Category")]` for filtering"
RULES:
- Prefer `[TestMethod]` over `[DataTestMethod]` — > "Use `[TestMethod]` for test methods (prefer over `[DataTestMethod]`)"
- Prefer constructors over `[TestInitialize]` so fields can be `readonly` — > "**Prefer constructors over `[TestInitialize]`** - enables `readonly` fields and follows standard C# patterns"
- Prefer `Assert.Throws` over `[ExpectedException]` — > "### Exception Testing (Prefer over `[ExpectedException]`)"
- Prefer `Assert` equivalents over `StringAssert`/`CollectionAssert` — > "Prefer `Assert` class equivalents when available (e.g., `Assert.Contains`)."
- Seal test classes by default — > "**Seal test classes by default** for performance and design clarity"
- Declare `public TestContext TestContext { get; set; }` with no nullable annotation and no initializer — > "✅ Declare without nullable or initializer - MSTest handles the warning"
- Always use `TestContext.CancellationToken` — > "Always use `TestContext.CancellationToken` for cooperative cancellation with `[Timeout]`:"
- Argument order is expected first, actual second — > "Assert.AreEqual(expected, actual);"
- Long async tests take `[Timeout(5000)]` — > "[Timeout(5000)]"
- Flaky tests take `[Retry(3)]` — > "[Retry(3)]"
- Parallelism uses `Workers = 4` at method-level scope — > "[assembly: Parallelize(Workers = 4, Scope = ExecutionScope.MethodLevel)]"
- Prefer `ValueTuple` or `TestDataRow` over `IEnumerable<object[]>` — > "prefer `ValueTuple` or `TestDataRow` over `IEnumerable<object[]>`"
- Enable the `MSTEST0020` analyzer for constructor preference — > "Enable relevant MSTest analyzers (MSTEST0020 for constructor preference)"
WORKFLOW: (1) Create `[ProjectName].Tests` referencing MSTest 3.x+ / MSTest.Sdk. (2) Declare a sealed `[TestClass]` with a readonly field initialised in the constructor. (3) Add `[TestInitialize]` only for async setup and `[TestCleanup]` for must-run cleanup. (4) Write `MethodName_Scenario_ExpectedBehavior` bodies in Arrange-Act-Assert. (5) Parameterise with `[DataRow]` or `[DynamicData]`. (6) Add `[Timeout]` + `TestContext.CancellationToken` for long async tests. (7) Apply `[Retry]`, `[OSCondition]`, `[CICondition]`, `[DoNotParallelize]` as needed. (8) Run `dotnet test`.
TABLES: `Execution Order` — 7 numbered stages (assembly init, class init, per-test init with 3 sub-steps, execution, per-test cleanup with 3 sub-steps, class cleanup, assembly cleanup). `DynamicData source types` — ranked list of 4 source shapes by type safety (ValueTuple preferred → `object[]` least preferred). `Common Mistakes to Avoid` — paired wrong/right code snippets (7 pairs) covering argument order, `ExpectedException`, LINQ `Single()`, hard casts, ignored cancellation, nullable `TestContext`, `null!` initializer.
ANTI-PATTERNS: `Assert.AreEqual(actual, expected)` → correct order is expected-first. `[ExpectedException]` (obsolete) → `Assert.Throws<ArgumentException>`. `items.Single()` → `Assert.ContainsSingle(items)` for a better failure message. Hard cast `(MyHandler)result` → `Assert.IsInstanceOfType<MyHandler>(result)`. `CancellationToken.None` → `TestContext.CancellationToken`. Nullable `TestContext?` → plain property. `= null!` initializer → plain property, MSTest suppresses CS8618. `IEnumerable<object[]>` data → ValueTuple/TestDataRow.
TOOLING: Attributes: `[TestClass]`, `[TestMethod]`, `[DataRow]`, `[DynamicData]`, `[TestInitialize]`, `[TestCleanup]`, `[ClassInitialize]`, `[ClassCleanup]`, `[AssemblyInitialize]`, `[AssemblyCleanup]`, `[Timeout]`, `[Retry]`, `[OSCondition]`, `[CICondition]`, `[DoNotParallelize]`, `[WorkItem]`, `[GitHubWorkItem]`, `[TestCategory]`, `[TestProperty]`, `[Priority]`. Assembly: `[assembly: Parallelize(Workers = 4, Scope = ExecutionScope.MethodLevel)]`. TestContext members: `TestName`, `TestDisplayName`, `CurrentTestOutcome`, `TestData`, `TestException`, `DeploymentDirectory`, `CancellationToken`, `WriteLine`, `AddResultFile`, `Properties`. CLI: `dotnet test`.
GOTCHAS: `Assert.Throws` also matches derived exception types — use `Assert.ThrowsExactly` when the exact type matters. MSTest already suppresses CS8618 for `TestContext`, so `null!`/nullable forms are redundant and harmful. `[DataTestMethod]` is superseded by `[TestMethod]`. `object[]` dynamic data defects surface only at runtime. Some APIs are version-gated: `IgnoreMessage`/`WorkItem`/`GitHubWorkItem` 3.8+, `Retry` 3.9+, `OSCondition`/`CICondition` 3.10+, `Assert.That` 4.0+, constructor `TestContext` injection 3.6+, `TestDisplayName`/`TestData`/`TestException` 3.7+. `[ClassCleanup]`/`[AssemblyCleanup]` accepting `TestContext` is 3.6+.
