- Tests for constructors, type-system-forbidden input, log-string formatting, constants → delete.
- Testing library validation/ORM commit/router 404 → test your own logic layered above.
- Mocking state objects → build a real instance; add a builder/factory if painful.
- Mocking the DB session when persistence is the subject → real DB + migrations via fixtures.
TOOLING:
- Parametrization: `@pytest.mark.parametrize`, PHPUnit `#[DataProvider]`, Jest `test.each`.
- Report template: "**Rule N violation** in `tests/path/file.ext::<test_name>`" with `- What:` and `- Fix:` lines.
- Scope exclusions: not for production/implementation review (use `clean-code-guard`), CI/test-runner config, running or debugging tests.
GOTCHAS:
- Skill is reactive by default; invoked before writing, it must guide writing rather than flag afterwards.
- Rule 3 can misfire on tests that look identical but have different mock configurations.
- Rule 9 is "Worth noting" — flag, but don't block small changes.
- Files with no violations must not be mentioned.
STRUCTURE: `references/pytest.md`, `references/phpunit.md`, `references/jest.md`, `references/llm-app-testing.md` (all declared, not bundled).

## S147 · unit-test-boundary-conditions
SOURCE: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boundary-value_analysis (plus Oracle Java `Integer`/`Double` docs and AssertJ feature docs)
PURPOSE: Tells an agent to write systematic Java/JUnit 5 boundary, corner-case, and limit tests covering numeric extremes, strings, collections, floating point, dates, and array indices.
CONCEPTS:
- **Boundary value analysis** — each limit is probed on both sides rather than only at the limit. > "Cover values just below, at, and just above each boundary"
- **Boundary identification checklist** — the first instruction is to enumerate limits per domain before writing any test. > "List numeric limits (MIN_VALUE, MAX_VALUE, zero), string states (null, empty, whitespace), collection sizes (0, 1, many)"
- **`@ParameterizedTest` boundaries** — the integer quintet is fed through a value source so five cases live in one method. > "@ValueSource(ints = {Integer.MIN_VALUE, Integer.MIN_VALUE + 1, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE - 1, Integer.MAX_VALUE})"
- **Overflow/underflow detection** — exact-math helpers turn a silent wrap into an `ArithmeticException` the test can assert. > "Use `Math.addExact()` to detect silent overflow"
- **Silent integer wrap demonstration** — the plain addition case is shown as what the guard exists to catch. > "assertThatThrownBy(() -> Math.addExact(Integer.MAX_VALUE, 1))"
- **Zero edge cases** — zero as numerator and zero as divisor are distinct behaviours: one returns zero, the other throws. > "int result = MathUtils.divide(0, 5); assertThat(result).isZero();"
- **String boundaries** — emptiness and whitespace are enumerated as separate inputs rather than folded into one blank case. > "Numeric min/max limits, null/empty/whitespace inputs"
- **Collection boundaries** — 0, 1, and many are explicit cases because accessors behave differently at each size. > "Explicitly test empty (0), single (1), and many (>1) element scenarios"
- **Collection accessor contracts** — `first`/`last`/`count` are pinned at the degenerate sizes where they usually break. > "assertThat(CollectionUtils.count(empty)).isZero()"
- **Floating-point precision** — `0.1 + 0.2` is asserted with a tolerance, the only form that survives binary representation. > "Verify floating-point precision: Use `isCloseTo(expected, within(tolerance))` with AssertJ"
- **IEEE special values** — infinity and NaN get their own comparisons, including NaN not equalling itself. > "assertThat(Double.NaN).isNotEqualTo(Double.NaN)"
- **Float division by zero** — the three signed zero-division outcomes each get a case. > "assertThat(1.0 / 0.0).isEqualTo(Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY)"
- **Date/time extremes** — `LocalDate.MIN`/`MAX`, leap days, and invalid dates are covered together. > "Test date/time edges: Verify leap years, month boundaries, timezone transitions"
- **Array index boundaries** — first, last, negative, out-of-bounds, and empty arrays. > "Array indexing: Always test index 0, length-1, and out-of-bounds"
- **Feedback loop** — a failing boundary is read as evidence of another untested boundary, so the case set grows from failures. > "When a boundary test fails, analyze the error to discover additional untested boundaries"
- **AssertJ idioms** — `assertThatThrownBy`, `hasSize`, `isZero`, `isNull`, `isNaN`, `contains` are the vocabulary the patterns are written in. > "assertThat(withNull).contains(null)"
RULES:
- Probe just below, at, and just above every boundary. > "Test both sides of boundaries (just below, at, just above)"
- Floating point is never compared exactly; tolerance-based assertions only. > "Floating-point precision: Never use exact equality; always use tolerance-based assertions"
- Use `isCloseTo(expected, within(tolerance))` with AssertJ. > "Use `isCloseTo(expected, within(tolerance))` with AssertJ"
- Test 0, 1, and many elements for collections. > "Explicitly test empty (0), single (1), and many (>1) element scenarios"
- Handle null and empty as their own cases, separate from valid inputs. > "Test null and empty separately from valid inputs"
- Exercise overflow and underflow on every numeric operation. > "Test overflow/underflow for all numeric operations"
- Cover index 0, length-1, and out-of-bounds. > "Always test index 0, length-1, and out-of-bounds"
- Assert error messages for invalid boundary inputs and record why the boundary matters in the domain. > "Verify error messages for invalid boundary inputs"
- Explicit boundary cases, not random or fuzz-only coverage of limits. > "Test at boundaries explicitly: don't rely on random testing"
- Run the suite after each boundary category is added. > "Run tests after adding each boundary category"
- Date/time tests account for timezone transitions and DST; string tests cover Unicode. > "Account for timezone transitions and daylight saving"
- Keep large collections and megabyte strings within memory limits. > "Be mindful of memory with large test collections"
WORKFLOW:
1. Identify boundaries (numeric limits, string states, collection sizes).
2. Apply parameterized tests (`@ValueSource`, `@CsvSource`).
3. Test both sides of every boundary.
4. Run tests after each boundary category.
5. Verify floating-point precision with tolerance assertions.
6. Test collection states 0/1/many.
7. Handle overflow/underflow with `Math.addExact()` / `Math.subtractExact()`.
8. Test date/time edges — leap years, month boundaries, timezone transitions.
9. Iterate on failures to discover further untested boundaries.
TABLES: none — content is organized as per-domain code sections (Integer, String, Collection, Floating-Point, Date/Time, Array Index) plus bullet lists.
ANTI-PATTERNS:
- Exact `assertEquals` on doubles → `isCloseTo(..., within(...))`.
- Comparing NaN with `==` / `isEqualTo` → use `Double.isNaN()`.
- Boundary-only happy-path tests → add null/empty/whitespace and error cases separately.
- Ignoring arithmetic overflow because Java wraps silently → `addExact`/`subtractExact`.
- Random/fuzz-only coverage of limits → explicit boundary cases.
- Testing only mid-range values → always include 0, MIN, MAX, length-1, out-of-bounds.
TOOLING:
- Dependencies: `junit-jupiter`, `junit-jupiter-params`, `assertj-core`.
- APIs: `@ParameterizedTest`, `@ValueSource(ints = …)/(strings = …)`, `@CsvSource`, `assertThatThrownBy`, `isCloseTo`, `within`, `Math.addExact`, `Math.subtractExact`, `LocalDate.MIN/MAX`, `Double.isNaN`.
- Frontmatter `allowed-tools: Read, Write, Bash, Glob, Grep`.
GOTCHAS:
- `Double.NaN` is "not equal to" itself — equality assertions silently fail or mislead.
- `Double.MIN_VALUE` is the smallest *positive* value, so `NEGATIVE_INFINITY < Double.MIN_VALUE` reads as a trap.
- Integer arithmetic wraps silently unless exact-math methods are used.
- `LocalDate.of(2023, 2, 29)` throws `DateTimeException`; leap-year logic often misses this.
- Large test collections (100,000 elements / 1,000,000-char strings) risk memory pressure.
- Array negative indexing in the example relies on exception behavior for `array[-1]`.
STRUCTURE: `references/concurrent-testing.md` and `references/parameterized-patterns.md` (both declared, not bundled).

## S148 · assertion-quality
SOURCE: none (license: MIT declared in frontmatter)
PURPOSE: Tells an agent to audit existing tests for assertion quality — depth, category diversity, and false confidence — and report a metrics-based verdict rather than fix the tests.
CONCEPTS:
- **Assertion diversity as the core measure** — the report asks whether tests cover different facets of correctness, not how many assertions exist. > "but also structure, exceptions, state transitions, side effects, and invariants"
- **False-confidence symptoms** — passing tests with bugs sitting in unasserted logic is the failure the analysis targets. > "Low assertion diversity signals shallow testing. Tests may pass while bugs hide in unasserted logic."
- **Twelve-category taxonomy** — every assertion is classified into one language-neutral category so spread can be counted. > "For each test method, identify all assertions and classify them into these language-neutral categories"
- **Multi-category assertions** — one assertion may count for several categories, which keeps credit honest without inflating totals. > "A single assertion can belong to multiple categories"
- **Language extension catalog** — framework detail lives in an external reference that must be read before judging any assertion form. > "Read the corresponding file in `extensions/` relative to the supplied `test-analysis-extensions` catalog"
- **Test-file discovery markers** — each language's test files are found by its own markers rather than by filename guesses. > "scan for all test files using the markers in the language extension file"
- **Per-test metrics** — each method gets an assertion count and the categories it uses. > "Assertion count: Number of assertions in each test method"
- **Suite metrics** — the suite-level numbers are what convert impressions into a verdict. > "Average assertions per test: Total assertions / total test methods"
- **Self-referential/tautological assertions** — round-trip and field-against-itself checks look like equality but pin nothing about the transformation. > "These are tautological — they verify the plumbing, not the behavior."
- **Calibration rule** — a weakness claim requires a defective value that the same predicate would still accept. > "name one realistic defective value or behavior that would still satisfy that exact predicate"
- **Counterexample discipline** — the inverse also holds: credit an assertion only by naming the behaviour it pins. > "For every assertion credited as meaningful, name the behavior it pins"
- **Framework-semantics precision** — matcher behaviour is stated exactly, so a subset check is never reported as full equality. > "verifies the expected subset structurally; it neither proves object identity nor full-object equality"
- **Triviality test** — a lone null check is trivial, and adding one meaningful value assertion changes that verdict. > "A null/None/nil check alone is trivial"
- **Exception-test allowance** — exception-focused tests are complete with a single assertion and are exempt from count warnings. > "Exception assertions are complete on their own — skip count warnings for these"
- **Mock-call verifications** — a verified call is a real side-effect assertion, not a missing-framework smell. > "`verify(mock).method(...)`, `expect(mock).toHaveBeenCalledWith(...)`, `Should -Invoke` are State/Side-effect assertions"
- **Snapshot assertions** — snapshots count as deep/structural, while staleness is reported separately. > "count as Structural/Deep assertions. Flag stale or never-updated snapshots separately."
- **Property-based tests** — the inner assertion logic is counted, not the generator scaffold. > "count the inner assertion logic, not the outer scaffold"
- **Unawaited async assertions** — a missing `await` turns green tests into assertion-free tests and is treated as such. > "silently pass tests where assertions are not `await`ed — treat as assertion-free even when assertion calls are present"
- **Report-depth scaling** — a short suite gets a short report, because a padded dashboard buries the answer. > "Scale the report depth to the size and complexity of the suite"
RULES:
- Activate on questions about weak, shallow, trivial, always-true, self-referential, assertion-free, or truthiness-only assertions. > "ALWAYS USE when asked about weak, shallow, trivial, always-true, self-referential, assertion-free, presence/truthiness-only, or insufficiently diverse assertions"
- Not for direct fixes or new test writing; those belong to the sibling skills named in the frontmatter. > "DO NOT USE for direct fixes: writing-mstest-tests owns supplied MSTest assertions; code-testing owns new cases"
- Target at least 10% of tests asserting what should not happen. > "target: at least 10% of tests should verify what should NOT happen"
- Flag trivial only when no meaningful value assertion exists. > "if it has no meaningful value assertions"
- Never claim `toMatchObject` proves identity or full-object equality. > "it neither proves object identity nor full-object equality"
- Boolean assertions on real properties are not trivial; only always-true forms are. > "Boolean assertions checking meaningful conditions are not trivial"
- Exception tests are not penalized for low counts. > "Exception tests are inherently low-assertion-count"
- Diversity is not volume; a long equality chain adds nothing. > "Don't conflate diversity with volume"
- Only recommend assertion types that would catch real bugs here. > "Only suggest adding assertion types that would catch real bugs in the code under test"
- Say so when the suite is well diversified. > "If the suite has good diversity, the report acknowledges this"
- Every report states which tests are assertion-free or trivial-only, the verdict, and concrete recommendations. > "answer the user's question directly and concisely: which tests are assertion-free or trivial-only, the overall assertion-quality verdict, and concrete recommendations"
- For each assertion-free create/update/delete, name the returned value or post-condition to check. > "For each assertion-free create/update/delete operation, recommend its specific returned value or observable post-condition"
WORKFLOW:
1. Detect language and load the matching extension from the `test-analysis-extensions` catalog.
2. Gather test code; scan directories using the language extension's markers.
3. Classify every assertion into at least one of the 12 categories.
4. Compute per-test and suite-wide metrics.
5. Apply calibration rules (counterexamples, triviality, framework semantics, mock calls, snapshots, property-based).
6. Report: Summary Dashboard, Category Breakdown, Gap Analysis, Recommendations, assertion-free test list — scaled to suite size.
TABLES:
- "Why Assertion Diversity Matters" — Problem / Symptom / Consequence; six rows (trivial assertions, single-value obsession, no negative, no state checks, no structural checks, assertion-free).
- Twelve-category classification table — Category / What it verifies / Framework-specific examples (MSTest, xUnit, pytest, Jest, JUnit, Go, Kotest, Pester, GoogleTest, Rust, XCTest).
- Inputs table — Input / Required / Description (Test code yes; Production code no).
- Summary Dashboard template — Metric / Value / Assessment, with sample values (`25` tests, `2.4` average, `5/12` spread, `3 (12%)` zero-assertion, `4 (16%)` trivial, `2 (8%)` negative, `15 (60%)` single-category).
- Common Pitfalls — Pitfall / Solution, eight rows.
ANTI-PATTERNS:
- Penalizing exception tests for low assertion count → skip count warnings for them.
- Flagging a guard null check as trivial → only when it is the only assertion.
- Counting meaningful Boolean assertions as trivial → only always-true forms.
- Ignoring framework differences → read the language extension first.
- Treating bare `assert`, Go `if got != want`, Rust `assert!()` as missing-framework → count them.
- Treating mock-call verification as assertion-free → State/Side-effect category.
- Recommending diversity for its own sake → tie every suggestion to a real bug class.
- Over-indexing on a full dashboard for tiny inputs → scale down.
TOOLING: language files `extensions/` under the supplied `test-analysis-extensions` catalog (`dotnet.md`, `python.md`, `typescript.md`, `go.md`, …); framework APIs cited include `Assert.AreEqual`, `pytest.raises`, `expect(fn).toThrow`, `assert.ErrorIs`, `#[should_panic]`, `XCTAssertThrowsError`, `Should -Throw`, `EXPECT_THROW`, `.toMatchSnapshot()`, `syrupy`, `SnapshotTesting`, `cmp.Diff`, `usingRecursiveComparison()`.
GOTCHAS:
- If the extension bundle is absent, "use the pinned framework and this skill's rules, report the missing reference, and do not search installation directories".
- An unavailable reference "changes the evidence limit, not the workspace root".
- Unawaited async assertions produce green tests that assert nothing.
- Stale snapshots hide regressions; flag them separately from diversity.
- Self-referential round-trip assertions are valid only when the round-trip *is* the test purpose, and still need non-trivial inputs.
STRUCTURE: `extensions/` language files (`dotnet.md`, `python.md`, `typescript.md`, `go.md`, etc.) declared via the external `test-analysis-extensions` catalog — declared, not bundled.

## S149 · playwright-skill
SOURCE: `source: community`, `date_added: "2026-02-27"`; references `API_REFERENCE.md`, `lib/helpers.js`, `run.js` (no URL)
PURPOSE: Tells an agent to write custom Playwright Node scripts for browser automation — responsive viewport checks, screenshots, login flows, form submission, link checks — and run them through a local universal executor.
CONCEPTS:
- **universal executor** — A single local runner executes arbitrary Node code the agent writes for the task, so no fixed test suite is needed; the script is the test. > "I'll write custom Playwright code for any automation task you request and execute it via the universal executor."
- **dev-server auto-detection** — The agent probes fixed localhost ports before writing anything, so the target URL is discovered rather than hardcoded and external sites fall back to asking the user. > "I auto-detect running dev servers (or ask for URL if testing external site)"
- **headless: false default** — The browser window stays visible because the visible run is the debugging surface; headless is opt-in and `slowMo: 100` slows actions to make them followable. > "Always use `headless: false` unless user specifically requests headless mode"
- **`TARGET_URL` constant** — The resolved URL is written to a single top-of-file constant so the same script can be re-pointed without editing call sites. > "Put detected/provided URL in a `TARGET_URL` constant at the top of every script"
- **`/tmp` script placement** — Generated automation is throwaway, so it is written to `/tmp/playwright-test-*.js` and kept out of both the skill directory and the user's project. > "NEVER write test files to skill directory; always use `/tmp/playwright-test-*.js`"
- **viewport matrix** — Responsive checks loop one page object through Desktop `1920x1080`, Tablet `768x1024` and Mobile `375x667` with `setViewportSize` plus a full-page screenshot per size. > "I'll test the marketing page across multiple viewports"
- **wait strategies** — Conditions are awaited by URL, selector or load state instead of sleeping, so slow pages wait and fast pages do not stall. > "Use `waitForURL`, `waitForSelector`, `waitForLoadState` instead of fixed timeouts"
- **broken-link audit** — The script collects `a[href^="http"]`, issues `page.request.head(href)` per link and buckets results into `{working, broken}`, but a HEAD result is only an HTTP observation. > "Keep checks to approved origins, cap count/time, and avoid authenticated cross-origin requests."
- **custom HTTP headers** — `PW_HEADER_NAME`/`PW_HEADER_VALUE` (single) or `PW_EXTRA_HEADERS` (JSON) tag automated traffic, request plain-text error bodies, or carry tokens into every request. > "Configure custom headers for all HTTP requests via environment variables"
- **context creation helper** — `helpers.createContext(browser)` builds the browser context with those headers applied, while raw-API scripts call the injected `getContextOptionsWithHeaders()`. > "Headers are automatically applied when using `helpers.createContext()`"
- **inline vs file execution** — Inline snippets are reserved for throwaway probes; anything re-runnable becomes a file. > "Quick one-off tasks (screenshot, check if element exists, get page title)"
- **helper suite** — `safeClick`, `safeType`, `takeScreenshot`, `handleCookieBanner` and `extractTableData` wrap common steps, and the click helper is documented as one action rather than a retry loop. > "await helpers.safeClick(page, 'button.submit'); // one action; do not blindly retry submissions"
- **path resolution (`$SKILL_DIR`)** — The skill installs to plugin, global or project locations, so the directory is discovered from the loaded `SKILL.md` and every command uses that path. > "Before executing any commands, determine the skill directory based on where you loaded this SKILL.md file"
- **progressive disclosure** — `API_REFERENCE.md` is held back until network interception, visual regression, mobile emulation or CI/CD is actually needed, keeping the entry point small. > "Progressive disclosure - API_REFERENCE.md loaded only when advanced features needed"
- **scope and data boundary model** — Arbitrary Node code runs with the account's full filesystem, environment and network privileges, so the model is test accounts, inert page content and authorized origins rather than a sandbox. > "The executor runs arbitrary Node code with the current account’s filesystem, environment and network privileges; it is not a sandbox."
- **private-mode wrapper file** — CommonJS input is copied into a uniquely named file inside the skill directory so `require()` resolves the skill's dependencies, and that file is deleted only on normal exit. > "The executor copies CommonJS code into a private-mode unique file in the skill directory for dependency resolution"
RULES:
- Follow the critical workflow in the given order, and run server detection first for any localhost target. — > "CRITICAL WORKFLOW - Follow these steps in order"
- One detected server is used automatically; with several, the agent asks which one to test. — > "I found 2 dev servers. Which one should I test?"
- Test scripts never go in the skill directory; they go to `/tmp/playwright-test-*.js`. — > "NEVER write test files to skill directory; always use `/tmp/playwright-test-*.js`"
- Keep the browser visible unless the user asks for headless or background runs. — > "Always use `headless: false` unless user specifically requests headless mode"
- Node 22 or later is required, and the install (dependencies plus a browser, including package lifecycle code) is reviewed before setup. — > "Requires Node 22 or later. Review package installation first"
- Close browser and context in `finally` and let failures propagate instead of swallowing them. — > "Always close browser/context in `finally` and propagate failures."
- `safeClick` performs one action; submissions are not blindly retried, and `handleCookieBanner` is used only when a rejection was actually requested. — > "await helpers.handleCookieBanner(page, '[data-testid="cookie-reject"]'); // only if rejection was requested"
- Do not put secrets in context-wide headers on pages with untrusted resources; scope authentication by trusted origin instead. — > "never use this feature for secrets on pages with untrusted resources; scope authentication by trusted origin instead"
- Remove scripts, screenshots and saved sessions after review, because OS temporary-file cleanup is not a retention guarantee. — > "OS temporary-file cleanup is not a retention guarantee"
- Stop and ask when inputs, permissions, safety boundaries or success criteria are missing. — > "Stop and ask for clarification if required inputs, permissions, safety boundaries, or success criteria are missing."
WORKFLOW:
1. `cd "$SKILL_DIR" && node -e "require('./lib/helpers').detectDevServers().then(servers => console.log(JSON.stringify(servers)))"`.
2. Write `/tmp/playwright-test-*.js` with `TARGET_URL` constant and `headless: false`.
3. `cd "$SKILL_DIR" && node run.js /tmp/playwright-test-*.js`.
4. Read real-time results/screenshots; delete artifacts after review.
5. First-time setup: `cd "$SKILL_DIR" && npm run setup`.
TABLES: none explicit; implicit viewport matrix (Desktop 1920x1080 / Tablet 768x1024 / Mobile 375x667) and an inline-vs-files decision split.
ANTI-PATTERNS: writing tests into skill dir or user project → use `/tmp`; hardcoded URL → `TARGET_URL` constant; blind fixed timeouts → `waitForX`; generic Accept/OK cookie click → explicit reject selector; context-wide header for secrets → trusted-origin scoping; treating HEAD results as proof of broken links → HTTP observation only.
TOOLING: `npm run setup`; `node run.js <script>`; `PW_HEADER_NAME`, `PW_HEADER_VALUE`, `PW_EXTRA_HEADERS`; `wireMockConfig`-unrelated flags: `slowMo`, `fullPage: true`, `waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded'`, `timeout: 10000`.
GOTCHAS: executor does not silently install missing packages; repeat browser install when Playwright version requires; `require()` scripts do not get `getContextOptionsWithHeaders` injected; relative imports resolve inside the skill dir, not beside the input; crash can leave the private-mode wrapper file behind; HEAD may be unsupported or authorization-dependent; API reference mixes standalone `playwright` with `@playwright/test`/`axe-playwright` that setup does not install.
STRUCTURE: `API_REFERENCE.md`, `lib/helpers.js`, `run.js`, `package.json` setup script — declared, not bundled.

## S150 · unit-test-service-layer
SOURCE: Mockito (`https://javadoc.io/doc/org.mockito/mockito-core/latest/org/mockito/Mockito.html`), JUnit 5 (`https://junit.org/junit5/docs/current/user-guide/`), AssertJ (`https://assertj.github.io/assertj-core-features-highlight.html`)
PURPOSE: Has the agent write isolated Mockito unit tests for Spring `@Service` classes with repositories/clients mocked, so business logic is tested without a Spring container, database, or network.
CONCEPTS:
- **`@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)`** — JUnit 5 wires the Mockito annotations, so `@Mock` and `@InjectMocks` take effect without booting a Spring context. > "Use `@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)` to enable Mockito annotations."
- **`@Mock` / `@InjectMocks`** — Dependencies (repositories, clients) become annotated mocks while the service under test is constructed with them injected. > "Use `@Mock` for dependencies (repositories, clients) and `@InjectMocks` for the service under test."
- **Arrange-Act-Assert** — Each test is staged: build data and stub returns, invoke the service method, then assert; the aim is speed and isolation. > "Enables fast, isolated tests without Spring container or database."
- **`when().thenReturn()` / `when().thenThrow()`** — Stubbing covers both the happy path and the exception path by configuring what the collaborator returns or throws. > "Create test data and configure mock return values using `when().thenReturn()`."
- **`verify()`** — Interaction verification checks that the service actually collaborated with its collaborator, not just that the result looked right. > "Verify mock interactions with `verify()`"
- **AssertJ assertions** — Returned values are asserted fluently with `assertThat`, and thrown exceptions with `assertThatThrownBy(...).isInstanceOf(...)`. > "Verify returned values with AssertJ assertions"
- **exception scenario testing** — The collaborator returns `Optional.empty()` (or throws) and the test asserts the mapped `UserNotFoundException`, including type and message. > "Validation checkpoint: Verify exception type and message"
- **argument captors** — Captors are documented as a further pattern for inspecting the value handed to a collaborator. > "For additional patterns (multiple dependencies, argument captors, async services, InOrder verification), see `references/examples.md`."
- **`InOrder` verification** — Call ordering across multiple collaborators is the check, treated as an advanced pattern. > "argument captors, async services, InOrder verification), see `references/examples.md`."
- **async services** — Services that complete asynchronously get their own advanced patterns rather than being forced into the plain Arrange-Act-Assert shape. > "For additional patterns (multiple dependencies, argument captors, async services, InOrder verification)"
- **coverage verification** — The full suite is run and a JaCoCo report generated so missing service methods are visible. > "Run full test suite: `mvn test` or `gradle test`"
- **validation checkpoints** — Explicit gates sit after arrange/act/assert and after the exception test, each requiring a green bar before moving on. > "Validation checkpoint: Run test and confirm green bar"
RULES:
- Mock only the service's direct dependencies. — > "Mock only direct dependencies of the service under test"
- One behavior per test method, kept focused. — > "Test one behavior per test method - keep tests focused"
- Use descriptive names such as `expectedUser`, `actualUser`, `captor`. — > "Use descriptive variable names: `expectedUser`, `actualUser`, `captor`"
- Value objects and DTOs are constructed for real with test data, not mocked. — > "Create real instances for value objects and DTOs (don't mock them)"
- Tests stay independent and must not rely on execution order. — > "Tests must be independent; do not rely on execution order."
- `@Spy` is used cautiously because partial mocking is harder to understand and maintain. — > "Be cautious with `@Spy`; partial mocking is harder to understand and maintain."
- Private methods are not tested directly; they are exercised through public behavior. — > "Do not test private methods directly; test them through public method behavior."
- `any()`/`eq()` matchers cannot be mixed with literal values in the same stub. — > "Argument matchers (`any()`, `eq()`) cannot be mixed with actual values in the same stub."
- Verification is limited to interactions that matter to the scenario, avoiding over-verification. — > "Avoid over-verifying; verify only interactions important to the test scenario."
- Every service method has a corresponding test before the work is called done. — > "Confirm all service methods have corresponding tests"
WORKFLOW:
1. Setup test class with `@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)`.
2. Declare `@Mock` dependencies and `@InjectMocks` service.
3. Arrange (`when().thenReturn()`), Act, Assert (`assertThat`, `verify()`); checkpoint: green bar.
4. Test exceptions with `when().thenThrow()` / empty Optional; checkpoint: exception type and message.
5. Run full suite `mvn test` or `gradle test`; coverage `mvn test jacoco:report`; checkpoint: every service method covered.
TABLES: none.
ANTI-PATTERNS: mocking value objects/DTOs → construct real instances with test data; mocking too many dependencies → consider refactoring the service; order-dependent tests → keep independent; direct private-method tests → public behavior; mixing matchers with literals in one stub → use matchers throughout; over-verification → verify only scenario-relevant interactions.
TOOLING: `@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)`, `@Mock`, `@InjectMocks`, `when/thenReturn/thenThrow`, `verify`, `mvn test`, `gradle test`, `mvn test jacoco:report`; allowed-tools `Read, Write, Bash, Glob, Grep`.
GOTCHAS: `@Spy` partial mocking is harder to understand and maintain; a service with too many collaborators signals a design problem; private methods only observable through public behavior.
STRUCTURE: `references/examples.md` (multiple dependencies, argument captors, async services, `InOrder`) — declared, not bundled.

## S151 · unit-test-wiremock-rest-api
SOURCE: WireMock (`https://wiremock.org/`, `https://wiremock.org/docs/stubbing/`)
PURPOSE: Tells the agent to test HTTP client/service integrations against a WireMock stub server — stubbing responses, verifying request details, and simulating failures — with no real network calls.
CONCEPTS:
- **`WireMockExtension` + `@RegisterExtension`** — Registering the extension as a JUnit 5 static field gives per-test lifecycle management, resetting stubs between tests so cases cannot leak into each other. > "Auto-reset: `@RegisterExtension` resets WireMock between tests"
- **`dynamicPort()`** — A runtime-assigned port is required because a fixed port collides when tests run in parallel, which is why the extension is built from `wireMockConfig().dynamicPort()`. > "Dynamic ports required: Fixed ports cause parallel execution conflicts"
- **`getRuntimeInfo().getHttpBaseUrl()`** — The client under test is pointed at the stub server by reading the URL back from the running instance instead of hardcoding one. > "Configure client: Use `wireMock.getRuntimeInfo().getHttpBaseUrl()` as base URL"
- **`stubFor(get(urlEqualTo(...)))`** — Requests are matched on URL, header (`withHeader`, `containing`) and body so the stub only answers the exact call the test intends. > "Stub responses: `stubFor()` with request matching (URL, headers, body)"
- **`aResponse().withStatus().withHeader().withBody()`** — The canned reply is assembled fluently, including status, content type and JSON body, so the client sees a realistic response. > "Stubs API responses, verifies request details, simulates failures (timeouts, 4xx/5xx errors), and validates HTTP client behavior"
- **`verify(getRequestedFor(...))`** — Server-side verification proves the client built the request correctly, which result assertions alone cannot show. > "Verify requests: `verify()` to ensure correct API usage"
- **failure simulation** — Timeouts via `withFixedDelay()`, 4xx/5xx statuses and malformed bodies are stubbed deliberately rather than waiting for the real API to misbehave. > "Testing error scenarios (timeouts, 5xx errors, malformed responses)"
- **stateful testing** — Scenario-based state is kept as an advanced technique in the references, along with body verification and timeout simulation. > "See `references/advanced-examples.md` for error scenarios, body verification, timeout simulation, and stateful testing."
- **AssertJ result assertions** — After the call, the deserialized DTO is validated with AssertJ, pairing the server-side check with client-side assertions. > "Execute and assert: Call service methods, validate results with AssertJ"
RULES:
- WireMock is a `test`-scoped dependency in Maven or Gradle. — > "Add dependency: WireMock in test scope (Maven/Gradle)"
- Always use `wireMockConfig().dynamicPort()`; fixed ports cause parallel execution conflicts. — > "Always use `wireMockConfig().dynamicPort()`"
- Never call the real third-party API; every external endpoint is stubbed. — > "Never call real APIs: Always stub third-party endpoints"
- Stubs stay focused, one concern per test. — > "Focused stubs: One concern per test"
- Stubs are kept synchronized with the actual API contracts they imitate. — > "API changes: Keep stubs synchronized with actual API contracts"
- Timeouts, 4xx and 5xx scenarios must be covered. — > "Test errors: Cover timeouts, 4xx, 5xx scenarios"
- When a stub does not match, check URL encoding and header names, and use `urlEqualTo` for query parameters. — > "If stub not matching: Check URL encoding, header names, use `urlEqualTo` for query params."
- When tests hang, configure connection timeouts on the HTTP client. — > "If tests hanging: Configure connection timeouts in HTTP client"
WORKFLOW:
1. Add WireMock test dependency.
2. `@RegisterExtension static WireMockExtension wireMock = WireMockExtension.newInstance().options(wireMockConfig().dynamicPort()).build();`
3. Configure client base URL via `wireMock.getRuntimeInfo().getHttpBaseUrl()`.
4. `stubFor()` with request matching.
5. Call the service and assert results with AssertJ.
6. `verify()` that the client used the API correctly.
TABLES: none.
ANTI-PATTERNS: calling the real third-party API → stub it; fixed port → dynamic port; broad stub masking intent → focused stub per test; drifting stubs vs. real contract → keep synchronized.
TOOLING: `org.wiremock:wiremock:3.4.1` (test scope), `org.assertj:assertj-core`, `wireMockConfig().dynamicPort()`, `WireMockExtension.newInstance().options(...).build()`, `stubFor`, `aResponse()`, `withFixedDelay()`, `getRequestedFor`, `urlEqualTo`, `containing`.
GOTCHAS: stub not matching due to URL encoding/header naming; tests hanging without client connection timeouts; fixed ports conflict under parallel execution; HTTPS/TLS requires WireMock TLS configuration; WireMock overhead — prefer client-layer mocks for speed.
STRUCTURE: `references/advanced-examples.md` (error scenarios, body verification, timeout simulation, stateful testing) — declared, not bundled.

## S152 · unit-test-controller-layer
SOURCE: Spring MockMvc (`https://docs.spring.io/spring-framework/docs/current/javadoc-api/org/springframework/test/web/servlet/MockMvc.html`), Spring Boot testing (`https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/docs/current/reference/html/features.html#features.testing`)
PURPOSE: Has the agent test Spring `@RestController` endpoints in isolation with `standaloneSetup` MockMvc — request/response mapping, status codes, validation, headers, content negotiation, exception handling — with services mocked.
CONCEPTS:
- **`MockMvcBuilders.standaloneSetup(controller)`** — The controller is registered alone so requests are exercised without a full application context, keeping the test fast and narrowly scoped. > "Setup standalone MockMvc: `MockMvcBuilders.standaloneSetup(controller)` for isolated testing"
- **`@Mock`/`@InjectMocks` + `@BeforeEach setUp()`** — Every service collaborator is a mock and the controller is injected with them, with the `MockMvc` instance rebuilt in `setUp()` per test. > "Mock service dependencies: Use `@Mock` for all services, `@InjectMocks` for the controller"
- **HTTP verb coverage** — Each verb (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) is exercised with the status code it should produce, including 201 on create and 204 on delete. > "Test HTTP methods: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE with correct status codes"
- **`jsonPath()` assertions** — Response bodies are asserted by path, e.g. `$[0].id`, `$.name` and the `$.errors` array, rather than by comparing whole documents. > "Validate responses: JsonPath assertions for JSON, content matchers for body"
- **`param()` and URI templates** — Query parameters and path variables are bound through `.param("name", ...)` and `get("/api/users/{id}", 123L)`. > "Covers request/response handling, HTTP status codes, request parameter binding, validation, content negotiation"
- **status semantics** — Matchers name the intent: `isOk`, `isCreated` (201), `isNoContent` (204), `isNotFound`, `isBadRequest`, `isUnauthorized`. > "Test errors: Verify 404, 400, 401, 403, 500 for appropriate conditions"
- **request/response header assertions** — Header handling is checked in both directions, incoming `Authorization` and outgoing custom headers via `header().exists`/`header().string`. > "Both request (Authorization) and response headers"
- **content negotiation** — `.accept("application/json")` combined with `content().contentType(...)` verifies the chosen representation. > "Test content negotiation: Different Accept and Content-Type headers"
- **`.andDo(print())`** — When an assertion fails the printed request/response is the diagnostic step before touching the assertion itself. > "Run test → If fails: add .andDo(print()) → Check actual vs expected → Fix assertion"
- **validation-error shape** — An invalid body is expected to yield 400 with a `$.errors` array, so error payload structure is part of the contract being tested. > "Test validation: Send invalid input, verify 400 status with error details"
- **`doNothing().when(service)`** — Void service methods such as delete are stubbed with `doNothing()` rather than `when()`, since there is no return value to configure. > "doNothing().when(userService).deleteUser(1L);"
RULES:
- Use `standaloneSetup()` so the controller test stays isolated. — > "Use `standaloneSetup()` for isolated controller testing"
- Mock the service layer; controllers own HTTP and services own business logic. — > "Mock service layer — controllers handle HTTP, services handle business logic"
- Cover the happy path and the error scenarios (404, 400, 500). — > "Test happy path AND error scenarios (404, 400, 500)"
- One focused assertion per test method. — > "One focused assertion per test method"
- Verify mock interactions with `verify(service).method(args)`. — > "Verify mock interactions: `verify(service).method(args)`"
- Validate both request headers such as `Authorization` and response headers. — > "Validate headers: Both request (Authorization) and response headers"
WORKFLOW:
1. `MockMvcBuilders.standaloneSetup(controller)`.
2. `@Mock` services, `@InjectMocks` controller.
3. Test each HTTP method with correct status codes.
4. Assert JSON with JsonPath / content matchers.
5. Invalid input → expect 400 with error details.
6. Error paths → 404, 400, 401, 403, 500 as appropriate.
7. Assert request and response headers.
8. Test different `Accept` and `Content-Type` headers.
Validation loop: "Run test → If fails: add .andDo(print()) → Check actual vs expected → Fix assertion".
TABLES: none explicit; the validation workflow is a one-line arrow chain.
ANTI-PATTERNS: testing business logic in controllers → mock services; single happy-path assertion → cover error statuses; guessing failure causes → `.andDo(print())` diff; conflating security tests with controller tests → separate security tests.
TOOLING: `spring-boot-starter-test` test scope, `MockMvcBuilders.standaloneSetup`, `MockMvcRequestBuilders.*`, `MockMvcResultMatchers.*`, `jsonPath`, `MockMultipartFile`.
GOTCHAS: controller tests verify HTTP handling only, not full request flow; `standaloneSetup()` may not support `@Validated` without full context; JsonPath requires valid JSON body; `@PreAuthorize`/`@Secured` need extra setup; file uploads need `MockMultipartFile`.
STRUCTURE: none (no references section).

## S153 · unit-test-parameterized
SOURCE: JUnit 5 parameterized tests (`https://junit.org/junit5/docs/current/user-guide/#writing-tests-parameterized-tests`), `@ParameterizedTest` API javadoc
PURPOSE: Tells the agent to collapse near-duplicate test methods into data-driven `@ParameterizedTest` cases using `@ValueSource`, `@CsvSource`, `@MethodSource`, `@EnumSource`, `@ArgumentsSource`, and readable display names.
CONCEPTS:
- **`@ParameterizedTest`** — One method runs once per supplied value, which removes copy-pasted test methods that differ only in their input. > "Reduces test duplication by running the same test logic with multiple input values."
- **`@ValueSource(strings/ints = {...})`** — Literal scalars are inlined in the annotation, making it the cheapest source when the inputs are strings or numbers. > "Choose source: `@ValueSource` for simple values"
- **`@CsvSource`** — Comma-separated rows encode multi-column cases such as email/expected-valid pairs, acting as an inline case table. > "Use `@MethodSource` for complex objects, `@CsvSource` for tabular data"
- **`@MethodSource("factory")`** — A `static Stream<Arguments>` factory supplies objects and multi-argument cases that annotations cannot express literally. > "`@MethodSource` visibility: Factory methods must be static in the same test class"
- **`@EnumSource`** — All enum constants are covered by default, or a subset is selected with `names = {"ACTIVE", "INACTIVE"}`. > "@EnumSource(value = Status.class, names = {\"ACTIVE\", \"INACTIVE\"})"
- **custom `ArgumentsProvider`** — `@ArgumentsSource` points at a provider class implementing `provideArguments(ExtensionContext)`, encapsulating reusable case sets outside the test class. > "class RangeValidatorProvider implements ArgumentsProvider"
- **display names** — `name = "{0}..."` with `{0}`,`{1}` placeholders turns each invocation into a readable sentence in the report. > "Use descriptive display names: `name = \"{0}...\"` for readable output"
- **boundary value analysis** — Ranges are probed at `Integer.MIN_VALUE`, `-1`, `0`, `1` and `Integer.MAX_VALUE` rather than at arbitrary midpoints. > "Test boundary values: include min, max, zero, and edge cases"
- **error-condition parameterization** — Invalid inputs are fed as a value set (`{"", " ", null}`) and each one is expected to raise `IllegalArgumentException`. > "@ValueSource(strings = {\"\", \" \", null})"
- **per-parameter-set invocation** — Each set is a separate test execution, so a failing set is reported individually and the failure count scales with the data. > "Each parameter set runs as a separate test invocation"
RULES:
- `junit-jupiter-params` must be on the test classpath (it ships inside `junit-jupiter`). — > "Ensure `junit-jupiter-params` is on test classpath (included in `junit-jupiter`)"
- Test method parameter count and types must match the chosen data source. — > "Parameter count must match: Number of parameters from source must match test method signature"
- `@MethodSource` factories are static and live in the same test class. — > "Factory methods must be static in the same test class"
- `@ValueSource` supports only primitives, strings and enums, not objects or null directly. — > "`@ValueSource` limitation: Only supports primitives, strings, and enums — not objects or null directly"
- CSV values containing commas are wrapped in single quotes. — > "CSV escaping: Strings with commas must use single quotes in `@CsvSource`"
- Keep a single assertion per parameter set and include boundary values. — > "Keep test logic focused: single assertion per parameter set"
- Confirm every combination executes by checking `./gradlew test --info` or `mvn test` output. — > "Run `./gradlew test --info` or `mvn test` and verify all parameter combinations execute"
WORKFLOW:
1. Add `junit-jupiter` (params included) and `assertj-core`.
2. Choose source: `@ValueSource` simple, `@CsvSource` tabular, `@MethodSource` complex.
3. Match method parameters to source types.
4. Set `name = "{0}..."` display names.
5. Run `./gradlew test --info` / `mvn test` and confirm every combination executes.
TABLES: none literal; `@CsvSource` blocks act as inline case tables (email/boolean, arithmetic triples, range quads).
ANTI-PATTERNS: copy-pasted test methods per value → `@ParameterizedTest`; unreadable default names → placeholders in `name`; object payloads in `@ValueSource` → `@MethodSource`; unescaped commas in CSV → single quotes.
TOOLING: `@ParameterizedTest`, `@ValueSource`, `@CsvSource`, `@MethodSource`, `@EnumSource(value = ..., names = {...})`, `@ArgumentsSource`, `Arguments.of(...)`, `ExtensionContext`, `./gradlew test --info`.
GOTCHAS: parameter count/type mismatch; `@ValueSource` cannot take objects or null directly; CSV comma escaping; non-static factory methods; each set is a separate invocation, so failure counts multiply.
STRUCTURE: none.

## S154 · unit-test-json-serialization
SOURCE: Spring `@JsonTest` javadoc, Jackson `ObjectMapper` and annotations javadoc (2.15)
PURPOSE: Has the agent verify Jackson mapping through Spring's `@JsonTest` + `JacksonTester` — serialization, deserialization, custom serializers, field names, nesting, date formats, polymorphic types, and null handling.
CONCEPTS:
- **`@JsonTest`** — The slice loads only JSON-related beans and JacksonTester auto-configuration, so mapping is tested without the whole application context. > "Annotate test class with `@JsonTest` → Enables JacksonTester auto-configuration"
- **`JacksonTester<T>`** — One tester is autowired per target type, giving type-safe `write`/`parse` calls and path assertions. > "Autowire JacksonTester for target type → Provides type-safe JSON assertions"
- **`json.write(obj)` → `JsonContent<T>`** — Serialization is asserted by extracting individual paths such as `$.id` and `$.name` from the produced content. > "Call `json.write(object)` and assert JSON paths with `extractingJsonPath*`"
- **`json.parse(str).getObject()`** — Deserialization is asserted on the resulting object's state, e.g. `user.getName()`, not on the raw string. > "Call `json.parse(json)` or `json.parseObject(json)` and assert object state"
- **round-trip validation** — Serializing and then deserializing the same object and comparing both sides catches asymmetric mappings that one-direction tests miss. > "Serialize, then deserialize, verify same data (if object is properly comparable)"
- **`@JsonProperty("order_id")` / `@JsonIgnore`** — Wire names and exclusions are part of the contract: `order_id` must map to the field and `internalNote` must not appear in output. > "Validating `@JsonProperty`, `@JsonIgnore`, and field name mappings"
- **nested objects and lists** — Nested structure is asserted by path (`$.category.name`) and collection size (`hasSize(2)` on reviews), and a null nested value points at missing or malformed inner JSON. > "Log parsed JSON; verify inner structure matches POJO"
- **date/time formatting** — `LocalDateTime.of(2024,1,15,10,30,0)` is expected to render as `"2024-01-15T10:30:00"`, with `@JsonFormat(pattern=...)` for non-default patterns. > "ISO-8601 is default; use `@JsonFormat` for custom patterns"
- **custom `JsonSerializer<BigDecimal>`** — A serializer writing `String.format("$%.2f", value)` is verified through the resulting `$.amount` string. > "Verifying custom Jackson serializers/deserializers"
- **polymorphic types** — `@JsonTypeInfo(use = JsonTypeInfo.Id.NAME, property = "type")` plus `@JsonSubTypes` bind the type discriminator to concrete classes, and the test asserts the parsed instance type. > "`@JsonTypeInfo` must correctly identify the subtype for deserialization to work"
- **null handling** — Whether nulls appear in output depends on `@JsonInclude(Include.NON_NULL)`, so null behaviour is asserted rather than assumed. > "Null handling: Use `@JsonInclude(Include.NON_NULL)` to exclude nulls from serialization"
- **`@JsonCreator` + `@JsonProperty`** — Immutable types deserialize through a constructor pair instead of setters. > "Use `@JsonCreator` + `@JsonProperty` for constructor-based deserialization"
- **circular references** — Managed/back references stop the infinite loop that bidirectional object graphs otherwise produce. > "Use `@JsonManagedReference`/`@JsonBackReference` to prevent infinite loops"
- **validation checkpoints** — After each assertion the test is confirmed to fail meaningfully with wrong data, proving the assertion has teeth. > "After each assertion, verify the test fails meaningfully with wrong data"
RULES:
- Test serialization and deserialization both, for complete coverage. — > "Test serialization AND deserialization for complete coverage"
- Assert JSON paths individually instead of comparing full JSON strings. — > "Verify JSON paths individually rather than comparing full JSON strings"
- Include a round-trip test, and cover edge cases: empty strings, empty collections, deeply nested structures. — > "Test round-trip: serialize an object, deserialize the JSON, verify the result matches"
- Test null handling explicitly because inclusion depends on `@JsonInclude`. — > "Test null handling explicitly — null fields may be included or excluded depending on `@JsonInclude`"
- Group related assertions in one test for clarity. — > "Group related assertions in a single test for clarity"
- After a fix, add a complementary test for the opposite case to prevent regression. — > "write a complementary test for the opposite case"
WORKFLOW:
1. `@JsonTest` on the test class.
2. `@Autowired JacksonTester<TargetType>`.
3. `json.write(object)` + `extractingJsonPath*`.
4. `json.parse(json)` / `json.parseObject(json)` + state assertions.
5. Round-trip serialize→deserialize→compare (if comparable).
6. Edge cases: nulls, missing fields, empty collections, invalid JSON.
7. Validation checkpoint after each assertion.
TABLES: "Debugging Workflow" table — 3 columns (Failure Symptom, Common Cause, How to Verify) × 7 rows: JsonPath assertion fails / null expected but value / wrong type / date format mismatch / missing field in output / nested object null / `JsonParseException`.
ANTI-PATTERNS: full-string JSON comparison → per-path assertions; only serialization tested → add deserialization and round-trip; assuming nulls serialize → check `@JsonInclude`; wrong-type deserialization → `@JsonTypeInfo` mapping.
TOOLING: `spring-boot-starter-json`, `spring-boot-starter-test` (test), `@JsonTest`, `JacksonTester<T>`, `JsonContent<T>`, `extractingJsonPathNumberValue/StringValue`, `.json` field on `JsonContent`, `@JsonFormat(pattern=...)`, `@JsonInclude(Include.NON_NULL)`.
GOTCHAS: `@JsonTest` loads a limited context — use `@SpringBootTest` for full context; annotation/Jackson version mismatch; ISO-8601 is default date format; circular references loop infinitely without managed/back references; polymorphic subtype must be identifiable.
STRUCTURE: none (References section lists external docs only).

## S155 · unit-test-security-authorization
SOURCE: none (no URLs; points to `references/setup.md`, `references/basic-testing.md`, `references/advanced-authorization.md`, `references/complete-examples.md`)
PURPOSE: Has the agent verify method-level Spring Security authorization (`@PreAuthorize`, `@Secured`, `@RolesAllowed`, custom permission evaluators) without requiring a full Spring Security context.
CONCEPTS:
- **`@EnableMethodSecurity`** — A test configuration class annotated with `@EnableMethodSecurity` turns method-security annotations on, which is the precondition for any allow/deny test to mean anything. > "Enable Method Security in Test Configuration"
- **`@WithMockUser(roles = "ADMIN")`** — The annotation injects an authenticated principal with the given roles, but it creates only a simple `Authentication`, so complex principals need custom setup. > "`@WithMockUser` limitations: Creates a simple Authentication; complex auth scenarios need custom setup"
- **`@WithUserDetails("alice")`** — Custom-principal tests go through a `UserDetailsService` and load the real user object instead of synthesizing one. > "For custom principal properties, use @WithUserDetails with a custom UserDetailsService"
- **expression-based authorization** — `@PreAuthorize("#userId == authentication.principal.id")` ties access to a SpEL comparison against the authenticated principal, so ownership rules become testable expressions. > "@PreAuthorize(\"#userId == authentication.principal.id\")"
- **`@PostAuthorize`** — The check runs after invocation against `returnObject`, so the rule can depend on the value that was produced. > "@PostAuthorize(\"returnObject.owner == authentication.name\")"
- **`@RolesAllowed`** — The JSR-250 standard annotation is supported alongside the Spring-specific ones, so both styles are covered by the same tests. > "using `@PreAuthorize`, `@Secured`, `@RolesAllowed`, and custom permission evaluators"
- **RBAC allow/deny pairing** — Each security rule is exercised in both directions: the permitted role passes and the other role receives `AccessDeniedException`. > "Test both allow and deny cases for each security rule"
- **custom `PermissionEvaluator`** — `evaluator.hasPermission(auth, doc, "WRITE")` is called directly with a `UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken` carrying `SimpleGrantedAuthority("ROLE_USER")`, testing the policy without HTTP. > "Testing custom permission evaluators"
- **`AccessDeniedException`** — Denial is asserted by exception type via `assertThatThrownBy(...).isInstanceOf(AccessDeniedException.class)`. > "Verifying access denied scenarios"
- **`assertThatCode(...).doesNotThrowAnyException()`** — The allow case is expressed as absence of a throw, which makes the positive path explicit rather than implied. > "assertThatCode(() -> service.deleteUser(1L))"
- **security-is-active check** — A test that must throw proves enforcement is actually wired; if it passes, method security is not active. > "If tests pass unexpectedly, add this assertion to verify security is enforced"
- **proxy-based enforcement** — Annotations work through proxies, so a direct in-process call on the raw object bypasses security entirely and gives false confidence. > "Method security requires proxy: `@PreAuthorize` works via proxies; direct method calls bypass security"
RULES:
- Add `spring-security-test` to the test dependencies with `test` scope. — > "Add spring-security-test to your test dependencies"
- Enable method security in the test configuration; a missing annotation silently bypasses every `@PreAuthorize` check. — > "a missing annotation causes all `@PreAuthorize` checks to be bypassed silently"
- Test both allow and deny cases for each rule; testing only the allow path is the common failure. — > "Not testing both allow and deny scenarios"
- Test different roles, expression-based security and anonymous access as separate cases. — > "Test anonymous access separately from authenticated access"
- Write `hasRole('ADMIN')`, not `hasRole('ROLE_ADMIN')`, because Spring prepends the `ROLE_` prefix itself. — > "Role prefix: Spring adds \"ROLE_\" prefix automatically; use `hasRole('ADMIN')` not `hasRole('ROLE_ADMIN')`"
- Mock external dependencies such as permission evaluators. — > "Mock external dependencies (permission evaluators, etc.)"
- When tests pass unexpectedly, confirm `@EnableMethodSecurity` is active on the test configuration. — > "verify that `@EnableMethodSecurity` is active on the test configuration"
WORKFLOW:
1. Add `spring-security-test` test dependency.
2. `@Configuration @EnableMethodSecurity class TestSecurityConfig { }`.
3. Test with `@WithMockUser(roles = ...)` for allow and deny.
4. Test custom permission evaluators via `hasPermission`.
5. Add a security-is-active assertion to prove enforcement.
TABLES: "Quick Reference" annotation table — 3 columns (Annotation, Description, Example) × 5 rows: `@PreAuthorize`, `@PostAuthorize`, `@Secured`, `@RolesAllowed`, `@WithMockUser`.
ANTI-PATTERNS: missing method-security enablement → "all `@PreAuthorize` checks bypassed silently", fix with `@EnableMethodSecurity`/`@EnableGlobalMethodSecurity`; only allow-path tests → add deny tests; testing framework code instead of authorization logic → focus on policy; unhandled null authentication → add explicit cases; mixing authentication and authorization tests unnecessarily → separate them.
TOOLING: `spring-security-test`, `@EnableMethodSecurity`, `@WithMockUser`, `@WithUserDetails`, `AccessDeniedException`, `assertThatCode`, `assertThatThrownBy`, `UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken`, `SimpleGrantedAuthority`.
GOTCHAS: "a missing annotation causes all `@PreAuthorize` checks to be bypassed silently"; method security requires a proxy so direct calls skip it; security context is thread-local — risky with async tests; `@WithMockUser` creates only a simple `Authentication`; complex SpEL is hard to debug; `@Secured`/`@PreAuthorize` need additional setup in MockMvc-style tests; method security adds runtime overhead.
STRUCTURE: `references/setup.md`, `references/basic-testing.md`, `references/advanced-authorization.md`, `references/complete-examples.md` — declared, not bundled.

## S156 · unit-test-utility-methods
SOURCE: none (no repo or URL in file)
PURPOSE: Tells an agent to generate JUnit 5 + AssertJ tests for utility classes, static helper methods and pure functions, covering happy path, edge cases, boundary conditions and null handling.
CONCEPTS:
- `pure function testing` — Helpers that hold no state and touch nothing outside their arguments are tested as input/output pairs; no doubles are involved anywhere. > "**Test pure functions exclusively** - no side effects or state dependency"
- `test class naming` — The test class takes the name of the utility under test, so source and test are paired by name. > "**Create test class**: Name it after the utility (e.g., `StringUtilsTest`)"
- `happy path` — The first layer of every example feeds valid inputs and asserts the expected output. > "**Test happy path**: Valid inputs with expected outputs"
- `edge cases` — Degenerate inputs — null, empty, whitespace-only, a single element — each get their own case. > "**Test edge cases**: null, empty, whitespace, single elements"
- `boundary conditions` — Values at the edges of the type domain, including overflow and precision loss, are asserted explicitly. > "**Test boundary conditions** - min/max values, overflow, precision"
- `descriptive test naming` — Method names state the contract as a readable sentence, so a failing case prints what broke. > "**Use descriptive names**: `shouldCapitalizeFirstLetter` instead of `test1`"
- `AssertJ fluent assertions` — Assertions use AssertJ's chainable style rather than JUnit's boolean asserts. > "**Use AssertJ**: For readable, chainable assertions"
- `@ParameterizedTest` — Inputs that share one assertion shape collapse into a single parameterised case. > "**Use `@ParameterizedTest`**: For multiple similar inputs (see `references/parameterized-tests.md`)"
- `null-safe utility pattern` — Helpers such as `getOrDefault` and `isNotBlank` form their own category, and the null contract is fixed before the tests are written. > "**Null handling consistency**: Decide whether utility returns null or throws; test accordingly"
- `math/precision handling` — Arithmetic helpers are probed at zero divisors, at rounding boundaries and at large magnitudes. > "**Test boundary conditions**: max/min values, large numbers, precision"
- `floating-point tolerance` — Computed floats are compared through a delta rather than against a decimal literal. > "**Floating point precision**: Never use exact equality; use `isCloseTo(delta)`"
- `collection utilities` — Filter, join and deduplicate helpers are asserted by exact contents and by content irrespective of order. > "common utilities like string manipulation, calculations, data validation, and collections"
- `validators` — Email, URL and card-number helpers are checked at both accepting and rejecting inputs. > "Generates AssertJ assertions and @ParameterizedTest for string utils, math utils, validators, and collection helpers."
- `Clock injection` — The one permitted double is an injected `Clock`, passed as a parameter and stubbed for a fixed instant. > "**Avoid mocking pure functions** - only mock external dependencies like Clock"
- `input immutability` — Whether a helper mutates the caller's collection is documented, because it changes what the test may assert. > "**Immutable inputs**: Document whether utilities modify input parameters"
- `thread safety` — Static helpers must stay safe under concurrent use, and that property is checked separately from the single-threaded cases. > "**Thread safety**: Static utilities must be thread-safe; verify concurrent behavior separately"
RULES:
- Apply the eight instructions in order: name the class, happy path, edge cases, boundaries, descriptive names, AssertJ, parameterised inputs, no mocks. — > "1. **Create test class**: Name it after the utility (e.g., `StringUtilsTest`)"
- Static methods are not mocked; reflection utilities are a last resort. — > "**No mocking static methods**: Use reflection utilities only when absolutely necessary"
- Float results are never compared for exact equality. — > "**Floating point precision**: Never use exact equality; use `isCloseTo(delta)`"
- Stateful utilities resist testing, so immutability is preferred. — > "**Pure function requirement**: Stateful utilities are harder to test; prefer immutability"
- The null contract is settled first — return null or throw — and every test follows it. — > "**Null handling consistency**: Decide whether utility returns null or throws; test accordingly"
- No test may depend on another having run. — > "**Keep tests independent** - no order dependency between tests"
- Mutation of input arguments is documented on the utility. — > "**Immutable inputs**: Document whether utilities modify input parameters"
WORKFLOW:
1. Name the test class after the utility (`StringUtilsTest`).
2. Test the happy path with valid inputs and expected outputs.
3. Test edge cases: null, empty, whitespace, single elements.
4. Test boundary conditions: max/min values, large numbers, precision.
5. Use descriptive `should…` method names.
6. Assert with AssertJ.
7. Move repeated input shapes to `@ParameterizedTest` (see `references/parameterized-tests.md`).
8. Add no mocks for pure functions; mock only external dependencies such as `Clock`.
TABLES: none
ANTI-PATTERNS:
- `test1`-style names → use `shouldCapitalizeFirstLetter` / `shouldReturnNullWhenInputIsNull`.
- Exact float equality on computed values → `isCloseTo(delta)`.
- Mocking pure functions → only external dependencies (Clock) are mocked.
- Mocking static methods → reflection utilities only when absolutely necessary.
- Stateful utilities → prefer immutability so the utility stays testable.
- Order-dependent tests → keep every test independent.
TOOLING:
- JUnit 5: `@Test`, `@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)`, `@Mock`, `@ParameterizedTest`.
- AssertJ: `assertThat`, `isEqualTo`, `isNull`, `isEmpty`, `isTrue`, `isFalse`, `isZero`, `isCloseTo`, `within`, `containsExactly`, `containsExactlyInAnyOrder`.
- Mockito: `when(clock.instant()).thenReturn(Instant.parse("2024-01-15T10:00:00Z"))`.
- Frontmatter `allowed-tools: Read, Write, Bash, Glob, Grep`.
GOTCHAS:
- Floating-point results differ from decimal literals (`0.1 * 0.2`); exact equality fails.
- Null handling divergence (return null vs throw) silently breaks tests written against the other contract.
- Static utility thread safety is invisible to ordinary single-threaded tests.
- File names two reference docs it never bundles, so the reader may hit a dead link.
STRUCTURE:
- `references/parameterized-tests.md` — declared, not bundled.
- `references/edge-cases.md` — declared, not bundled (boundary testing patterns).

## S157 · unit-test-scheduled-async
SOURCE: none in body; References section links `https://docs.spring.io/spring-framework/docs/current/javadoc-api/org/springframework/scheduling/annotation/Async.html`, `.../Scheduled.html`, `https://github.com/awaitility/awaitility`, `https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/concurrent/CompletableFuture.html`
PURPOSE: Tells an agent to unit-test Spring `@Scheduled` and `@Async` methods by calling them directly and waiting on `CompletableFuture`/Awaitility, instead of waiting for real scheduling intervals.
CONCEPTS:
- `proxy bypass` — In a unit test the async proxy is not in play, so the method is called like any other method. > "**Call `@Async` methods directly** — bypass Spring's async proxy; the annotation is irrelevant in unit tests"
- `direct invocation of @Scheduled` — A scheduled method is invoked directly; cron and fixed-rate timings are never waited on. > "**Call `@Scheduled` methods directly** — do not wait for cron/fixedRate; the annotation is ignored in unit tests"
- `CompletableFuture.get(timeout, unit)` — Completion is awaited through a bounded `get`, five seconds in the example. > "**Wait for completion** — use `CompletableFuture.get(timeout, unit)` or `await().atMost(...).untilAsserted(...)`"
- `ExecutionException unwrapping` — A failed future surfaces as `ExecutionException`, so the cause is unwrapped and asserted for its type. > "If `ExecutionException` is thrown, check `.getCause()` to identify the root exception"
- `Awaitility polling` — Where shared mutable state races, Awaitility polls every 100 ms for up to five seconds until the assertion holds. > "Awaitility: use for race conditions with shared mutable state"
- `execution-count assertions` — After several invocations the count is asserted before mock interactions are verified. > "After multiple task invocations, assert execution counts before `verify()` calls"
- `cron-expression logic testing` — Cron expressions are validated as logic instead of letting the scheduler fire. > "Testing cron expression logic without waiting for actual scheduling"
- `thread-pool behaviour` — `ThreadPoolTaskScheduler` gives no ordering guarantee, so order-dependent assertions are invalid. > "**Thread pool ordering**: `ThreadPoolTaskScheduler` does not guarantee execution order"
- `CompletableFuture chaining hazard` — Exceptions raised inside intermediate stages can disappear, so each stage is asserted. > "**CompletableFuture chaining**: exceptions in intermediate stages can be silently lost — test each stage"
- `Mockito injection` — The task under test is assembled with `@Mock` collaborators and `@InjectMocks`. > "**Mock dependencies** with `@Mock` and `@InjectMocks` (Mockito)"
- `fixedDelay metadata` — The sample refresh task declares a 60-second fixed delay. > "@Scheduled(fixedDelay = 60000) public void refreshCache() { /* ... */ }"
RULES:
- Every `get()` carries a timeout, so a stuck future fails instead of hanging the suite. — > "Always set a **timeout** on `CompletableFuture.get()` to prevent hanging tests"
- No real external service is contacted; every collaborator is mocked. — > "**Mock all dependencies** — never call real external services in unit tests"
- Awaitility is reserved for genuine races; simple async methods are called directly. — > "Use **Awaitility** only for race conditions; prefer direct calls for simple async methods"
- Values are asserted before `verify()`, and verification happens only after the future completes. — > "Assert values before verifying mock interactions; verify **after** async completion"
- The first checkpoint after `get()` is the returned value, ahead of any interaction check. — > "After `CompletableFuture.get()`, assert the returned value before verifying mock interactions"
- On `ExecutionException` the cause is inspected to name the root failure. — > "If `ExecutionException` is thrown, check `.getCause()` to identify the root exception"
- A timing-out Awaitility block is retuned by raising `atMost()` or lowering `pollInterval()`. — > "If Awaitility times out, increase `atMost()` duration or reduce `pollInterval()` until the condition is reachable"
- `atMost()` always gets a finite value, because an unbounded wait hangs the suite. — > "**Awaitility timeout**: always set a reasonable `atMost()`; infinite waits hang the test suite"
WORKFLOW:
1. Call `@Async` methods directly — bypass Spring's async proxy.
2. Mock dependencies with `@Mock` / `@InjectMocks`.
3. Wait for completion with `CompletableFuture.get(timeout, unit)` or `await().atMost(...).untilAsserted(...)`.
4. Call `@Scheduled` methods directly — do not wait for cron/fixedRate.
5. Test exception paths — verify `ExecutionException` wrapping on `CompletableFuture.get()`.
TABLES: none
ANTI-PATTERNS:
- Relying on Spring's async executor instead of calling methods directly → call the method and await the future.
- Missing timeout on `CompletableFuture.get()` → always pass `(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)`-style timeout.
- Forgetting exception propagation testing → assert `ExecutionException` plus cause.
- Not mocking dependencies the async method invokes internally → mock every collaborator.
- Waiting on real cron/`fixedRate` timing → test the logic in isolation.
TOOLING:
- JUnit 5 `@Test`; Mockito `@Mock`, `@InjectMocks`, `doThrow(...).when(...)`, `verify(...)`.
- AssertJ `assertThat`, `assertThatThrownBy`, `hasCauseInstanceOf`.
- Awaitility `Awaitility.await().atMost(Duration...).pollInterval(Duration...).untilAsserted(...)`.
- `CompletableFuture.supplyAsync`, `.get(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)`.
- Gradle/Maven dependency blocks live in `references/examples.md`.
GOTCHAS:
- `@Async` self-invocation from another method in the same class executes synchronously — the proxy is bypassed.
- `ThreadPoolTaskScheduler` ordering is unspecified; order-dependent tests are invalid.
- Intermediate `CompletableFuture` stage exceptions can be lost silently.
- A hard `Thread.sleep`-free test still hangs forever if `get()` has no timeout.
STRUCTURE:
- `references/examples.md` — declared, not bundled (full dependencies, extra test classes, execution-count patterns).

## S158 · unit-test-exception-handler
SOURCE: none (no repo or URL in file)
PURPOSE: Tells an agent to unit-test Spring `@ExceptionHandler` / `@ControllerAdvice` classes through standalone MockMvc, asserting HTTP status plus every field of the JSON error payload.
CONCEPTS:
- `standalone MockMvc` — `standaloneSetup()` with `setControllerAdvice()` exercises the advice with no application context. > "Use `MockMvcBuilders.standaloneSetup()` for isolated handler tests without full Spring context"
- `test controller as trigger` — A throwaway controller raises each exception type, so every handler can be reached on its own. > "**Create a test controller** that throws specific exceptions to trigger each `@ExceptionHandler`"
- `@ResponseStatus mapping` — A missing status annotation collapses every handler response to 200, which is why the mapping is asserted explicitly. > "**`@ResponseStatus` default**: without `@ResponseStatus` or returning `ResponseEntity`, HTTP status defaults to 200"
- `error DTO records` — Two record types carry the payload: a plain error and a field-error map. > "public record ErrorResponse(int status, String error, String message) {}"
- `field-level validation errors` — Binding-result field errors are folded into a field→message map and asserted by key. > "**Test validation errors** by sending invalid payloads and checking `MethodArgumentNotValidException` produces field-level details"
- `jsonPath assertions` — Nested error keys are addressed by JSON path, and a mismatch is diagnosed by printing the exchange. > "JsonPath mismatch: use `.andDo(print())` to inspect actual response structure"
- `status matchers` — Status is asserted with `status().isXxx()` matchers alongside the body fields. > "**Assert HTTP status codes** with `.andExpect(status().isXxx())`"
- `handler precedence` — Specific types win over `Exception.class`, and `@Order` settles competing advices. > "**`@ExceptionHandler` specificity**: more specific exception types are matched first; `Exception.class` catches all unmatched types"
- `global vs local scope` — Advice-scoped handlers cover every controller; a handler declared inside a controller covers only that controller. > "**Global vs local scope**: `@ExceptionHandler` in `@ControllerAdvice` is global; declared in a controller it is local only to that controller"
- `logging side effects` — Handlers that log are checked through a mock logger rather than a log capture. > "**Logging side effects**: handlers that log should be verified with `verify(mockLogger).logXxx(...)`"
- `localization` — Message resolution is exercised across `Locale` values when a `MessageSource` is in play. > "**Localization**: when using `MessageSource`, test with different `Locale` values to confirm message resolution"
- `security context` — Handlers that read `SecurityContextHolder` are tested with that context populated. > "**Security context**: `AuthorizationException` handlers can access `SecurityContextHolder` — test that context is correctly evaluated"
RULES:
- Exactly one advice instance is registered on the builder; skipping it leaves the handler unexercised. — > "Register exactly one `@ControllerAdvice` instance via `setControllerAdvice()` — never skip it"
- The status and every payload field are asserted, not the status alone. — > "Assert all fields in the error response body, not just the HTTP status"
- Validation responses are checked on both the field key and the message value. — > "For validation errors, verify both the field name key and the error message value"
- Each handler gets its own test and its own throwing route. — > "Test each `@ExceptionHandler` method independently with a dedicated exception throw"
- Advice is registered through `setControllerAdvice()` on the standalone builder. — > "**Register ControllerAdvice** via `setControllerAdvice()` on `MockMvcBuilders.standaloneSetup()`"
- `.andDo(print())` is chained so a failure prints the request and response. — > "Log assertion failures: chain `.andDo(print())` to print request/response when a test fails"
- Internal handler logic is out of scope: collaborators are mocked and only the response transformation is asserted. — > "Testing handler logic instead of behavior: mock external dependencies, test only the response transformation"
WORKFLOW:
1. Create a test controller that throws specific exceptions to trigger each `@ExceptionHandler`.
2. Register the advice via `setControllerAdvice()` on `MockMvcBuilders.standaloneSetup()`.
3. Assert the status with `.andExpect(status().isXxx())`.
4. Verify each error body field with `jsonPath("$.field")`.
5. Send invalid payloads and check `MethodArgumentNotValidException` yields field-level details.
6. Debug with `.andDo(print())`; if the handler was not invoked, confirm `setControllerAdvice()` ran and the exception type matches.
TABLES: none
ANTI-PATTERNS:
- Handler not invoked → ensure `setControllerAdvice()` is called on the builder.
- JsonPath mismatch → `.andDo(print())` to inspect the actual response structure.
- Status 200 returned → add `@ResponseStatus` to the handler method.
- Duplicate handlers → control precedence with `@Order`; specific types win.
- Testing handler logic instead of behaviour → mock external dependencies and assert only the response transformation.
TOOLING:
- `@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)`, `@BeforeEach`, `@ControllerAdvice`, `@ExceptionHandler`, `@ResponseStatus`, `@RestController`, `@RequestMapping`, `@GetMapping("/users/{id}")`, `@PostMapping`, `@Valid`, `@PathVariable`.
- MockMvc: `mockMvc.perform(get("/api/users/999"))`, `.contentType("application/json")`, `.content("{...}")`, `.andExpect`, `.andDo(print())`.
- `record` DTOs; `HashMap` for the field-error map.
GOTCHAS:
- Missing `@ResponseStatus` (and not returning `ResponseEntity`) defaults the HTTP status to 200 — a test that only checks the body passes wrongly.
- An unregistered advice silently makes the framework return 200/500 instead of the handler's payload.
- Asserting only status hides wrong field keys in `$.errors.*`.
- Localized messages differ per `Locale`; a single-locale test hides resolution gaps.
STRUCTURE: none

## S159 · unit-test-config-properties
SOURCE: none (no repo or URL in file)
PURPOSE: Tells an agent to test Spring Boot `@ConfigurationProperties` binding, validation, defaults, type conversion and profiles with `ApplicationContextRunner`, without starting a full Spring context.
CONCEPTS:
- `ApplicationContextRunner` — Each case builds a throwaway context with the properties it needs and asserts inside the callback. > "**Use ApplicationContextRunner**: Test property bindings without starting full Spring context"
- `context isolation` — No state crosses between cases, because every runner starts a fresh context. > "**Context isolation**: Each `ApplicationContextRunner` creates a new context with no shared state"
- `prefix matching` — The prefix on the class must match the paths handed to `withPropertyValues`, or nothing binds. > "If properties don't bind → Check prefix matches (kebab-case to camelCase conversion)"
- `kebab-case to camelCase` — Kebab property names map onto camel-case Java fields. > "**Kebab-case to camelCase**: Property `app.my-property` maps to `myProperty` in Java"
- `loose binding` — Binding is loose by default, and strictness has to be opted into. > "**Loose binding**: Spring Boot uses loose binding by default; use strict binding if needed"
